analysis.name: Ali Kashani
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Broo Professor Ak is the goat. Super easy class for your first year at Berkeley!! He was lowkey funny when he wanted to be. It was literally just weekly readings, taking notes of them, and writing an essay-length discussion post due every Friday. (Tip: the GSI likes it when you don't use any quotations, just paraphrase everything, and ur chillin.)

Entire class is graded on repetitive weekly discussion posts and a midterm + final paper, which I'm pretty sure he doesn't read because his GSI has graded every single assignment this semester. Lectures are helpful sometimes, however he doesn't take attendance or track participation so a lot of kids just don't show up. Rather lazy, in my opinion.

Mostly graded on weekly discussion + midterm&final. Pretty chill, most people barely showed up to class, and submitted stuff late. Fairly easy, but also interesting served as a great backbone for future philosophy (im a philosophy major). Definitely would recommend and if your someone who's on top of their work you'll get an A

The grading scale is at the highest, 95, which can change your GPA. Very heavily graded on responses and in-text citations are the by far the most important thing for getting a good grade. Great and interesting class material, but the lectures are a bit slow and make the material monotonous.

The class was good, and I ended up passing, but it is slightly difficult if you do not keep up with the readings or work. The TA is the one who grades the weekly assignment, so it's really based on their interpretation.

analysis.name: Melanie Abrams
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Pretty good teacher, allowed for group work which was great. There were some concerning and off-putting views she talked about when it came to reading certain words out loud. Overall I liked her and felt that I grew as a writer.

Abrams is a wonderful professor for those getting into creative writing! The class is structured very well to include a mix of reading poems from professionals and students. Her feedback was always immensely helpful, and the small group workshops were a great idea. Having a few students look at my work made a huge difference. Relatively easy A

Very clear assignment instructions, the readings are interesting and short. You will be put into a group who will review your assignments through the semester and it's pretty cool. Discussions in class were always fun.
She is a great professor, with few assignments and a great grader. She makes us work in groups on fridays which become your good friends throughout the semester.

Protect this woman at all costs! I loved taking her class, it was fun and immersive and really made me a better writer. The exercises were super easy and enjoyable with how they tested ur creativity. She felt like a friend who was always there to give you valuable feedback. If u love creative writing u will love this class. I wish I could tae again

analysis.name: Alan Hammond
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof doesn't pay much attention to whether the students are learning. The lectures were not of much use, neither were asking questions. Flow of theorems does not follow textbook so need to attend class. But then again you will need to study the textbook yourself for doing assignment if you want to really understand the concepts. Won't recommend.

Professor makes very less effort to make himself understood. Doesn't address questions. Spends excess time on trivial points and leaves out important concepts. Class is not recorded and professor doesn't follow a textbook, so one has to attend every class and take down everything. Reading a textbook will help more than this course.

The lectures are very verbose and pedantic, and not enough attempt is made to be understood. The honors course could have been much better had it not been for the extreme (ridiculous) formalism adopted by the professor to explain and prove very simple theorems. The grading criteria is almost all over the place and very unclear. Don't be surprised.

Lectures are blatantly soporific. Another Cal class where I had to teach myself everything in the last two weeks.. Prof recommended one textbook and spent the rest of the semester basing the class off a different one. Statistics is an applied discipline yet this felt only theoretical. All proofs. Overall 0/5 if i could

Lectures are often incomprehensible, since he's a rambler AND a mumbler. You can ask him the most basic question, and he starts spiraling into a mess of spaghetti for like 5 minutes trying to answer it. Thankfully, his psets and exams are incredible! Challenging, but extremely rewarding. This is a class I actually learned something from.

analysis.name: Antonio Montalban
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: For a college calc class, 16B is pretty chill. Lectures were good, homework was doable, you got 10 attempts on the online quizzes. The final and 2 midterms made up the majority of your grade. All three tests weren't too challenging, but he didn't provide much prep material. I would recommend going to the SLC review sessions.

Did not enjoy my time in this class. Exams were computationally easy and had a pretty generous curve, but I wish he provided more practice (no practice exams provided, minimal homework). A few GSIs made worksheets, but if it weren't for them, there would be basically no practice sets at all. Lectures were hit-or-miss, but he's funny ig.

Professor Moltalban is one of the silliest professors I've had. He has a very calm pace to the class and can take the whole class to solve 2 problems. Hw is really easy if you are integral savvy or took BC or Math AA HL in HS. Lots of resources available for you to study. GSIs are eager to help you. If you're not STEM, take this class.

Lecture is very slow paced and boring most of the time, but actual content is very easy. Not too much homework and quizzes are easy with multiple attempts allowed. Midterms are also not too hard as long as you study and curved very generously (e.g. 20/30 = A, 15/30 = B)
The professor was kind and would give funny examples, I found some of the content confusing at times and he isn't always the best explainer but I found the class interesting.

analysis.name: Wasim Azhar
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Wasim is knowledgeable in his field. He gives lectures with no notes, just walks around reciting all his knowledge which is kind of cool. Just know that attendance is mandatory, there are surprise quizzes in class and if you aren't there you lose the points. Make sure you read the cases and homework because that is usually the quizzes.

I don't understand the disrespect for Professor Azhar, he was a great mentor and teacher to my whole class in the Summer 2024 course; there were many memorable moments and times where I was inspired. He's very qualified and intelligent. It's easy to berate somebody when the grudge is really on oneself, a 5.0 difficulty for THIS course shows it all.

Wasim is really boring lecturer. He is also not that interesting or exciting to listen to in his class. His marketing class seems to be lifted out of a textbook from 10 years ago, as there is nothing new or innovative about the concepts he teaches. However, he is caring and a kind-hearted person. There are a lot of assignments and very long exams.

Each hour I was required to attend his lecture was by far the worst part of my week. Be prepared to stuff your backpack with hundreds of printed lecture slides and not understand one word he says all semester.  I wouldn't wish this professor upon my worst enemy. AVOID AT ALL COSTS.

God awful. no real world experience. out-of-touch. complacent. monotone, mumbling, talk-to-self lecture style. gets offended by simple questions. cant answer basic questions. makes up stories about himself; self-promotion. In-the-box thinker. rewards safe answers. slides all rambling text; spend class time reading slides silently like 2nd grade.

analysis.name: Alan Karras
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 60 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He is certainly NOT the best and his teaching content and style are not very good. However, you can get an A in his class very easily.
Poor lecturer but easy class. The class material is also very outdated.
Easy class but a teacher below par!

The subject material for this course is so so interesting yet he manages to make every lecture boring and give a history lesson instead of talking about the actual theories from the reading. He rarely talks about how the theories apply to our world today and lectures are very boring. Most learning comes from the reading and going to discussion.

I hate this seminar. It is long and redundant. We receive very few (or no) guidelines for our papers. I think Karras is a nice guy, but, after taking this class, I would warn any and all IAS students not to take the honors seminar,  unless you want an enjoyable year. Wow, I really detest this class.

analysis.name: Ananya Roy
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 63 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Roy is DEFINITELY overrated! Just go watch her TED talk and see how much you learn. She gives a one-sided argument without acknowledging important counterarguments even when she knows they exist. She has become the consultant that she criticizes about in Dead Aid since she only criticizes with esoteric, made-up terms without providing a solution.

Global Poverty is inherently an interesting subject & everybody ought to take a class on it. The Idea of the Global Poverty Minor is very cool & hats off to Roy for that. Is she the best Global Poverty teacher I had at Berkeley? No.Is this class the best in terms of expanding your mind? Also no. The focus is rather narrow with a few repeated ideas.

I found this site and I can't believe this! I earned a (pretty easy) "A" in her class and I agree w/her politics, but Roy is SUCH a case of The Emperor's New Clothes. All of her lectures can be boiled down to two or possibly three coherent thoughts. The rest is a sort of theater. Life is short, time is valuable, and I don't need to pad mine.

Huge class, about 500 to 700 students. Good teacher. But not necessarily as amazing as everyone claims for her to be. The class seems like it is very difficult because of all the reading, but a little effort will take you a long way. Used a reader. I got an A-. Overall, a class I would recommend if interested in international development.

Didn't learn much. Categorization of development concepts and testing for theoretical terms were excessive and impractical. She's a talented professor, although I feel that I still can't exactly pinpoint what those talents are. She was able to tie in a wide range of disciplines as they related to development.

analysis.name: Ron Hassner
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 77 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Ron is the best professor Ive ever had, the only class I never miss lecture and always enjoy. He is knowledgeable and funny, and cares deeply about his students. He will make active efforts to get to you know you and make himself available to talk if you just send him an email. He makes questions for midterms and finals available ahead of time!

Prof Hassners War class is incredible and one of my favorites at Cal. I definitely recommend taking it. You learn so much that is applicable outside of the realm of war and IR. Lectures are really engaging and Prof Hassner is very accessible and encourages OH visits. Class is some work but everyone is able to succeed. Offers extra credit!

Take Ron's War class. You'll learn a lot. Grading on the midterm and final are fair. Section attendance is worth 20% of the grade. Ron is an amazing prof who is entertaining, caring, and is excellent at explaining concepts. Go to his office hours!! He genuinely cares about each of his students.

Stellar man.  Tries hard to be fair and profesional.  No wonder Muslim and Jewish students who are against or for Israel/Palestine sit in the class together.  I guess that's why.  Respect.  Also lectures are fun and exciting.

Great Class, professor gives 3 additional points for writing a film review, so many people got an A in the class. The midterm and final are 2 essays and a few ID questions. The essays needs to include the readings and lecture materials into it. The essay questions often are very vague, you need to ask your GSI to give you an outline for each essay.

analysis.name: Adrian Lee
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 74 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The professor is nice, mediocre at explaining concepts and walking through practice problems, but his exams were beyond difficult. He doesn't cover or explain enough, and the difficulty and complexity of problems far exceeded his lecture content. The concepts are basic, but exams are about difficult, complex, and twisty applications of the topics.

Lee is a very nice and caring person overall, but his methodology for classes and exams lacked a bit. His online pre-lectures were nice to introduce the student to the topics, but his actual real-life lectures were hard to keep up at times or he took way too long to explain how to solve a single problem. Also, good luck with rotational motion lol.

The median of our final exam was 33%, a testament to Prof. Lee's lazy approach to teaching. All material was taught in pre-recorded homework videos, with follow-up practice in lecture that we never finished due to Prof. Lee's tendency to ramble. My grades improved after I stopped going to lecture because I was able to use my time more productively.

Chill guy but terrible lecturer. Seems to be very knowledgeable and intelligent but he can't teach. He utilizes a 'Flipped classroom', nice in theory but with how busy college gets, expecting us to watch around 1h before the start of the school week is an insane time commitment bc on weekends we have HW/Lab in addition and other subjects to work on

The flipped classroom approach in theory is good, however in practice it was truly a struggle especially for someone who is taking physics for the first time. The GSI's aren't very helpful either because there are things that the professor glosses over without explaining and he expects us to know these things from a previous class.

analysis.name: Eliza Brown
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Brown, while intelligent, is quite a patronizing professor. There is mandatory attendance, and she will often berate students for arriving 2 minutes late in a hall of 300 people. The lectures are also pretty boring, and the readings are numerous and tedious. The class itself is pretty easy, as she offers a lot of extra credit.

Great professor and such a sweet + genuine person - you can tell she is very knowledgable! Class was really interesting and covered a wide range of topics in the field (very nice for an intro class). If you paid attention in lecture, did the work, and understood concepts, not too hard. Would definitely recommend and take one of her classes again!

I really enjoyed the class. Attendance was mandatory as we did short write ups at the end of lecture. Lots of reading assigned but passed the class by just reviewing lecture slides and memorizing main ideas(never did any reading). Professor Brown was always very sweet, understanding and always gave extra credit for our essays. 10/10 recommend!

I did really enjoy the content, the professor's lectures were engaging/interesting; however, there are some things I wish I knew. Every lecture is mandatory to attend w/ an in-class assignment. The reading assignments were extensive, with some containing over 60 pages of reading due before each class. In the end, GSI determines final grade.

I totally understand the comments on Prof. Brown's attendance policy, but honestly she was really wanting to be respectful of people's ability to focus, especially during in-class assignments. Every lecture was really interesting! Just skim readings, get the main idea/ argument. I really enjoyed this course, she is a really kind person!

analysis.name: Alexis Shusterman
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 237 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: One of the best & passionate teachers I've had! The night before our final, she stayed up until late at night to answer student's questions on Piazza. She is ALWAYS available. Her lectures are clear & interesting. Esp as someone who didn't take AP Chem & only took HS chem freshman year I learned SO much this semester & she's very fair. TAKE HER!!

Prof. Shusterman is a really kind person and is receptive to questions. She's young and lively and definitely knows what she's talking about when it comes to Chemistry. While I am definitely not the best at the subject, I still have no ill will towards her because she's very nice. On all of her Piazza posts and emails, she puts smiley faces :)

Professor Shusterman is a Wonderful chem professor! Her lectures are clear and relatively interesting and she offers a lot fo resources for her students to do well. The exams aren't impossible but you definitely need to study for them! She provides study worksheets, practice exams, and always answers her piazza questions for her students.

LIVE LAUGH LOVE DR.S ! Her lectures are concise and clear, and her office hours are very helpful; she's super receptive to any and all questions. Chemistry is hard and the exams aren't easy (three midterms), but if you watch the lectures and complete all the extra practice sheets/exams she provides, you will do well.

Professor Shusterman is an excellent lecturer and I would I highly reccommend taking courses with her. I've never met such a caring professor like her. Now keep in mind Chem 1A has 1500 students, so she doesn't really know everyone. During office hours she takes her time learning your name and addresses you by name. She really is amazing.

analysis.name: Mohamed Ben Hammed
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The passion and vivacity Professor MWBH brings to his field is genuinely inspiring. Anytime I had a question or wanted extra reading on a subject, I knew I could reach out and he would expediently find a time to meet and give a fantastic answer. Understanding of circumstance and rewarding of demonstrated interest, my favourite this semester.

Professor Hammed is a wonderful teacher! His passion for the course's content shines in each lecture. Comlit 155 was all about course participation, and deep engagement with the readings; the selection was extremely interesting and carefully curated, and I will think about this class for the rest of my life! 100% recommend taking his classes.

It was a pleasure taking a class with professor Ben Hammed. Class felt like a breath of fresh air and discussions were something I always looked forward to. His knowledge in his field is, to say the least, impressive, and I learned a lot from him. He is also very understanding and readily available outside class.

MWBH is an excellent professor. I took this class for an upper div humanities breadth but it genuinely became my favorite class. He is outrageously educated and intelligent. He truly knows so much about language and the world. There were two papers in the class, one 5 pager and one 10 pager, very manageable and he grades nicely.
Very sweet and caring about his students and what they are learning. Encourages students' passions and is very responsive. Good selection on syllabus.

analysis.name: Bonnie Morris
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Class is made up of: short paper, midterm, and final. Attendance is taken at lectures, there are lots of readings, some films in class, but no homework. Overall, professor is very interesting and passionate about teaching. Paper is 3 pages MLA, Midterm is 3 in-class essays, and final exam is ~10 short answer questions with a longer in-class essay.

Professor Morris is organized, and her lectures are engaging. The course has 3 assignments which are based on the course material. Take her class if you want to learn about history and not have to sacrifice your life to get a good grade.

I marked that attendance is mandatory but I think she said you could have like 5 unexcused absences. She described it as "your easy class". Her lectures are very engaging and she is very nice but she holds herself in very high regard and makes that clear; I can see why people would find that annoying but she is nice. Office hours are chaotic

She is not tech-savvy at all and attendance is required, her lectures are just her talking so you need to pay attention and they are important. There are readings for the class but if you attend class she will cover it. She is a very nice and informative professor and you will watch movies in class would recommend talking to fulfill AC requirement.
i definitely recommend 100D even if you aren't a history major. i took it spring of ‘25 of loved it

analysis.name: Stephen Bianchi
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 84 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Classes are boring and filled with unnecessary proofs that not only does he not explain, but then has to correct in the following class. Often its completely unclear what we are even trying to prove. Little structure, a close reading of the textbook is necessary for this class. No notes posted online, no use of slides.

Dont think he knows what hes talking about since hes constantly making mistakes. His idea of teaching proofs is literally to memorize every step and he often goes on unnecessary tangents instead of focusing on more difficult concepts. For such a slow teacher, he is also very impatient with students and lacks basic empathy. Do not recommend.

Bianchi is by far the worst professor I have had at Cal. He is extremely arrogant, does not care about his students, and straight up rude. His grading is easy and he doesnt teach/ test for anything beyond the surface. If you want to take it easy without mandatory attendance, go for it. For anything else that is worth your time, stay away

Avoid this class at all costs, it will kill any interest you might have in finance. I've had a 4.0 up until taking this class, and this one killed it. Midterm was hard and final was insanely hard. The culmination of micro, calculus, and even linear algebra you have to know for this class makes it ridiculous. Formula and proof heavy for no reason

Created my account just to rate Bianchi. Lots of thing's come to mind but the main point is that none of them are good. No point of even taking the class as there is no support at all. Midterm was fine but the final exam is clobber for 65% of your grade. There are three final practice exams he gives, none of which actually helped for the test.

analysis.name: Laleh Behbehanian
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 77 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: What an amazing professor who's passionate about her work. Even though I'm a stats major, this is the only humanities class (out of 3) that I thought was worth attending this semester (and attendance is mandatory for all 3 of my classes). Elucidates the readings in class lecture, and is very accommodating. Take her 100%

I took political sociology in summer 2017 and Laleh is amazing! She unpacked this topic in a unique way with various theorists like Tilly and Brown. She is truly invested in her students and made every effort to know students names and be available above and beyond outside of class. "Pop quizzes" were broad enough where you had to try to fail.

AMAZING lecturer. Taken 4 of her classes. Sociology of Policing was the best class I've taken in my life. Prepare for light reading. Since you only have to do 9 reading responses throughout the course you don't have to do all the readings, the lectures will make you feel like you did the reading anyway. Heavy content trigger warning.

Laleh was my absolute favorite professor! I took 4 courses with her over my 5 years at Berkeley and I learned so many things in every single one of them. Laleh cares so much about her students and the topics she teaches. Readings are mandatory, but nothing she assigns is filler and she takes the time to create extensive reading guides.

laleh is amazing. if you can take anything with her plz do. im not a soc major but she makes me want to be. she always repeats what you need to know & says it in a super accessible way. take good notes. tells you exactly what concepts to study for midterm & keeps to her word. once in a lifetime prof. just take her!

analysis.name: Siri Brown
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I enjoyed her class, even if it didn't relate to my major. I learned a lot, and despite the fact that there was a fair bit of homework, it was mainly watching videos with some reading (easy work, just takes time). Her exams also have a BIG focus on that homework, so definitely take notes! She also offered exam prep. sessions, which I found helpful.

Great class overall and for pre-law students, since there is cold-calling in class. Very clear on instructions and grades fairly. 2 tests. Gives very specific content for review before midterm and final. 1 Group project, will boost score. Make sure to read and attend class. 2 papers, not excessively long. Offers 1-on-1 feedback through Zoom.

She's an easy grader when it comes to group projects and essays as long as you follow the rubric. She grades more harshly on the midterm and final which are worth 50% of your grade. She does require you to buy a course reader. Not bad of a class you will pass as long as you keep up with assignments, follow guidelines, and participate.

Overall, this was one of the weakest academic classes I have taken and offered little intellectual challenge, functioning largely as an easy A. The requirement to purchase a $20+ course reader was especially frustrating, as the materials consisted of articles freely available online that could have been distributed via bCourses.

Interesting lectures where you learn a lot she makes it clear in the beginning what to expect from the class. Very educational and relevant to issues in our world today and I thought that the readings were very interesting. She also makes it clear when office hours happen.

analysis.name: Carlos Bustamante
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Bustamante starts off his section for 102 by saying that you need to know everything from the textbook, lecture slides, and things that he mentions during lecture. All you really need to study are his slides--they are concise and well made. Make sure that you record his lecturers, and review them later with the slides. Hardest section for 102.

Frankly, Carlos Bustamante tarnishes his legacy and the very study of biochemistry every time he speaks in Wheeler 150. He lacks a picogram of insight or skill when it comes to teaching, I image toddlers would explain protein structures in far more robust and detailed manners than him. He is a disgrace to the very name of Berkeley, should be sacked

This professor was actually one of the worst professors I have taken in Berkeley. Absolutely atrocious! He made our exam three pages of his research, which he barely covered. His accent is very hard to understand, and he did not post recordings even though he could have fully understood them. Actually hates students. If you can, AVOID!!!

Terrible teacher. Should never ever be allowed anywhere near a teaching environment again. He does not post recordings just to mess with us and make us memorize a billion things and guess what? On the midterm very little of what he asked us to memorize was on it and instead he included tons of info about his garbage, useless research.
If you aren't religious, pick a religion and pray. I'd recommend recording the lectures in class as he does not post them. GO TO EVERY CLASS.

analysis.name: Jill Bakehorn
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 77 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Jill Bakehorn was a decent professor. I'm a sociology student and I thought her lectures were a bit dry and boring. But overall not a terrible class. The readers on the other hand were horrible! Lets just say I got A's in every other class except for this class. The expectations for the papers were unrealistic.

Took Sociology 160 Fall 2025. It was a good course; the workload wasn't too much, and it was basically just reading. Some in-class written assignments and the final was a take-home essay; there is a no-electronic policy in class unless DSP accommodations. Professor Jill is very chill, and the class is not difficult. I recommend this class.

very writing heavy, esp. in class, so make sure you know the readings! lectures aren't attendacne mandatory but i highly suggest going since her uploaded slides don't contain ANYTHING (like 2 words per slide) and she does a good job of breaking down some dense readings. pretty tough grading, esp on the in-class responses.

Dr. Bakehorn has the most engaging, informative, and enjoyable lectures of any professor I've had. They & their grad-student graders are tough but they give good feedback and provide lots of help along the way. There are no in class tests, but there are lots of short to medium length papers. I would absolutely take a class from Dr. B again.

Though grader, overall her classes are interesting, but she is always contradicting what she says. Especially if you are a DSP student shes not very caring of your accommodations. She seems to give your her own accommodations of what she wants not what your asking. I get her position and respect her, but she should do the same.

analysis.name: Robert Braun
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Don't get me wrong--Braun is an amazing lecture. He is a brutal grader and not empathetic at all. There was no clear communication between what he wanted in his essays and what the GSI's were looking for. It was almost impossible to get an A (I get all A's in other upper div classes). He also doesn't follow departmental rules. Wouldn't recommend.

Although this course was very interesting, Braun's approach was often times demeaning to groups and condescending. Definitely has an air of superiority, and the GSI's for Spring 2019 were incredibly tough graders, never gave any feedback even when prompted, and Braun cares little about the students.
Great lectures. Exams were a bit confusing.
I really enjoyed the lectures.

Braun is a good professor and a good public speaker. I took this class for a GE, so I am biased when I say that it's unfortunately boring. The readings were subpar and often too lengthy for the amount of information received. His grading criteria was not very clear, and the grades given by GSIs varied a lot. Solo projects were incredibly boring.

analysis.name: Robin Ball
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 45 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Ball is awesome! This course is not lighthearted though -- definitely took a lot of studying. I made and grinded Anki decks every week. Read the modules before and after lecture. Everything on the midterms and final exam were things covered in lecture or the modules. There were opportunities for extra credit for attendance and quizzes.

Lectures are not particularly great for learning the material as the course modules yield the same material featured in lectures, except in more depth. The class often had 50-60% average scores on midterms and 60-70% on quizzes. However, Ball does not curve so you must grind out every point to get a desirable grade. # of ppl. w/ A is probably 10%.

only take this class if you are looking for something to consume your entire life & suck all joy from the world. she changed away from open note tests. she has a personal vendetta against letting students enjoy life. prepare to memorize everything under the sun + the chemical composition of the sun while you're at it. i can't unrecommend this more.

Most overrated professor. Her lectures were a reiteration of the homework so they were useless. A lot of the course grade came down to harshly-graded health social justice topics which only offered a very progressively-biased take and were only tangentially related to health. Weirdly refused to call them "male" and "female" reproductive systems.

Dr. Ball was a fantastic profesor that made course material very accessible via bcourses, while also clearly breaking down concepts during lecture. This class required a lot of studying, but there were opportunities for extra credit and very cool class that everyone should take at some point.

analysis.name: Lawrence Cohen
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 48 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This guy is so bad. I feel like he's knowledgeable but he sucks at teaching the material. Period.

He's passionate but his class is a BORE. He took away the free online readings halfway thru and made us pay for it. Avoid this class when Steve's at the helm.

The midterms are not representative of what is covered in lecture or homework, and the harsh grading is discouraging to all students. It's a shame that he has made an interesting subject so unbearable.

analysis.name: Erica Bree Rosenblum
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof uses prerecorded lectures which likely have been reused throughout the years. GSIs literally do all the work and are confusing in their expectations. The textbook (that she wrote) is mandatory and has confusing graphs. She has done nothing to interact with the class herself directly. She feels very disconnected from her classes.

She is a great lecturer, her course was really organized, expectations and rubrics are clear, content is interesting, it's easy to reach out for help, and it's really easy to get a good grade. You will need her textbook and GSls do most if not all the grading so keep that in mind. The class has honestly been my favorite so far in Berkeley.

Bree is one of the best professors at Cal. She REALLY cares about the students. She goes so far beyond the call of duty for any professor's duties! The class is interesting and she is so enthusiastic and fun. She is funny and bubbly. Always a pleasure to be around. You can ask her any question and she will not make you feel stupid. TAKE THIS CLASS!

Bree was a great professor. She got to know each student individually and support us in achieving personal growth as scientists and as people. This was the most humanistic approach I have seen any professor take to teaching a science course and it was extremely rewarding. You will gain new research skills and meaningful connections.

Bree is an amazing professor and I highly recommend to take her class. I had some moments where I was not sure about things but going to office hours really helped me and I did well in the class. The material is interesting and Bree is just amazing! Highly recommended!

analysis.name: Enrico Moretti
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 70 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Everyone struggled with time on the midterm. I got slightly below average on the midterm because I didn't budget time well. Still got an A because I did all of the practice problem on the back of each chapter to prepare for the final. A lot of the questions on the final were similar to the book questions.

Moratti does not teach at all. He just reads off of lecture slides which can be pretty dry. You solely depend on your GSI to basically teach you the concepts besides doing independent reading yourself. You are graded on literally three things : the midterm, a tiny paper, and the final. Be wary of this class if you do not have a background in Econ!

i had no econ experience. bro really needs to either post lecture recordings or at least give the slides (he does neither for an 8am). the final had questions that were on topics about lecture. i got an A- without ever going to lecture for the second half of the course and just read the textbook. curve is crazy. he is not a good prof at all.

Exams are graded very strictly. One thing that drew me back about Moretti was his accent, it just made lecture slightly more difficult to understand. Lectures weren't particularly useful or helpful and felt lifeless and boring at times.  Exams are above average difficulty, so do lots of practice problems. Go to review sessions and youll be fine.
Interesting class but tests almost have nothing to do with textbooks or notes

analysis.name: Erick Bell
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The concepts taught in the class itself are not difficult, but the professor does not teach with the same rigor as the midterm and final. He carries a superiority complex and focuses less on accounting and more on his opinions on social issues. Make sure to review outside of class, the McGraw-Hill is very good practice, also spend time on projects.

Took UGBA120AA (Intermediate Fin Accounting) with Professor Bell. He's the GOAT. Very funny personality and easy grading. Homework is due every couple of weeks and 2 final projects due at the end of dead week. Bell uses Becker CPA tests for midterms and finals, but usually reuses the practice exams he gives. So, as long as you study that, easy A.

Professor Bell is collectively known by students as one of the worst professors at Haas. This semester, his midterm was completely different from the massive amounts of homework he assigned every week and not a single person finished on time. He makes students pay for an online textbook to complete homework but wont make any tests relevant to them

I am a decent student, who puts in the work to study and do well on exams. Professor Bell's midterm was terrible and dropped my grade to the lowest I have ever received. The average on the exam was a 60% with no curve!! The format of exams are not at all reflective of homework and quizzes. Do take this class if you want to be scared for your life!

I don't know how I passed this class. Especially knowing that I wasn't given the opportunity to clobber. I also note that attendance, though on the syllabus stated as not mandatory, is MANDATORY. (If you want the unfair advantage in signing a contract to clobber) Haas please reevaluate this courses policies as listed from my peers below.

analysis.name: Fang Xu
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr.Xu is a great lecturer, however, assignment rubrics are not clearly communicated at all. Students who followed her advice would often end up losing points in the process. She claims to be accommodating, but refuses to allow absences due to illness without a doctors note. The reader for this course is cold and clearly dislikes their job.

Professor Fang Xu is awesome. She is super knowledgable about her field and loves to facilitate group discussion. I've been super grateful to learn not only from her but from the diverse linguistic perspectives that she encourages to be shared in class. She takes the time to learn every student by name and she's funny too!!

While the course material is interesting, the professor is not lenient at ALL with absences, even with illnesses, considering this is a 3x a week class. The GSI and professor don't communicate, which leads to awful grading. So many presentations and discussions that don't contribute to anything.

Fang's lectures are very clear and relevant to the assignments she gives. Readings are mandatory, don't slack in the first few weeks, those are the toughest ones. Grading depends on the GSI's, one GSI was a harsher grader. Discussions help with the denser readings. 3 short papers, 5 in-class quizzes (based on completion), midterm exam, final exam

Fantastic professor - had her for ISF 189 and ISF 100C as well. She is clear about her grading criteria and her lectures are posted online (with audio). Provides excellent feedback and is readily available via email or during office hours. If you follow her assignments closely and revise based on feedback, it is not hard to receive a good grade.

analysis.name: Noha Farghal
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The best professor. I took her Physics 4A at De Anza. She's probably one of the best professor that gives the easiest gradings. She only have quizzes and finals exam. The quizzes are on mondays. Quiz are super easy. It's only once question and super super easy. Final exam is very manageable with two hours. I finished the exam in one hour. Pick Her!

I took Prof. Farghal for 4A. This class is super easy to get an A in. She isn't the best at lecturing, it's very surface level. But she is very nice, cares about her students, wants you to pass the class. Responds to emails quick as well. Your grade is just based on a couple quizzes and the final.
Super nice teacher would recommend!

The lecture is too long without a clear focus. No emphasis on what to study. Also, I hate group project in an online environment especially we never see our classmates. Group project are good for GSI so they don't have to grade too much but not good for student. However, prof is nice.
Too many "ums" during the lecture. She might need to practice her presentation skills. It's not pleasant to listen to lectures with frequent pauses. Can be more prepared!

analysis.name: Francisco Armero
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This guy was the best professor I have had at Berkeley. His lectures are extremely well organized and crystal clear.  He seems really serious at first but he turned out to be hilarious. This class was a lot of work though, so be prepared.  But he is a fair grader and curved his ridiculously hard final.

Prof armero is a great guy but he does not teach the best unfortunately(might have been an off semester as he was dealing with health and personal issues). you could tell he wants students to suceed and really tried to get to know people but it was hard to understand lectures. he curved really hard and gsi eduardo was the goat

the exams are very challenging, but if you practice w/ tau beta pi you should survive(though the final is 30% more complicated then the ones on there). he still have a good sense of humor and will answer questions more in depth after class or in OH fairly well. Also sit in front row, he likes front row students a lot.

I had this professor and for our midterm he didn't allow me and a few other students to start the midterm until after 30 minutes (out of 1:30). Every other student was allowed to start. His reasoning was that we didn't come to lecture enough

He is not the best at explaining things, so I learned everything from the GSI and book. His lectures didn't seem to be related to the homework or exam problems, so make sure to read the book and do extra practice problems. He notices whether you come to class, so try to ask and answer questions to get participation points.

analysis.name: F. Dean Toste
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Pretty easy class. Two in class lab reports that are just the discussion and post-lab questions in the book. NMR section was really tough, but if you go to office hours the GSI's will answer every confusing question for you. Final was also very easy.

i foolishly decided to take this class for fun.  turned out that i wasn't as much of an organic chem whiz as i had thought.  i should have put in more effort. no textbook, must attend class and pay attention (class goes by quickly, he's easygoing and fun). easy to be in the mean of the class but must go above and beyond to get an A.

He is obviously really good at Chemistry but he is not good at teaching students who aren't naturally good at or previously experienced with it. I found his class very difficult as someone who hadn't taken AP Chem in high school. He seemed very snobby, as if someone who didn't understand what he is teaching is dumb.

Toste is a decent professor and a real chemistry whiz, but I noticed pretty early on that teaching doesn't seem to be what he's here for. There were a few occasions when students tried to ask questions and he refused to answer, however he still gave great demos and had a sense of humor!

I thought he was a great professor. He showed us very interesting aspects of chemistry and tried hard to make things clear. The beginning was rocky but then it got a LOT better. OH are very helpful and he is very approachable.

analysis.name: Benjamin Faber
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: 2 Problem sets, midterm, and final exam. Attendance is required for both lectures and discussions. Study the lecture slides and section assignments. Grading can be strict for the problem sets. Lectures can be difficult to follow; very self study orientated. Textbook is optional. Class is curved to a B. Recommend taking Ryan Edwards instead.

Appreciated the good vibes. Speaks fast, but lectures are super clear and breaks down the concepts really well from my perspective. Always available for office hours. Not sure what some of the low ratings are on about, honestly.

Confusing professor and very hectic lecture style. He throws concepts at you and will jump between different lectures within one class. Makes it really hard to follow along and GSIs don't offer much support either.

This class is already difficult enough but he makes it much harder. I go to every class and always come out more confused. He either talks in circles with no substance, or calls things "intuitive" (when it's not at all) and moves on. His lectures are long and his slides don't make sense.
The class is difficult but Prof Faber tries his best to make the material understandable.

analysis.name: Francis Annan
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Lectures move quickly & can be all over the place, but he'll re-explain previous concepts. Appreciated voting on grade weights; however, didn't communicate well w GSIs, often causing general confusion. Doesn't curve individual assignments, but curves entire class's grades so that nobody fails. GSI OH was helpful pre-exams (1 MT & Final).
Very caring professor who values his students' experience in the class. Lectures could be more organized, but overall fine delivery of course content.
Genuinely caring professor who's super accessible and willing to help his students outside of class

His democratic way of choosing the class structure was considerate (we got to vote on the date of the final and the weight of each assignment on the syllabus), but sometimes confusing since he didn't update on bCourses. Lectures were super engaging, and he's happy to explain anything you don't understand and set up an OH meeting.

He's a nice person, but not a very good professor. His lectures are just a summary of the textbook chapters. The textbook can also be a bit confusing and wordy. Homeworks on pearson are boring and not very helpful. Overall, would not recommend him as a professor unless you're ok with self-teaching yourself from the textbook. Calculus heavy as well.

analysis.name: Francoise Sorgen-Goldschmidt
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Native speaker of French with graduate degree from the Sorbonne. Helpful, consicentious, optimistic.

phonetics course, web-based. the nastiness of the course is the website, not the teacher so much. she's very helpful and devoted to listening to questions during office hours. she's strict and mean sometimes, but that's okay.

Made me question my french language abilites.  Very condesending, doesn't teach in class, relies on the website.  Makes class sing a lot.  Generally unpleasant.  However, phonetics will improve your french.
Prof Sorgen Goldschmidt is really nice and helpful especially in office hours. She is really quirky and  funny and will definitely teach you practical french.

analysis.name: Emiliano Gomez
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 114 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Gomez sticks 100% to the textbook (STUDY IT). He is absolutely brilliant and always willing to take extra time to help his students. His pacing for lectures could definitely use some work. Often times he would cram 4-5 examples into the last 3 minutes of class. He listens to his students, he's nice, he cracks jokes here and there; he's a great guy.

Gomez makes sure he is transparent about course policies, what will be on tests, consistent on posting online lecture notes, and is very willing to answer questions on homework problems in office hours. He also talks very fast during lecture as he mostly reads off of his own notes. One of the final questions was modeled off of the 2nd midterm.

His entire curriculum revolves around doing the homework. The quizzes? Revised Homework problems. The exams? Harder homework probelms that are super niche. Just do the homework assigned and turn it on time; actually understand how it's solved and you'll do great. Curve was decent; had pneumonia half the semester and bombed tests and still got a B.

Easy class made slightly more difficult by the professor. He has a deep interest in proofs and concepts that we are not tested on. It is inspiring to watch him break down the concepts but it really feels like a waste of time. He is a charismatic, flexible professor with good GSIs. Tests and quizzes are ridiculously easy.

Bad at teaching the material. Don't bother going to the lectures; they are worthless. His handwriting is too poor to make out on lecture notes, and he talks so fast it is impossible to follow what he is saying in lecture. Ur cooked if u didn't take calc in high school (I didn't). REFRESH URSELF ON GEOMETRY. Big class curve, my 50% curved to C+.

analysis.name: Mark Goble
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Goble was excellent. He asked provoking questions, even if the class sometimes didn't take them up immediately. Intelligent, amiable, highly approachable, culturally well rounded, down to earth, and an all around nice person! This made his paper comments seem somewhat harsh at times, but the grades didn't reflect such. Highly recommended!

The class was okay.  His ideas on some of the novels weren't broad enough; he liked to keep it to one theme.  He made my favorite novel--this was the reason I took the class so I could  hear something from a Berkeley Prof. and learn more--and made it seem dull. When I talked to him about some symbolism, he one-up'd me and just quit talking to me.

Did not have that conceited Berkeley English Professor attitude. Attentive to students, connected material to modern society/culture. Very fair grader, reasonable expectation of students. Lectures were interesting, he was funny and shy in a charming way. Would really recommend him, he treats his students well

Goble is one of the better lectures I've met, if only for his balance. If you really pay attention to what he is pointing to he is extremely profound, but he is not overly oppressive about his topics. As for approachable, you could not ask for a better. I've taken 3 classes with him and just watch out for awful GSI's as he is just too nice.
Lecture was great, GSI was not. Prof Goble is incredibly smart and has a great sense of humor. I loved the film clips and context around the books.  Extremely kind and helpful in OH

analysis.name: Mariane Ferme
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 47 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Instructor said no recordings, but only recorded for DSP students. Said cameras are not mandatory. Later got mad during Zoom, saying we needed cameras on for participation and attendance. Someone brought up no-cameras statement in chat, but instructor ignored it despite often responding.

While P. Ferme is very interested in Africa, her class environment is the worst I've ever seen. She becomes easily frustrated with her students for answering questions wrong or for doing poorly on a test. The tests are in exam format and based purely on readings. She did offer a retake, but it was oral. Just save yourself the trouble.

This professor is the worst, I just took her and she was so cold and quite disgusting to be around. I tried my best and ended up not even being able to pass the entire class because she said I didn't participate to her standards because I was sitting in the back... I attended every one of her class and she met twice a week and still failed me.

Ferme is very brilliant and that is clear. At times she could be a bit pretentious which is seemingly the reasoning for many of these bad reviews, however, her class is full of interesting content. Despite minor disorganization in how we go about discussions/readings, this class is for someone who will ACTUALLY read and be engaged- She's fine.

A passionate researcher forced into an undergraduate teaching position, that's what it gives. Cold & excessively apathetic. People who are criticizing here aren't lazy. I was one of the most engaged students in discussion, but given all the wonderful professors in this department, save yourself the trouble, don't think twice, don't take her classes

analysis.name: Josh Grossman
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Amazing professor. Josh Grossman was engaging, knowledgable, and polished during lectures. Prof Josh really cares about his students and wants them to do well in the class. Made data science fun and super understandable. Would take again if I could

Def the goat of Dat 100, makes time for his students even after the semester is over to talk to them about career goals, you can tell he is passionate about the subject in all his lectures, give this man a tenure.
really passionate, took data 100 with him in sp25 and wanted to leave a great rating cause he is always so caring of his students and is really welcoming in OH

Has very similar vibes to Data 8 but since the material is better, I think this class is better by default. Prob the best class I've taken at Berkeley and a prof makes sure you understand the material. The only non-mandatory attendance class where I've gone to more than half the lectures in person and don't regret it.

Josh is the GOAT! Genuinely the most caring and accessible professor at Berkeley. His explanations of even the hardest topics were so amazing and hands-on, and he was always advocating for the students and their well-being. can't recommend him enough. Professor, if you are reading this, please know that you helped so many students this semester 🙏

analysis.name: Karine Gibbs
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 52 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Spends time rushing through the lecture but expects us to know so many minute details for the midterm. It is practically impossible to keep up with what she says during lecture.
Overpacked and rushed lectures. Poor planning. Hard midterm. I had to self-study almost all of the content. Least fun section of any class I have taken at this school.

Gibbs was very enthusiastic about the subject, but she was not good at teaching it. Her slides were essentially just the textbook and she spent little time explaining anything really. She would often not finish her slides and the exam was very difficult. I had to self study the entire unit from her lack of clarification during lecture.

Honestly very amazed at how the Spring 2025 staff managed to make every single worst possible choice while running this course. She is enthusiastic about the material but relies heavily on the students to read the material beforehand, because she doesn't get to finish most her lectures. Take when Mike Meighan retires and Lones teaches genetics.

Beware! She says you don't need the textbook because everything's on the slides, but the slides are a total mess. Half the time I couldn't even tell if I understood English because the way she explains things makes zero sense. She can't explain even the simplest ideas. Unfortunately, she teaches the hardest section in Bio1A.

analysis.name: Karina Gutierrez
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The worst experience I have ever had with a professor, avoid at all costs. Not only did this professor never cover any material pertaining to this course, they also used it as their personal advertising space to promote ticket sales for shows they were involved in. If you value your time or your art, stay far away from this professor.

Prof Gutierrez is disorganized and we were always behind in class. I think she uses in-class discussion as a way to not have to lecture tbh. The lectures were rambling like she didn't know what she was saying or what she was going to say next. Grading is insanely hard for no reason. I felt like my grades were random. Maybe she will get better, smh.

Came to our theater directing class to sub  class and basically just wasted time for2 days bragging about the play she is directing. Didn't teach us anything and just keeps smiling like that's supposed to make everyone feel chill about it. This department is a disaster for real- wants to be closed add. Lmao

Profe gutierrez is really nice and I really enjoy her personality, but I don't think theater ac is the class for her. She really leans on discussion, rather than lectures, and we wasted a lot of time discussing during lectures. I wish there was more structure to her class, though I will say that it was her first time teaching the class at Berkeley

surface level, very sweet, but there's a performative arrogance that I disliked. She was often behind on her lectures, I don't think she finished a lecture in the entire semester, and the ones that she did do were riddled with typos. Despite having discussion sections, she wasted time on discussions during class. Way more difficult than necessary.

analysis.name: Grace Lavery
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Lavery is my favorite professor at Berkeley; I take her classes no matter what the subject is because I know the lectures will be amazing. She's witty and hilarious while also clearly caring deeply for her students and the subject matter. She wants everyone to succeed and takes feedback very seriously. I can't recommend her highly enough.

Professor Lavery is one of the greatest professors I have ever had. I am lost for words while writing this review because the man changed my life. He made me rethink literature (and the world) in so many ways, and taught me what critical thinking really means. He's an amazing, super dedicated teacher. Just take it, I promise you will learn. AMAZING

If you get a chance to take this (or any) class with Professor Lavery do it! Their lectures are phenomenal brilliant/funny/organizedit's not an easy class the midterm and final were the hardest I've had at Cal, not because Prof Lavery tries to trick you - they just inspire you to think harder, write better and work harder-will make you smarter.

Professor Lavery is both the most personable and most otherworldly professor I've ever had. She is the perfect combination of an intellectual and stand-up comedian. Her lectures were incredibly thorough and thought-provoking, and she easily kept the attention of the entire room. If you pay attention and do the readings, you'll be fine.

Eng 161
Prof Lavery is a brilliant lecturer, but oftentimes trailed onto confusing side tangents (w/ the addition of obscure references that are hard to follow). Her grading style/coursework requirements were relatively lax, but grades were never regularly updated. If you're passionate about philosophy, English, and the arts, definitely take her!

analysis.name: Marco Gonzalez-Navarro
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The class is disorganized. The syllabus said we were supposed to have multiple partial quizzes and he removed those after the first quiz, leading the class to be very test heavy. The Psets aren't helpful for prep because they're in R (not included in exams). His slides don't include the information being tested, making review difficult.

Graded mostly on exams and 2 homework assignments that seemed random. He also expects you to already know R. Lectures are just summaries of weekly readings. Tough grader on tests, but the test prep provided is helpful. Some exams questions aren't specific enough, leading to lost points. The concept of the class is interesting, but poorly executed.

DO NOT TAKE THIS MANS CLASSES. The class I took (Econ c171) was extremely test heavy. He doesn't care for his students or external circumstances at all. Highly disorganized in terms of instructions and exams. He's a tough professor, please try and take any other class. Save yourself. 

Test heavy. Unfair/discretionary grading practices.

Professor Gonzalez-Navarro is amazing. I loved his class, and have been recommending it to others. He cares a lot about his students, the subject material is really interesting, and really encourages participation during lectures. I highly recommend engaging with the material during lectures and asking thoughtful questions.

Avoid this class if you can! The concepts and course itself isn't difficult but the professor is really disorganized making it difficult. He changed the syllabus 3 times after the first day of classes.  The course topics can be interesting, they're just not lectured well

analysis.name: Greg Aponte
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 66 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The lectures were dreadful and he often went off on tangents so you didn't know what info to absorb. For midterms and final, you have no clue what exactly you need to study. Do not recommend if you are not a STEM major or haven't taken AP bio or similar. Assignments were easy and you're fortunate if your GSI is good. Rougher class than expected.

To be honest, he was boring. Lecture was boring and I did not learn in lecture. I learned from reading the slides on my own time, which were not too great either. People say this class is an easy A, but I would say that if for students who have taken AP Bio or have a Bio background. For me, I spent my time memorizing the slides. Wish I did P/NP.

If you have taken any bio the material in this class is easy. I just made flashcards based on his powerpoints a couple days before midterms and got an A. You should go to weekly discussion and make sure to do all the hw assignments. Overall, the class was a breeze but the professor was incredibly boring and uninteresting so I never went to lecture.

Don't take. Most boring prof ever. Very fast-paced too, so impossible to take good notes. The only reason I went to class is bc he doesn't webcast his lectures, but I realize now that going was a waste of time. Just go through all the slides and memorize everything the night before a midterm. Got a healthy A, but feel like I didn't learn anything.

He's a nice person, but lectures were very dry and sometimes confusing. The tests were pure memorization and it's easier for people who've taken molecular biology (AP or college course) before. Assignments were pretty easy to complete and having a good GSI is beneficial.

analysis.name: Peter Hurtubise
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Peter's lectures make no sense, have nothing to do with the textbook or section activities, and are always closed by a 5-10 minute long motivational speech that is literally unbearable incomprehensible nonsense. Your ability to learn anything in this class will hinge on if your GSI is a good teacher, not on anything that Peter says.

by far the most passionate prof i've had at cal and i always left his lectures inspired. unfortunately the grading is confusing, with vague rubrics and a page limit i found too constrained for the complex prompts. also there are no lecture slides or recordings. i would recommend this course tho esp for ac credit- great guy with good things to say !

Didn't really like teaching style. You're "supposed" to learn Stata but he just assigns YT videos and textbook so unless you do it, you won't learn. Stats part really missing overall. But you do choose a research topic interesting to you and work on that all semester. Grades based on midterm, final, and participation. Both exams relatively easy.

Professor Hurtubise talks very fast, but it makes the class go by quickly. He makes all of his students feel included, even though it is a big lecture. he is very passionate about his subject and grades a total of 3 assignments throughout the semester.

Amazing guy, very inspirational and passionate, but poor format for the class. BCourses is bare, there's no syllabus, and expectations for assignments are, not just unclear, but never stated. There's about two sentences of directions, no rubric, and he barely mentions it in class. Lectures are good and interactive but no slides, no recordings.

analysis.name: Ian Holmes
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: For me, this class was easy. I had no trouble went by breezy. This is because, im a prodigy. To put it quite simply, im a genius, hehehe. Prof. Holmes aint for everyone, but for me, twas breezy.

Lectures were extremely dense and often hard to follow, with explanations that assumed a high level of prior knowledge. Much of the learning felt self-directed, relying on past modules and old Zoom recordings. The professor's tone could be rude, communication was inconsistent, and exams were complex with material barely covered in lecture.

Unfortunately, I felt as if the material he chose to teach was rather simple. Of course it's one of the "harder" courses as noted by the average minded people. Yet, I noticed a lack of truly difficult deep cutting material. Maybe I'm just...smart

Don't take this class unless it's the very last class offered in Berkeley. You will have to spend a considerable amount of time doing the lab assignments, your grades will very likely suffer, and you will learn jack from this class. Please do yourself a favor and learn from my mistake.

VERY VERY helpful and sweet! Ian has sufficient knowledge and he's brilliant, the material he brings to class covers the core ideas in Bioinfomatics, and he can bring even more ideas from other subject like machine learning and statistics ! Really enjoy his class.

analysis.name: Josh Hug
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 86 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He came out of a garbage can on the last day of lecture.
Best professor I've ever had at Cal. Great lecturer, hilarious guy, and realllly cares about the students. He knows 61B is tough and gives all the support he can.
Josh only joined the faculty a summer ago, but if you want definitive proof that Berkeley's CS department rightfully deserves its place at the top of the universe, take 61B with Hug.

He's an entertaining lecturer, is up to date with meme humor and has funny, reasonably timed and appropriate side tangents. He talks too fast sometimes and he's better suited for someone who can keep up with a fast paced lecture. Not a fan of how he drastically changed the 61B format this year without giving us a study guide on the new format.

Although the class has a heavy workload and exams are difficult, I cannot imagine a better intro CS class. Professor Hug prepared us extremely well for basic coding interviews and taught problem-solving and algorithms in a way that stuck with us for a long time. Always grateful for CS61B!

analysis.name: Dan Garcia
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 163 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Dan tried hard to make CS10 fun, but in my opinion, too much time was spent on building "energy" and hype and not enough on concepts like recursion. You will only interact with the GSIs in this class - Dan seems accessible at first, but you'll find that he's quite aloof. The exams are difficult but all of the points are made up in projects.

Garcia is an enthusiastic lecturer, but lectures were not deep enough to match exam difficulty. The Fa25 semester ran as a test run for Dan's “A's for Everyone” initiative, and it just didn't pan out well (exams averaged below 65, extra points didn't bring the avg up to a 65, yet bins remained the same). Beware if you care about your GPA.

Dan throws out a lot of "As for All" nonsense to make you hopeful about passing the class, but he wont pull through with that. Grade bins are set with an expected exam avg of 65%, and when all of them are under 65% he wont shift bins. He wont curve exams/final grades and gatekeeps score distributions so students are really left in the dark.

The “A's for everyone” model felt like a poor fit for a CS class in my experience. It was stressful since small point losses mattered a lot. I found some exams unclear or ambiguous, with high score variation. There is a small curve at the end, but earning an A+ felt extremely difficult.
A's for All? More like A's for None!

analysis.name: Hidetaka Hirota
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 42 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Horrible class and a very unfair professor. He shows a complete lack of understanding that this class is simply an american institutions requirement for many of the students, and he creates unreasonable exams. He comes off as very punitive and grading in the class appears to be inconsistent. Overall, a really unpleasant experience.

Grading is convoluted and seems not tied to syllabus or assignment descriptions. Focus on regurgitating exactly what he said and when he said it (cite lectures by date) rather than course concepts. Incredibly difficult to obtain even a decent grade and grading scale complicated and difficult to follow. Cumulative grades unavailable through semester

The final for this class was extremely tough. The professor seems to not be able to recognize that most of the students in the class are here for a breadth requirement and are not fully immersed into the topics. Course policies and grading were extremely detailed for no reason and caused further confusion. Unnecessary late submission penalties.

This review is for HISTORY 137AC, this class met online every other day and involves reading about 100+ pages a week. There are weekly assignments which are not very hard, two essays, and a final, which is composed of 2 small essays and one big essay, all graded by GSIs who grade quite harshly. Not the worst for a summer course.

Lectures were SO interesting for the entire 90 min, held my attention. But, not recorded so showing up is important; lecture slides on their own will not be useful, it's all about what he actually says. Essays were kinda harshly graded, but as long as you take good notes you will understand everything and be very well-prepared for midterm/final.

analysis.name: Ian Swinburne
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Bad lecturer, mumbles, can only hear 50% of what he says, lecture content is completely different form the lecture slides, slides filled with so much words but he doesn't go over them

Absolutely atrocious. Ong he had to have taken these slides from somewhere else. There's so many words on the slides that he doesnt go over and so i have no idea how to study for the exam. on top of that, IN GENERAL THERE ARE JUST TOO MANY WORDS. he is super unorganized and boring. the WORST out of the three professors teaching this class.

I took this class Spring 24. His lecture material wasn't particularly difficult to grasp and he would let us ask questions during lec. He isn't the most engaging lecturer (kinda dry) and is honestly very soft-spoken. It can be easy to doze off when he's presenting. His exams are really generous though and he's kind/patient. Overall a chill dude.

One of the WOREST prof I ever have. Lectures are SOOOOOOO dry and boring. HE DOESN'T KNOW HOW TO TEACH. He only put tons of facts on the slides and read off his slides. Even the GSI it better than him.

analysis.name: Kayoko Imagawa
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
