review_highlights.comment: Doesn't give clear answers; in fact, after office hours, she leaves students more confused than they already are. I learn more asking AI to explain concepts and textbook examples combined than from her. She says: "textbook will help" for everything, but she doesn't mention herself to support students. She also favors Japanese descent students
very interesting classes, kind professor

One of the best Japanese teacher.  She is very clear in her lectures and explains difficult materials well.  She is also a very funny teacher and makes the class very fun.  Very patient in office hour.  Willing to stay overtime to help me understand the readings.

Imagawa sensei is a very funny, happy, sagacious teacher. She is very helpful and creates a healthy comfortable classroom environment. you are expected to learn a memorize a lot of grammar and vocab in the class, so having a teacher like Imagawa sensei is key to doing well.

analysis.name: Ion Stoica
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Goes far beyond surface-level operating systems concepts. Instead of just memorizing how virtual memory or scheduling works, you are forced to understand the invariants, failure modes, and performance tradeoffs behind real systems. The projects are intense, but they teach you how OS components interact under concurrency and resource constraints.

Class is a must take but if you can avoid Stoica I would. Droning and mumbling 90 minute lectures, and he forced in some overly complicated scheduling algorithm when we were still learning the basics. Ended up watching lecture videos from years past for most of the term.  On the credit side his homework assignments were interesting.

Goes far beyond surface-level operating systems concepts. Instead of just memorizing how virtual memory or scheduling works, you are forced to understand the invariants, failure modes, and performance tradeoffs behind real systems.
Amazing professor, its great and is a great lecturer, Amazing professor, its great and is a great lecturer
Amazing professor, its great and is a great lecture, Amazing professor, its great and is a great lecturer

analysis.name: Ignacio Chapela
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 47 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He's a kind and passionate professor who is constantly questioning the world around him + enjoys conversational lectures. No hw other than 2 tracks to pick from: quizzes throughout the semester or writing for the final. I recommend the writing track, it's not graded harshly and it's more of a way for you to write about what you're interested in.

Ignacio was an incredible lecturer! I felt like I could engage strongly with the material and he definitely made me think of my role on earth so much differently. The syllabus was a bit messy, but I learned a lot, and formed a great group of friends by attending his field opportunities! DO NOT skip those, they're so fun!!

Really enjoyable class. Prof liked to make lectures a conversation and encouraged us to share our ideas, even if they were contrary to his own. I chose the writing track which ended up being one 2-3 page, hand written essay, a field opportunity, and microcosm project. Guidelines weren't super clear, but all the assignments were interesting.

I choose the quiz track and it only requiered 3 quizzes, the semester long project, and field opportunity. Professor Chapela is really cool and passionate about what he teaches. Attendance is not mandatory, and he turns the discussions into field opportunities in the mornings or office hours, very accessble even tho getting an A is easy.

Very easy class, didn't go to lecture or discussion at all. I chose the quiz track, 3 very manageable quizzes, one microcosm project, one field opportunity project, and that was pretty much it. The instructions were a bit brief for the projects but very doable. Definitely an interesting class if you engage.

analysis.name: Ryan Hass
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 175 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Hass is brilliant, but he struggles to carry that intelligence over into a lower division math class. I have quite literally studied for dozens of hours before midterms, only for the practice problems, homework, and textbook to simply not show up. His tests are the hardest I have EVER seen, and this is his second(?) time teaching the class ever.

He was a bad lecturer, was not very inviting. Additionally, his exams felt quite different from the way he taught us the material. I found it very difficult to learn from him. Also, he assigned so much homework, which was so unnecessary. He also frequently made mistakes during the lecture and would correct himself a day or so later.

He makes his midterms very hard, and he's definitely teaching 54 from a pure math point of view. He includes a lot of proofs which are interesting, but hard to understand in lecture. His practice midterms are also terrible and don't reflect actual midterm material one bit.

Lectures were too fast for my liking. He doesn't give practice tests in the form of his actual tests, which every other teacher I've ever had does. And I've compared his tests to the tests of other professors and his are definitely the hardest. Who knows why. He's not the worst teacher but I don't think he understands how hard he makes his class.

I mean pretty much echoing what the previous students have said. Professor Haas is obviously incredibly good at math, but not a great teacher. Lecture videos were gatekept until end of the year, and exams were not like review guides at all. Yes he's smart, no I would not take another course with him.

analysis.name: Alastair Iles
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Alastair is a fantastic professor- he is involved with his students' interests and whipsmart.  Take his classes if you can!

Great professor and class. Most lectures were structured around learning a sustainability transition framework and then a case study that fits it. There was one group project. A fair amount of readings, but they were all really interesting.

This was a great class. Although the three papers and the final exam were pretty time consuming, they were all graded very easily and also pretty enjoyable if you are interested in environmental issues. While the professor unfortunately cannot speak to the class, he puts much effort into writing good lectures and including interesting material.

A great professor- you will learn a ton in his class.  The hearing impairment makes for challenging communication at times, but he has worked out a great system for delivering his lectures with GSIs, and is able to respond to questions and give feedback with a computer.  Thoughtful research assignments.  Overall, a fantastic class.

class was super chill, you are graded off of two problem sets, a group project, and a final essay. The professor and GSI were great and want you to succeed. definitely recommend this class to anyone interested in the topic

analysis.name: Iain Clark
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The class is very disorganized. Lectures weren't that helpful, had to rely on discussion sections most of the time to understand what was happening in class. Prof Clark was nice, and the class itself was not that bad, but it was very disorganized.  The homework seemed to be nothing like was taught in the lectures and it seemed pretty random a lot of the times.  There were times when the professor did not know how to answer to the homework which was frustrating.
His lectures are unnecessary to go to. He's a really nice person, but rambles a lot.
Very disorganized class. Do not take if it's not a requirement.

Professor Clark is amazing! His lectures are super interesting and you can tell he cares a lot about what he teaches and his students. He's very accessible outside of class if you ever need help with homework.

analysis.name: Ian Davis

Davis was like a breath of fresh air after trecking 15 mins from Jha's lecture (iykyk)

Passionate and genuinely interested in the topic and student's opinions. Helpful GSIs and clear, thought-provoking essay topics. I genuinely enjoyed his class and respect him as a lecturer. Not a very difficult class, you definitely reap what you sow.

MS112&114-
Dr.Davis is a nice guy; however, he's interesting. He gives you 2 chances on quizzes, but doesn't let you see your score after the 1st attempt??? Makes you do "stages" of the essay (a series of 4 mini-essays for the real essay... by now, I could have finished the essay). Hard to follow his train of thought as he frequently digresses.

Very nice guy, but kinda harsh and not very organized. There were so many unnecessary assignments that weren't worth a lot, but require quite a bit of time. Exams would ask for pretty specific details that aren't necessarily related to the concept (eg. what is the name of that clown from a study...) Honestly ended up hating the class by the end.

Prof Davis is very straight forward. His readings are always super brief and full of info. The exams were online, open note, with exception to the written portion. For this class we had to do three essays and a bibliography which felt excessive given the 3rd essay and final are almost the same thing just with your analysis added to it. It was great

analysis.name: Jordan Mursinna
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: Nice professor. Class has a good amount of reading with weekly responses in discussion. He puts nothing on his slides and reads off his script for the lecture, so you have to pay attention. Overall though, if you do the readings and listen the tests are very predicable and reasonable. Your GSI is what really matters.

He is a an intimidating person. He is knowledgeable and passionate about what he teaches. No notes on slides, write everything down. Assigns 70 pages of reading a week. Reading quizzes every week. Thoughtful participation affects your grade a lot. Just memorize history well enough and exams will be fine. Grades writing sorta harsh. Daunting class.

Lots of reading, but content covered again in lectures. Lectures were super interesting and felt like he was telling a story. Grading sets up students for success. You'll do well if you do the readings (just skim them, he explains further in lecture), go to lectures, and participate in discussion. He made content I usually find boring interesting.

This class is reading heavy but each subject is covered 3 times (in reading, discussion, and lecture). Mursinna's lectures are entertaining, easy to follow, and rarely off topic. This is mainly because he reads off of a script which is off putting at first but I became used to it quickly. Lectures were not recorded and exams were graded easily.

Taking Data 104. Does Mursinna know he doesn't have to lecture like a self-aggrandizing TEDTalk speaker all the time? I'm. trying. to. learn. about. Silicon. Valley. but. I. can't. pay. attention. because. he's. talking. like. this. with. the. strangest. vocal. inflections. ever. His cadence of voice is grating.

analysis.name: Jess Johnson

Great and very caring teacher!

After taking this class with O'Brien I changed my focus to graphics.  He has worked with me to help get a good internship at DreamWorks.  Most profs are Cal are to busy to talk to you, this guy  actually acts like he cares about the students.

Monotonous but informative lecture. Has an insane knowledge of the subject and can answer any question. Take the class with him if you are interested in graphics because you will learn anything you are interested in. If you dont have a special interest, it will seem way too broad and dull, however.

At the start of the semester, everyone hyped up Professor Ng as really good at teaching and said that Professor OBrien was very monotone. While it appeared like that initially, if you went to lecture, it was clear that couldn't be further from the truth. He was great in answering q's but I will say that he caters to the top students in his lectures

I think he focuses more on the top students in the class.  For example he will skip basic stuff and focus on big picture.  I liked that a lot but my project partners got frustrated that little details were not covered.  He has really good industry connections and just got an Oscar.

analysis.name: Stephanie Jones-Rogers

review_highlights.comment: Rogers is kind, approachable, and gives really interesting lectures. She is super helpful and friendly during office hours; she even gave me feedback on a paper for another class. Also, this class is fairly easy to get an A in. She gave us 3 extra credit papers adding up to 18% on top of our final grade! Got an A+ overall.

I absolutely loved Professor Jones-Rogers! I'm a soc major but I took her class to fulfill requirements outside my major and her class ended up being MY ALL TIME FAVORITE AT UC BERKELEY! Seriously, she explains some pretty graphic and violent material from history with grace, understanding, and knowledge. She is approachable and helpful! Gold star!

Professor Jones-Rogers is amazing! A wonderful lecturer, approachable, concise, and well organized. All readings available on bcourses. If you're willing to work hard, you will learn a lot! Well worth it! This was my favorite class this semester! I'd take another class with SJ-R if I wasn't graduating! She's the best!

Assignments are fair imo, but the professor's tone makes the environment tense. Feedback can feel belittling, with emails comparing course errors to "not paying rent." She expects 100% dedication to this single class and enforces strict participation rules she doesn't personally model. Hard to stay engaged when the communication feels hostile.

The professor is clearly very passionate about what she teaches, if we were going solely off of lectures I'd give her a 5. This is more about the structure. No feedback on assignments that take hours to complete, harshly graded writings that come with rough feedback. Constant changes to extension policies + yelling at students via announcements.

Refused to talk into mic bc her “toe was numb” & she needed to walk around but didnt set up any other solution for the huge group of Zoom students.

A professor that clearly could not care less about teaching. Her slides are poorly prepared, full of errors, and as a result her lectures are terribly confusing. A very sadistic professor who cares little about teaching and more about showing off what she knows. Was never present for office hours. After one particular office hour she asked me to walk to her car and promptly cut me off mid question as soon as she reached and said “times up”. 
Someone who hates students should not be a teacher.

analysis.name: Karthik Shekhar

review_highlights.comment: Prof Shekar is really great lecturer, cares about students and their learning, and is also pretty funny. The class is difficult and a good amount of work as all the chem e classes here are.

Shekhar is not good at teaching. He expects students to understand from his lecture, but in reality you need to consult the textbook to score well on his exams. He also sets grade bins to "show" students their place by saying if your not up to a certain standard you shouldn't pursue ChemE.

One of the clearest and engaging instructors I've had. He explains difficult concepts in an intuitive way, and his notes and real-world examples really helped me understand thermodynamics. He's approachable, funny, and genuinely committed to helping students succeed. I always felt supported, and his flexibility and fairness made a big difference.

Professor Shekhar is an incredible professor that is able to take intense and overwhelming topics and create a story that is easy to follow from beginning to end while leaving no detail out. Incredibly knowledgable about the topic and incorporates humor into his lectures to ensure students pay attention.

Shekhar gives excellent and well organized lectures. Even though he has a stern, no-nonsense style, he cares about his students and is really helpful during office hours. Attending his lectures are the best way to follow the material. Exams are tough but fair.

analysis.name: Kristin Sangren
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

review_highlights.comment: The worst class taken at Cal. She treats the class like hers is the only one we are taking. Very negative & discouraging, she discouraged everyone from going to law school. Lectures are disorganized, readings were boring. Would not recommend. Also brings in a lot of politics into class lectures, of course one sided and not up for discussion.

I found the instructor to be unapproachable and dismissive when clarification was needed about course standards. This made it difficult to understand how to succeed in the class.

Sangren is great and loves her content. There is A LOT of reading, and she does not hand you an A for doing nothing, so if that's what you want look elsewhere. If you want to learn however, it's a great class, stressful, but fun. It's a good class to push yourself and see what you can handle, especially if you're interested in law school.

Extremely boring and monotone during lectures. Workload is unreasonable, and we have readings before each class, up to three large readings per class. Doesn't give study guides or post-lecture slides and CONSTANTLY goes over time. She gets upset when people get up after she's been talking for 10 extra minutes. Unorganized, rude, and unapproachable.

Prof. Sangren is incredibly knowledgeable and well-spoken. Her lectures truly give me a greater understanding of the legal institutions and their interplay with society. This course and her other one, 160, are two of the best classes I've ever taken. The readings can be quite long, but they are well chosen and always interesting.

analysis.name: Khalid Kadir
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 59 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: You shouldn't graduate from UCB without a class with Khalid! He's balanced, energetic, and makes you want to read and learn more.

Khalid made my experience at UC Berkeley worthwhile.  I love how he is able to merge his engineering background into poverty alleviation.  You can't bs or rush his assignments because he KNOWS when you are, which means he also knows your true potential and believes in you.  He gave me a lot of valuable feedback that'll stay with me into my career.

PE 101  was best class I've taken at Cal. You can tell he really cares about his students and lives to educate.  He really changes the way you see the world, see development and underdevelopment, and understand power in general. Kadir is truly inspirational and you must take one of his classes before graduating!

My first review but Kadir is definitely worth it! Such an exceptional professor with amazing GSIs as well. His PE101 class should be mandatory for all students--he is super knowledgable, helpful and transparent and wont trick you on the midterm/exam. Favorite class I've taken at Cal!

I am now a super senior and I can say he has been the best lecturer I have had to chance to take. I took his GPP intro course. Amazing. My palms would sweat every time I went to lecture because of the excitement and passion he'd put on 'em. Lecture becomes a luxury and not a responsibility. Talk to him. He gave me a letter of rec.

analysis.name: Kai Xu

Okay the readings are a bit absurd, but you can kinda just skip them and read the slides and/or go to/watch lecture recordings. uri is a funny guy and always kept it real. i appreciated all the transparency within the course. they can be slow on grading assignments, grade cutoffs are weird (above a 95% is an A), and tests are confusing. takes feedback seriously though and always checks in. class felt really ai heavy. overall, just an okay class experience.

analysis.name: Leo Chen

Great professor. His exams were fair. Just do the work he asks you to do. Do the optional problem sets in addition to PLWS. Professor was very generous with participation credit and plws assignment credit. Only got around half of the plws credit and attended only half the lectures, but still got full participation credit. Extra credit available too

Leo is one of the best professors I've ever had at Berkeley. Super engaging and really helpful. He was also generous with grading as needed, so as long as you consistently went to office hours, did problem sets, and worked through post-lecture WSs, you were set. Sometimes exam questions could be quite difficult/weird, though, so keep that in mind.
Had him for 3b/3bl. Very clear lectures that are easy to understand and puts in a LOTTT of effort to help students succeed. Really willing to answer questions and made me like organic chemistry!
Had such an awesome experience and made me actually like chemistry. Connects well with students and makes sure you're understanding the material. Best class at Berkeley so far!

analysis.name: Lisa Yan
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Not recommended. Professor Yan may not be well suited to teach a mandatory course. The material is very difficult, and there is limited support for the student perspective. The teaching style felt lacking in empathy, which made it harder for students to understand the material and progress in the course.

The professor's interactions with the teaching assistants have often come across as dismissive and lacking empathy. Additionally, there seems to be limited support or encouragement provided to help students progress in their academic journey.
Very difficult professor with little empathy for student learning or progress. I would not recommend taking this class. Unfortunately, she regularly teaches this course.

There was little flexibility for students who wanted to go deeper or needed alternative ways to engage with the material. This made it difficult to feel supported in my learning. I believe offering more options for self-paced learning or extra support from qualified TAs could greatly benefit future students to progress.

One of the worst lectures I've had; it always felt like she hadn't practiced before class. Many times, she stumbles over her own jokes which unnecessarily wastes time with the awkward silence. 

The class is harder than it needs to be and it seems to be designed as a "weeder" class rather than actual instruction. If you know low level, it's easy.

analysis.name: Jonathan Lang
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 47 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The agenda of the class is great (Monsters); but taking this class with Prof. Lang was pointless. He's a close-minded professor with a huge ego, analyzes everything in a sexual perspective, and will demean your intelligence if you ask too many questions.  Save your time and pick a better professor, unless you took R1A with him.

Professor Lang was often condescending to students. The entire course it felt like you were writing to satisfy his opinions instead of actually bettering your writing. All writing techniques were taught by yourself with quizzes. He didnt teach in lectures. If you dont feel comfortable talking about sexuality the entire course, dont take it.

WORST PROFESSOR EVER!! he is very ambiguous about all of his assignments, and it seems as if he doesn't really want to help you. DON'T EVER TAKE THIS COURSE WITH HIM! it'll be the biggest mistake you'll ever make in your life.
Only if all the other classes are full for College Writing R1A, DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!The professor is extremely unhelpful and he grades the essay really hard.

First I thought the class was interesting, but then dreaded it. Books were interesting, he was available for office hours, and let you resubmit essays. But, the class was entirely about satisfying the way he interprets novels. He was often condescending and never fully explained what he wanted. If you arent big on lit analysis, dont take his class

analysis.name: Lev Michael
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is such an eccentric and likeable person who wears a cardigan every day and lights up, as though you are a genius, every time you ask a question. I loved the focused learning environment--no computers allowed, and he WILL call people out for being on their phones.

Very sociable and very friendly, the real life "Indiana Jones" minus the bad parts. A genuine adventurer of the modern age with his trips to the Amazon rain forest to research languages. He is really a cool professor who cares for his students.Also a linguistic anomaly as he is a real life example of complete loss of his first language(Japanese).

Great and fun class that I thought was pretty easy. If you're good at solving puzzles and finding patterns you'll be fine. Weekly HWs are short multi-choice quizzes, there are three midterm exams and a final but the midterms are not too bad. No writing is involved and you don't really need to do the readings.

I wish I could take Lev for all of my classes. He is so funny and charming and his lectures are genuinely enjoyable. 3 midterms is a lot but it is honestly not bad at all and everything is open note. Copy down the slides and understand them and you could get a 100% in this class. He also gives two attempts for weekly homeworks. Best professor ever!

lev is a great lecturer and i love his sense of humor. his lectures were boring sometimes. 3 midterms + 1 final which i think is too much. some of the gsis suck in terms of teaching, but you will learn a lot from lev. very passionate and extremely articulate! not fond of him not providing recordings of lectures, and exams were kinda tricky too

analysis.name: Lorenzo  Lones
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 71 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Maybe he knows what he is talking about but he does not convey that properly to a class. Will draw way too much focus to irrelevant things and then say the important info in a sentence not on the slides. Feels like I'm furiously writing the whole lecture to keep up and then still have to rewatch lecture to make sure I didn't miss anything.

was struggling in his class, went to office hours for advice. all he had to say was i don't know how to learn, and if i don't know how to learn i will never be a scientist. worst thing i have ever heard from any professor, ruined the class for me and is something i still think about when im struggling in class.
Good lecturing but he is a strict grader. There were also alot of different issues like typos/ mistakes on different assignments and questions were often worded confusingly on exams.

Dr. Lones is an eloquent lecturer and an amazing public speaker. However, the contrast between his lecture persona and office hours is kind of insane. He was kind in lecture, but office hours felt awkward and intimidating, making it hard to ask questions without feeling judged for not knowing. I wish he showed more compassion for students needs.

His lab section is poorly organized and feels genuinely deflated. I think this course is not organized well from a grading standpoint, and you learn almost nothing - it practically just makes the already difficult 1A material much worse. Some of those exam questions were out of pocket and felt like trivia questions bc of how random they were

analysis.name: Maciej Zworski
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 139 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Mixed bag. His lectures were more of a Comedy Show than educational that you won't learn anything going to them. Doesn't help that he refuses to provide a list of GSI office hours so you're completely on your own in this class. Exams were curved down since we did too well. If you care about learning Multivariable, take this class with someone else!

Very poor lecturer, disorganized, messy handwriting. Uses discrete grade bins for exams instead of a continuous curve so barely missing a cutoff can screw you over (think n = 4 Riemann sum instead of an integral). Overall, a negative, tedious, and stressful experience, and not what I was hoping for from my first UCB math course. Wouldn't recommend.

Zworski teaches interesting lectures which encompass a lot of proofs and derivations, which I believe are quite helpful. Though, he will often switch up notation or teach concepts in somewhat awkward manners in order to make you think. He also has a good sense of humor and answers questions well. His grading is the only thing I would be wary of.

By far the worst math course I've taken so far. Zworski seems like an alright guy, but he only teaches theory in lectures and not how to actually solve problems. Exams are graded extremely harshly, with very little (almost no) partial credit being given on the final. Avoid Zworski at all costs, wait a semester to take MATH53 with a better professor

He did end up actually curving  the final, but nonetheless still wouldn't recommend Zworski. The class was exam heavy (90% of our grade) and he was very big on giving us negative credit for questions we got wrong. His handwriting is definitely messy and doesn't record lectures but is obviously a talented mathematician. Overall wouldn't recommend

analysis.name: Margot Szarke
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Super enthusiastic about the class and encouraged all her students to share their ideas. Margot encourages everyone to participate in discussions and is an overall super kind professor. A LOT of mandatory reading but it makes class discussions more interesting. A lot of essays too but she provides great personalized feedback!
Explained grammar very well and always took time to detail exceptions and clarify confusions. Grading was fair, she was understanding of our language level.

participation is key in this class and if you dont participate voluntarily enough then she will make you participate. participation was a weekly grade and if you miss class you get points marked off

it's not a difficult class though, and as long as you take the work seriously (especially the sam) then the class is easy

she is also very nice

Margot is very passionate about Art History and I am glad that this was my introduction to the subject. This course satisfied the R1B writing requirement, and she actually had excellent writing advice. I will use a lot of these writing tools for the rest of my life and I can thank her for them. The reading did get to be a bit too much at times.

Margot is an awesome french teacher! As it is a language class, she often cold calls, but it really helps with actually learning how to spell the language rather than just write. Amazingly energetic and bubbly, and very accommodating for office hours and any help you need. All around great experience!

analysis.name: Nicholas Mathew
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 42 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: best class I've taken at Berkeley. Didn't even know when I signed up that we'd be going to see some amazing concerts for free, and even meet players from the Vienna philharmonic!! Mathew is a riot: razor sharp and  opinionated, totally changed how I think about classical music. the few times you're bored, it's kinda nice just to watch him... ;)

Mathew is a born lecturer. Easily the most hilarious and well-spoken professor I have ever had. SO in touch with his audience (this is rare in lectures) and always open to chat. Everything he says is simultaneously a riot and poetic. Always walked away with something to think about. I'll miss this class; wish there were more like it. Keep it up NM.

In all my years at Cal (and believe me, it's been too many...) I've never had a professor as eloquent or as engaging as Prof. Mathew. Most entertaining lectures I've ever sat through - between the copious wisecracks and pop culture references he gets the course material across very clearly. TAKE HIS CLASSES. :) Ladies, he's kind of a dreamboat.

One of the best professors I have ever had.  Funny, clear, passionate about the subject matter, concise, friendly and approachable.  Tests were fair, papers were short and lectures were fun...  Go to them and you don't need the book for much.  As stated by others, don't miss the Beethoven lecture.  Great professor and class!

He's an excellent lecturer, no doubt about it. My issue was the fact that he seemed to heavily dislike me on a personal level. He would  take lines out of my paper and dissect it in front of the class, which was a bit hypocritical considering he ranted about my vocabulary, yet he himself is quite bombastic. Marked me down for illogical reasons too.

analysis.name: Mary-Ann Robak
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 223 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Professor Robak is the best professor I've had after 3 semesters at Berkeley. Lectures are clear and highlight the concepts that will be important for the class while leaving room for student inquiry. Problem sets correspond to the material taught in lecture. Exams correspond to the problem sets. Leaving this class with a greater love for chemistry

Professor Robak is probably one of the worst present at Cal. She refuses to curve and makes her tests incredibly hard, theyre not up to par with her lectures at all or the psets/practice tests. I studied everyday for this class and had a B. Her final however, was very difficult so my grade fell from a B to a C. Avoid at all costs if possible.

Success tips: If you can understand how she writes/organizes her notes, do iClicker in bed and skip lecture. Each week, spend 4 hours learning/reading from her posted lecture notes, and 8 hours tackling her *2* psets for the week. Practicing mechanisms can become muscle memory (like a jigsaw puzzle) rather than mentally straining. Do hw before quiz

I made an account here just so I could give my review of Dr. Robak. Overall, she is friendly and approachable. Problem sets way more (annoyingly) redundant than other profs, and exam unfairly tests specific material that rewards you for coincidentally studying the right things, rather than knowledge. Final exam heavy; I went from A to C this week.

She's a great professor! Super helpful and super kind. Stay on top of the material, and you'll do well. Doesn't deserve any negative feedback. She works hard and knows her stuff extremely well. Definitely worth enrolling in her class

analysis.name: Karen Nakamura
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Honestly really annoying and was doing too much for an AC class. I can tell she's passionate but it's really not that helpful when she just goes out of her way to make the tests difficult. Dont understand why she would do that. But otherwise, it's a lot of work for an AC class and I dont reccomend. Loved my GSI though.

Absolute joke of a class. Grades are based on ability to regurgitate professor's opinions. Lectures are mostly about the professor's personal emotional state. One lecture was her just reciting the poem from the Biden inauguration and talking about the "big orange turd" president. Like what is the point of this?

Lecture is a waste of time. If you want to hear someone talk about everything without saying anything—take this class! I thought this was going to be an easy A, but this professor did everything possible to make it hard. I would not take this class again it was a waste of time.

good overview of disability studies. many lectures were off topic discussions about totally random topics. I felt those were a waste of time/money. criteria for assignments was incredibly frustratingly vague ("entertain me!" "half points if you submit sh*tty work full if u do something interesting") but the class was easy and I enjoyed the readings

This class is one of the most frustrating classes I have ever taken. Not a single valuable piece of information has been taught, and we are literally being tested on her random rants about who knows what during lectures. I do not recommend taking this class or any class by Karen. Good luck.  WOAT

analysis.name: Jesse Nathan
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: hands down best professor I've had at berkeley. I wish i could take his 100 on Yeats over and over. Classes were the highlight of my week. He is so chill, kind and easygoing and facilitated the most interesting and fun discussions ever. I am usually shy but looked forward to participating in class. Highly recommend any chance you have to take him
Professor Nathan is far and away the best professor I have had at Cal. I took his English 90 and English 100, and I couldn't recommend him highly enough. Wonderful both in and out of the classroom.

Professor Nathan is simply amazing. There aren't even words to describe how much I enjoyed his class. He fostered a comfortable environment and was a class I very much enjoyed. His knowledge on the subject was remarkable and I couldn't recommend this class more. His class is one of those classes where it makes me happy to be an English major at Cal

Professor Nathan is such a genuine and kind instructor. I can tell he is genuinely interested in what his students say, especially with how he sometimes bases his points on a student's insight. Nathan cares for his students, which is present in his feedback and his moderation of class discussion. If you're an English major at Cal, take his class!

Professor Nathan is the best!! Classes were always interesting and he really listens to what everyone has to say. I took his Langston Hughes seminar and we were able to take a mini filed trip to the Bancroft Library to looks at some first-hand materials. One of the best professors at Cal!

analysis.name: Krishna Niyogi
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Niyogi was the best Bio 1A professor. He is genuinely a kind person and is approachable in office hours. He will work with you if you get stuck/need extra explanations without judgement. That being said, he does have some timing issues (didnt finish lectures on time, rushed through teaching translation), but I really liked him and his section.

Out of all three of my Bio1A professors, I liked Niyogi the most. He explained things well in lecture and his exam questions were difficult but fair. I appreciated how he annotated his slides and put up key concepts to know. I didn't score amazingly in his unit only because Genetics isn't my favorite, but he was great!

While his material is hard and complex, his lectures certainly cover everything you need to know. He gives great review slides, and it is very clear what will be on the test. Don't get me wrong, the tests are hard and cover a LOT. But believe him when he says what will be on the test, study hard, and you will do well.

one of the only profs who seems to care about us learning. very active on ed and u can tell he cares abt students. uses engaging ways (like fun demos) to teach content so it's quite memorable. answers questions in a non-degrading way. very nice.

His lectures actually focused heavily on what pertained to the content of the exam, and he did provide review slides for his section. Very smart professor, and highly simplified and answered questions often.

analysis.name: Mohammed Nadeem
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 151 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: One of the best professors here at Haas, and a must take for marketing. This class has a lot of group projects graded very fairly and two midterms, which he basically gives you the answers for. The final is a little harder but has the same format. The only problem with this professor is that he does not accomdate for DSP students very well. :(

Prof Nadeem is genuinely invested in his students. By the end of the semester, he knows everyone's name by heart and is generous with accommodations when needed. The class is well-designed (with real-world applications) and fair (no curveballs). My favorite part was the field trip project, where students can visit companies like Apple, Nvidia, etc.

Professor Nadeem is an amazing instructor! The course was well-structured and the projects we do are directly applicable to the real-world. Exams are pretty easy too - just attend lecture. I love that he takes the time to get to know all his students by name and connect with them:) I learned a lot in his class and would highly recommend taking it!

Professor Nadeem's marketing class was really fun! It's relatively easy and you just have to follow the study guide for exams. He really cares about this students and also brings in interesting guest speakers. He does not require attendance though his class is still fun to go too and you do a lot of group work in class.

Professor Nadeem truly cares about his students and takes time to get to know everyone. He keeps the class engaging through group discussions and participation. One assignment involves an office tour to learn a company's marketing process, which clearly shows how course concepts work in the industry.

analysis.name: Fae Myenne Ng
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Super chill and easy class. She cares a lot about her students and really facilitates an intimate, familial setting in class. Lots of class discussion and writing, but easy to BS. Also, she acts super strict and demanding the first week or two to weed out the weak ones but she's actually really caring and easy-going.

I enrolled into this course after the second week of the semester and she refused to share any information for the first two lectures. She considered the class closed when it was open to enroll on Cal Central. The professor did not disclose any information in the course description which is extremely misleading for a student.

Life changing professor and life changing class. With Prof Fae's leadership & guidance, the class really became a community (the real deal, not just the buzzword) and I grew a lot both as a person and as a writer. She's intimidating initially (I think to scare off those that won't take the class seriously), but softens up with time. TAKE THE CLASS.

Prof. Fae has kind of a prickly demeanor, but she's friendly if you personally speak with her. She likes facilitating student discussions and encourages us to self-reflect, which did help me improve my personal writing. I will note, however, that she doesn't write letters of recommendation.

I've never encountered a more condescending instructor during my time at Berkeley. Professor Ng, would deflect all of my questions with snarky responses and made me feel like my value as a student in her class didn't matter. She's great with memorizing names but that falls in line with her holding grudges. I don't know if others had the same issues

analysis.name: Rasmus Nielsen
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Super chill AC! Lab (basically attendance-based) is 30% of the grade. Optional project to boost your grade and you get a lot of freedom w it--just do it. I got 100% on both the project and paper, without really stressing about either (and doing them two days). Lecture may get a little boring but Rasmus does his best to make it interesting - fun guy

Population Genetics. Tough class. Lots of studying will be involved. Keep up with the class and do the end of the chapter problems FREQUENTLY. Reading the book is advised.  All in all, quite a fun class actually. Lectures are not boring, quite interactive, and clear... until you step out of the classroom. 2 midterms, 1 cumulative final.

Great professor that genuinely cares for his students. Tried to make lecture engaging since it was mandatory. Exams are cumulative and open note, so they're easy as long as you review lecture/have notes. A decent amount of your grade is based on your GSI's grading.

Wonderful prof. He def understands that most are taking for the breadth/AC requirement, and still makes the class very engaging. One of the most kind, welcoming people (not just profs) I've encountered at Berkeley. Great human, easy class, learned some interesting stuff in a subject I originally didn't care much for. Highly recommend him and IB35AC

Rasmus is a nice guy but this class is so boring. Additionally, the essay guidelines are really annoying (why is there a max word count??) Overall one of the most boring classes I've had to take here. Discussions and GSI are also not very useful. 
1/5 Class, 3/5 Professor.

analysis.name: Terrance Odean
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class has annoying af pollev, but the prof's (and the other prof's) lectures are interesting if you care about the personal finance stuff. I took this freshman year and think it's def targeted more to upperclassmen as it's not really applicable at all for me. Still a cool and relatively light class.

He was overall a great lecturer with few dull moments. The class required multiple videos outside of class to watch with quizzes alongside the videos. There's in class questions to account for attendance. Topics are complicated 'adulting' things like mortgages and he does a good job of breaking them down. Exams are relatively easy.

Terrance Odean/Robert Shaye teach you a lot in this class! While the course is mostly made up of upperclassmen, as a freshman I found all of the information extremely valuable/applicable to everyday life. When it comes to course policies; attendance is vital to understanding concepts/getting good grades. I highly recommend this class to anyone!
definitely take 135 w/ him... lectures can be a little boring but he's easily one of the best profs ive met on campus

UGBA 135 was a good easy class if you want something useful for 2 units. Watch the videos and take weekly quiz before lecture. MT and final were easy. Good class for P/NP. Lectures could be a little boring sometimes but the material was very real-world applicable and I would recommend this class to just about anyone w/ room on their schedule.

analysis.name: Magdalena Ostas
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Do the readings and participate and youll do good. Make sure to show you are reflecting on the readings and show improvement in your writing. Gives rewrite opportunities. You will learn a lot if you participate and do the assignments.
Extremely kind and considerate, if you have to take an english class try and get her because you will have to read and write essays regardless.

She's very nice and passionate about what she teaches. Participating in class is easy as long as you do the reading, and she always acknowledges/validates your input. Overall a solid teacher who grades pretty easily too.
Very sweet lady, helpful and understanding. Very easy grader, if you go to class and participate you will be fine.

- Expect to participate in class (basically discussions)
- Remember to print out the readings before class
- R1B English - critical thinking w poets and philosophers is a horrendous class
- Tho she gives good feedback on your essays

analysis.name: Nicholas Paige
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 39 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Great professor! Loves interacting with students during class, makes an effort to learn people's names. 2 midterms + final exam, 6 short writes (which are basically one-page essays, which you can resubmit if you get a bad grade), and 3 readings per week that you must annotate for a grade. Recorded every lecture, was super accommodating.

Professor Paige is incredibly engaging and wants the best for students. He's super lenient with his grading of the short writes (unless you use AI), but be prepared to actually study for the exams. The class itself was super interesting and honestly one of the best ones I've taken so far. It made me have a whole new appreciation for Paris.

Took this class Fall 24 for Art and Lit breadth and it ended up being one of my favorite classes I've taken thus far at Cal! Prof Paige was super engaging and I always enjoyed going to lecture. You'll do just fine if you do the readings and study appropriately for midterms. Maybe not the easiest breadth out there, but I loved it!

I'd say that making a study guide of the recorded lectures is the best way to go with this class, as well as using flashcards or something similar to remember certain concepts. The tests are very lecture heavy material wise and they also borrow some from the readings/films. The professor is fantastic!

Although Professor Paige is friendly, if you want a low-commitment AC course to fulfill the requirement, avoid this one. There was an excessive amount of lengthy and confusing readings, all of which were assigned via Perusall. Moreover, the exams cover bizarrely specific details from the lectures that I never would have considered reviewing.

analysis.name: Kay Ousterhout
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I believe this was Ousterhout's first semester teaching at Berkeley, and she did amazing teaching 61A! Very engaging lectures, funny questions and comments with Denero at the beginning of the class! Kay Ousterhout was very confident, energetic and helpful with the contents of the course. I seemed to prefer the lectures she taught over Denero :)

Professor Ousterhout is an amazing professor! I was lucky to have her as my discussion TA, and she genuinely cared that each student understood the material or, if they didn't, that she helped them learn. She is a very accessible and caring professor, and her lectures were clear, helping to reiterate the concepts from the lecture videos.

Ousterhout always explained concepts clearly and thoroughly. Her lectures were always very well paced, and she was great at answering questions. She would also share extra tips on topics that she saw students struggling with in discussion/OH. Exams are very tough, but I would definitely recommend her.

Very clear lecturer and great at addressing student questions. Go for those easy EC points by submitting projects early. Entire course staff is super supportive on Ed, they genuinely care about student grades and wellbeing. This is a hard course, prepare to grind all past exams from 2021 by DeNero onwards.
Very good office hours and one on one teaching for students. Always approached student questions with openness, empathy, and clear guidelines. Also incredible overall teacher and lecturer.

analysis.name: Oscar Perea Rodriguez
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Honestly, I don't recommend the professor. Yes, the class was engaging but I got a 93% in the class and it was considered an A- which by the standard scale it should be an A. I knew people in the course who got a A as a 93. Preferred his section class rather than the actual SPANISH 25 lecture.

Attendance is entirely mandatory. He is an arbitrary grader and makes no exceptions for absences. His grading scale is frankly ridiculous. A 94.8 is an A minus in a class where he refuses to give high marks, barring complete fluency. Furthermore, he is a terrible teacher who gives useless feedback. I learned almost nothing. Avoid at all costs.
He was a nice professor, his grading was indeed towards the rougher side, but he was an amazing lecturer and also very fun!

Quizzes have weird timing, don't miss them bc I did. Great lectures, only class I truly enjoyed this semester. Class is every day, but only an hour long and he makes it fun and engaging. Just be on the lookout for the assignments online. He won't give many notices, and they only open the day it's due

I struggled a lot with the course because of the topic, but he was very nice and caring and still did his best to work with me and help me understand the material better.  Attendance is 100% mandatory and goes towards your participation.

analysis.name: Oskar Hallatschek
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Lectures are completely boring and useless. Professor Hallatschek enjoys using iClickers, which are a terrible way to engage students and a waste of your money. Tests are straight forward, but the curve is a very strict bell curve.
He is supposed to be clear but takes basics high school mechanics and instead of clarifying it makes you confused about something you had previously mastered. reading the book is more useful.

5A is difficult under any professor, but Hallatschek taught it well. The homeworks were difficult and time-consuming, but doing them greatly simplified the exams, which were fair. Lectures were long and at times difficult to follow, because the course covers so much and mathematical simplification steps would be skipped for the sake of time.

Professor H was respected by our 5A class for his in-depth knowledge, detailed lectures, and fun demos. Expect to learn concepts in lecture while most of the applicable material (solving strategies, etc) outside of class though textbook/videos. Tests push your understanding and problems sets are difficult but all interesting if you put in the time.

Very sweet person, gives decent lectures and assigns difficult (but enjoyable, interesting, and very well picked) homework problems. I spent around 4 hours a week on them. Midterms and final generally around the lower to middle end of the difficulty of homework problems. Will throw some shade at engineers from time to time. Good accent.

analysis.name: Kaya Oakes
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Genuinely felt like I was not at Berkeley. Easiest English course of my life-time. She does take attendance since she teaches a discussion-style english class however it's not necessarily graded. Lots of collaboration assignments with other students for essay feedback and such but it is so easy.

Great professor. She really cared about her students and had great resources available. There was a lot of readings in the beginning, as expected in R1A. English is not my strongest subject, but attending office hours really helped. Would recommend!

Had Prof. Oakes for Fall 2024 and even though the theme was not necessarily something I was interested in, she made the class super enjoyable. She is very flexible, supportive, and understanding! All her readings were accessible online too. She gave us precise feedback and the opportunity to revise previous essays. Go take her class!!

Prof. Oakes class was a blast! In her Cultural Critique course everything couldn't have been more clear and straight forward. We had two essays worth 40% and 50% of the course grade and discussions posts that were easy and engaging. She also provided extra credit that helped give reassurance we could get whatever grade we aimed for. She's great!

Incredibly sweet and understanding Prof! Kaya is the best and even though I wasn't very well versed in many topics, she provided helpful insights and expanded my perspective on many topics for the better. If you can take her, def do!

analysis.name: Ko Ohm
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 89 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: If you aren't religious, pick a religion and start praying. She draws hieroglyphics on her ipad and starts giggling to herself when no one understands a single thing she says. Paulin has always been the goat and always will be. If you love yourself do NOT take this class. I would rather switch majors than take this class again.

Ko Ohm isn't the best choice for math. She's very nice and caring but to be frank I wouldn't suggest her for math. Her lectures difficulty is very simple. Homework is difficult, and the exams are about 9x more difficult than homework. Her teaching style could improve. Try avoiding at all costs if you want to keep your GPA high.
I don't like the way she teaches the content. It often makes the material more confusing. The exams are much harder than she says they will be. I wish I had waited a semester and not taken her class.

Def a weeder class. Experience should be mandatory but even ppl w/ experience struggled a lot. I went to every lecture, did all HW, went to SLC a lot, but still bombed every quiz and test. They are SUPER lenient with grading, which I appreciate, but the last exams (final) were so hard that it barely mattered. U PM have to teach yourself everything.

She's tough. With that being said, the practice exams (for the midterms, esp #2) were almost identical to the actual midterms. Final was pretty heinous but each exam gets boundaries that are around 8-10% higher than the actual grade.Quizzes are fair and very similar to homework. Homework was heavy but def doable and you have a whole week to do it.

analysis.name: Ori Ganor
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Arguably one of the best physics professor I have ever taken class with. He was kind and caring and would extend homework deadlines during midterm and final weeks (which was a great help for my exam preparation and stress relief). Exams were hard (by nature) but he curved generously.

I have taken three courses with him so far and he is definitely my favorite professor of all time!! He is very enthusiastic and extremely friendly. I have kept in touch with him since the first course and he has great insights into lots of things. The course is typically challenging but will not kill you. Highly recommend to those who enjoy physics
His lectures could be confusing sometimes, but office hours are extremely helpful. He genuinely loves physics and is willing to help us learn.
A great professor who genuinely wants his students to learn. Office hours are excellent for clarification; be sure you go. All in all one of the best physics professors I've had.

Ori is absolutely wonderful! ALWAYS willing to help students and ALWAYS willing to go deeper into a topic during office hours. His HWs were short but challenging and his tests were fair. Overall, great prof. His only weakness is he focuses on certain mathematical topics/formalisms for too long which end up taking time away from later topics.

analysis.name: Saul Perlmutter
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Nice guy, but there's disconnect between him and course staff. There is barely any helpful communication from them and stuff isnt usually updated on time. Theres also impossible quizzes every week with trick questions.

Professor is good, but the class is not well run at all. Assuming you took science classes in HS, you don't learn much, and there was a bunch of messed up logistics. Lectures/discussions were WAY longer than they needed to be, and similarly there was a lot of work in this class (although all of it was not hard). No tech policy is just ridiculous.

Prof Perlmutter was very cool and clearly cared about the material. The class was run absolutely horribly (not the profs' fault) and I would not recommend anyone to take it, at least not as it is now- the discussions and plenary are painfully long and drawn out and the test questions are very confusing. but saul helped make it tolerable

Whatever everyone else said about an easy class, I feel like they took that personally and just made it difficult. The grading this year was bad, & there were not clear rubrics when it came to the projects. The final had so many questions that SO many were confused upon, as the guidelines for studying weren't accurate. I felt so duped w/ the class

Class was interesting and Saul was really passionate about teaching the material. As far as the grading, 35% of your grade is homework and participation, which you just need to complete/show up for. Then 20% was quizzes (there are six, all pretty easy, lowest two dropped). The rest is the final and two projects (all not hard with generous grading).

analysis.name: Brandi Pearce
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Bradni Pearce is great, she is very lively and brings alot of joy to each lecture. In this class, it's mostly group work, so hope and pray you get good teammates. The worst part of the class is the GSI, who is an MBA student who grades very harshly. The lectures do get a little long and boring at times, but overall, a great professor!

In UGBA 10X Brandi was a sweet prof, but out of the four professors in this class, her lecture was the least interesting to me. Of course this might be because I am least interested in her topic, but over all the lectures were boring. Also, mandatory attendance for this 8 AM class, which she makes you take selfies in class to prove you attended....

I really enjoyed UGBA 150 and Dr Pearce. She is really kind and you can tell she loves her job tremendously. I learned a lot in regard to leading teams and the class was worthwhile and a part of the UC Berkeley Changemaker certificate. At times the material can get a little slow and boring, but she picks it back up well.

Brandi seems sweet. Just her lectures were really tough to process at 8 am, especially as a freshman... She often got frustrated by the class's lack of engagement. 

I think her lectures were honestly the least engaging out of the four professors who taught the class

Her class was interesting even though it can get repetitive and boring, however the class was easy and I came out there learning more soft skills. Your grade all depends on your GSI, the prof doesn't grade anything and is only there to lecture and guide you through your group project. Honestly, very minimal work.

analysis.name: Matthew Potts
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This course is a little heavy on math and problem solving. The GSI's help alot. The professor is always willing to help and cares alot. The grading is really good too.
He keeps going on and on about how amazing AI is and it is pmo

Before Midterm you will be crunched with Lab assignments. You will learn excel and linear programming, after MT it gets much easier. Prof. Potts is very caring and flexible and super knowledgeable. GSI's help alot too.

Personally, I was really disappointed in this class. I felt Matthew was a pretty confusing lecturer. He would go back and forth on his definitions and the material for the class was so scattered. You learn something very different from what the weekly assignment would be and you depend so much on the GSI for help since they are the ones teaching...

Over 60 students in the class and roughly 90% of them were confused with what was going on. Classes were riddled with information that no one could understand, and there was constant confusion between the staff on how to do things in excel. This class is difficult because of how unorganized it was, and I highly recommend that you do NOT take it.

analysis.name: Oliver P John
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 69 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. John is a super nice guy and is great to talk to in office hours (definitely visit him there). The class wasn't a good fit for me though. We spent way too much time on the history of personality psych. It's an easy class and Dr. John is great, but I didn't walk out of there feeling like I learned a lot about contemporary research on personality

Prof. John was radiant and colorful. Genuinely kind & goofy. Reading is wordy, LONG, & dry. Course content  history of personality psych. vs real life application. 2 non cumulative tests but HEAVILY weighted. Web exercises & articles saved me. Articles take forever to do. Got our grades SUPER late. Offered extra credit  in the end. I say take it.

this class was disappointing - could have been really great and i was initially excited, but i don't think i really learned anything substantial from professor john's lectures. he's a very talented scholar and amazing researcher, but not the best professor in my opinion. he loves teaching but again, didn't learn anything. easy A though.
took this course over summer. 1/5 of the class got an a+. 1/3 a. 1/3 a-. easiest course i've taken at cal. memorize the slides the night before the exam.
Oliver P. John... Cool German dude with a great "personality" and hilarious yet effective teaching style :) Do take a class with him!

analysis.name: Zachary Pardos
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Class has no use in terms of material. Prof is often visibly unprepared for lectures, midterm was dysfunctional, staff didn't bother to use DataHub (assignments were links on bCourses to Google Colabs you had to manually save a copy of) and lab questions were unclear/poorly written. No finals yet they couldn't even submit CalCentral grades on time.

Completely online course with a clear weekly structure. The labs are due each week and are manageable, helping reinforce the material without taking too much time. Lectures are three hours per week and recorded. The instructor explains concepts clearly, and expectations for assignments are straightforward. Final is project-based rather than an exam

Class is honestly a mess. Haven't learned anything useful, lectures are boring, course staff is not unresponsive They took the entire semester to grade anything. Its been over two weeks since finals ended and they just released the grades, many of which were incorrect scorings with assignments still not put in. No communication efforts at all.

You take this class to get an A, not to learn anything. It's unfortunate this is an approved DS course. It makes sense, though, given how smug the prof is. But when you see his "research," you quickly realize he became one for producing endless slop. I encourage you to read his work, going back to 2010s

Grading was finished around a week before the last day of finals, and they are somehow still not released. He has no transparency or communication around grades. His lectures are just high level summaries that can be found if you ask ChatGPT what a neural network is. Easy class though, just only take it if you want an easy A.

analysis.name: Daniel Pirutinsky
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Wait I actually liked Prof Pirutinsky :( Sad to see all the negative reviews. The exams were extremely predictable thanks to the homework being well-structured, I feel I learned so much about ML and grew as a data scientist by taking this course. Great intro class and every concept felt applicable to the real world. Just be ready to review slides

Took IndEng 172...70% of your grade is final & midterm. Makes the GSI's write all homeworks and exams (90% of your grade) and lectures are barely correlated with any of the work done in the class. Fails 10-20% of his classes. Is extremely graphic about his personal life.

Extremely nice teacher, however the content is a bit dull, and his personality can't make up for it. The homework are about the same level of difficulty as the final, however the exams tend to bring up content not as heavily emphasized which frustrated me several times.

One of the worst professors I have had here at Berkeley. Randomly decided to change the structure of the midterms and finals midway through the course, making it harder just for "bringing the average grade down". Poor explanation of topics and just reads off the slides.

Not a traditional professor per se but caring nonetheless. Crazy backstory crazy lore. Super optimized life u could say. Had him for 120 and now 172 and it took me a while to warm up to him but once u get the vibe u vibe with him if u catch my vibe. Go to lecture and he is very open to helping u understand topics but he reads of slide for majority.

analysis.name: Aaron Parsons
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This prof is all kinds of bad - lecture is all over the place. Very inaccessible outside of class and sometimes do not come to office hours. Emails are usually ignored. The class is too much work for how many units it's worth, and it's even worse when the prof is just plain unhelpful. Will avoid this prof with a passion from now on.

His lectures are very boring and just a waste of time. He's not approachable and does not help you in office hours IF you get a chance to catch him at office hours because he did not show up multiple times. Basically you're on your own to learn everything. I do NOT recommend taking his class.

This is actually for ASTRON 128, I didn't find it in the Course Code list. Definitely recommend taking this course if you want to do research in the future, very similar to the actual research experience. Professor Parsons is an amazing instructor and really helpful during the office hours. He is one of the best professors I've ever had.

Professor Parsons is an amazing instructor who knows the material inside out. The course is demanding, as lab classes are, but the effort pays off. I gained more practical research experience here than in any other class. Even if radio astronomy isn't your main interest, the skills you develop in lab are incredibly valuable and broadly applicable.

Aaron is an incredible professor. He was very receptive to all our questions (and always down to chat), he cares about his students, and his explanations are uniquely intuition-forward/demo-oriented. Radio Lab gave me so much practical knowledge about research, moreso than any other class at Berkeley. It is a lot of work, but super fun!

analysis.name: Alexandra Pfiffner
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I really enjoyed having Professor Pfiffner! She timed her lectures perfectly, but the pace was a bit fast to take notes by hand. She is very kind and open to questions & conversations. The first half of the semester was definitely harder than the second. As long as you pay attention in lecture and find a good group for the projects, you're set.

Prof.Pfiffner is one of the best lecturers I've ever had at Berkeley. Many silly anecdotes, case-studies, & encouraging words. I'm no linguistics major but I found this class's overview to be SO interesting & applicable. And the GSIs are amazing (shoutout Franco and Madeleine!!). That said, be ready to memorize (e.g. MUSE IPA table) & learn a lot.

She is great! She is very caring and kind; hilarious and approachable even in lecture for questions! HWs can be pretty difficult but start early and you will be ok. Make sure to do well on the IPA quiz because I thought it was a tiny little thing and its worth 5% of our total grade, haha. She is great and her GSIs are amazing.

I came into this course with prior knowledge, so I only attended lecture maybe 4 times but the course content is very interesting and she does a very good job at teaching it! I do wish i couldve skipped the course but id highly recommend others take it.

I loved this class. Professor Pfiffner is incredible, she always has a great attitude. Lectures were accessible online, graded on one (very straightforward) homework per week, a midterm exam and project, and a final exam and project. Light + fun workload, if you're interested in languages you should definitely take this as a breadth! She's great!

analysis.name: Zi Qiang Qiu
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Zi Qiu was genuinely one of the better physics professors I've ever had. Lectures weren't mandatory, but I suggest going to them since he really enforces getting an intuition for the physics. The midterm and final were of reasonable difficulty, so if you understand the lectures and about 75% of the homework, you'll be fine.

Decent lecturer, went deep into deriving equations and explaining concepts, but rarely showed examples. Accent made it difficult to understand at times. Not the most helpful in OH, especially if you come to him with a personal problem. Homework questions taken directly out of textbook, solutions can be found easily. Tests are short, graded fairly.
Amazing lecturer would highly recommend! teaches concepts from the ground up, which makes it easy to learn and fully understand the material.

Qiu emphasizes physical reasoning above abstract and detailed mathematical calculation. He is great at extracting the physical meaning of formulas and building your intuition. However, this also means he passes over some interesting mathematics. The class is paced very slowly and the work is easy. He could have taught more topics pretty easily.

He's almost too easy; the homework could have been more challenging.  The only other flaw I can prescribe is he follows the book a little too closely.  But, it's a great book, he's a great lecturer and he'll even interject cool little anecdotes into his lectures occasionally.  I highly recommend taking a class from him!!!

analysis.name: Qing Zhou
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Zhou is great. The class was easy to follow along with-- hw assignments and exams were directly related to lecture content. Final paper isn't too bad either, as it gives you a lot of freedom to discuss what you'd like. Only one "group" project in section (presentation on a specific article or journal) and it's simple. I def recommend her :)

Overall super chill class. Dont need to go to lecture just review all of the notes before exams and you will be fine. Section attendance is mandatory. 50% of your grade is completion only assignments due at the end of the semester. Big research paper to write but can do it on any topic. Very easy way to satisfy clinical psych requirement.

She is so sweet, has very relevant material to the field of study that is updated as well. Homework and all assignments vary, very lenient on late homeworks but there is a group project in section. Midterm and Final was online and if you pay attention in lecture and write down what she says you can definitely pass with an A.

Prof. Zhou is amazing! She's very kind, has a deep passion for what she does, and obviously wants everyone to succeed :) The 3 exams are very straightforward, the majority of your grade is based on completion/participation, and the final project is pretty open-ended and has clearly outlined criteria. Loved her and loved PSYCH 131!
Very fair in grading and workload. I am not Psych major but still found the material digestible. Solid choice for clinical req.

analysis.name: Joseph De Quattro
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: took it in the first semester of my freshman year. The best class I have taken here at Berkeley. Much of the advice given helped me through tough times. Learned much more beyond knowledge to write. The most caring professor so far. Didn't think that this would best class experience so far. Just be present. a solid 6/5. Take it.
