I took this professor my first semester at Berkeley, I absolutely loved the way his discussions were set up. It's an easy class because he offers immense support all you have to do is pull your weight by participating in class and submitting essays. Additionally he allows you to resubmit essays for better grades.

He wants you to pass the portfolio evaluation, which is a hard pass or fail for all R1As. Surprised more don't talk about that here. Two weeks of missing class especially early on is grounds for drop, I think, especially if you didn't provide evidence. Covid or not, you can't make that time up on your own. Why bother with the course then? Great.

JDQ is an amazing R1A professor. As long as you participate in his classes (he cares a lot about showing up), hand homework on time, and show thinking in your essays, he is probably going to give you an A. Class gets really chill once you are used to JDQ's teaching style. Love him.

This is the worse professor to take if you get sick. I had him back during freshman year, got COVID, and after the two weeks in quarantine were over I tried to join class again and got banned from attending in-person classes and was removed from the canvas for no reason even though i did all of the homework while sick. I don't recommend.

analysis.name: Kevin Quintero
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Quintero creates such a wonderful learning environment! He effectively shares information while encouraging lots of questions and discussions. The atmosphere in class is incredibly friendly and welcoming—I've built closer connections here than in most of my previous classes. Plus, he presents information in so many fun and different ways.

Incredibly, unnecessarily rude. The first day of class, I came up to him afterwards and asked a very normal question (just if there were any writing resources posted for the class). He told me, word for word, "It's really *NOT* that hard, it's pretty straightforward. If you think you struggle then go to the writing center." Like?? What?? MEAN.

Weirdly off-putting and unhelpful towards his students, puts on a fake chill vibe but is completely mean behind closed doors. Don't take his class, you'll be draining your eyes from how much work he assigns. Doesn't actually know how to improve kids' writing, just has to prove something bc of his inexperience and his prejudices towards them.
Made class very engaging by having us do group discussions, group presentations, and peer feedback. Very smart professor knows how to deliver his class materials. Was my favorite class.

analysis.name: Amm Quamruzzaman
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Amm is a lovely human being. He is passionate about his discipline, and very kind/understanding towards students. He can be a little boring in lecture but ultimately all papers are (mostly) straight-forward and related to them. The final is also fair, as long as you review carefully and ensure a basic understanding of topics you're good

The content was interesting and engaging, but lectures could get long and somewhat confusing. Professor had very interesting things to say, but at times just lectured his opinion. The class had a few assignments throughout the semester and a large final (supposed to handwrite 10+ pages in 3 hours) worth 40% of the class grade.

Provided detailed lectures and had good GSI's to reinforce the learning. The final exam was five essays (hand written) with the rest of the grade coming from multiple papers and one essay throughout the semester. I would take this professor again but would suggest for him to make the final based on the computer.
love like a father or a mother

analysis.name: Qiang Zhou
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Friendly and funny professor.Yet AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS!His exam is long and insane.Some of his questions are taken from nowhere.His midterm was the hardest exam I've ever had in my life.And I studied for it from A to Z, non-stop.Don't take chances,and wait until another professor teaches this course.Zhou's exam is a killer

Professor Qiang Zhou was my favorite professor within the MCB 110 course. He was a real gem to take this course from and he was amazing at teaching us about one of the most difficult macromolecules to understand, RNA.

Dr. Zhou is one of my favorite professors! His extreme clarity in lecture is super helpful for a memorization heavy class. In his unit, it isn't necessary to read the textbook, but important to attend lecture to know what to expect on his midterm exam (BIG part of grade). I did have to set out lots of time to study all the details, but it paid off.

Loud and clear lectures! One of the few profs to use powerpoint as a good thing - we had his exact slides in a reader with lots of space for taking notes. Good at fielding questions and good pace. One bad thing was no homework, quizzes, or past exams to study - not much idea on what to expect on the midterm, which was the whole grade of his section

He is a very good lecturer, holds your attention through very complicated topics. Material is very experimental based. Same with his exams, experimental questions testing conceptual knowledge. Definitely one of my favorite professors at Cal. Take him if you have the chance, you'll learn a lot with him, without having to sacrifice grades.

analysis.name: Poema Q. Valente Meyer
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Poema is really nice. I took Portuguese 50 (the introductory Portuguese class at Berkeley) with her a few years back. So long as you memorize the verb conjugations (use Quizlet for that), you will do fine. The three compositions you have to write are graded more or less generously.

Poema is a wonderful teacher who genuinely cares about her students. She has a way of explaining the material that makes a lot of sense and helps out anyone who might have any doubts. There are a lot of little assignments, but if you stay on top of things you should do just fine.
Poema really cares about her students and was a great instructor; although beware that there are a lot of little assignments you have to be on top of and it's a lot of self-learning.

analysis.name: Eliot Quataert
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Amazing.  I have considered having his babies, but unfortunately, I am a man.

40% of the class grade is weekly HW, but it's graded super harshly. Even though it's supposed to be a non-majors class, he gets very technical and tackles some difficult concepts. The midterm was very difficult, and the class wasn't curved. The subject matter was very interesting though.

Amazing lecturer. Inspired me to go into Astrophysics. The class is very fair and well structured. Easily accessible. Very friendly and encouraging to students. The tests and homework are a bit hard but well worth it. Best professor I've ever had.

Professor Eliot is one of the most awesome professors I have ever encountered. He explains everything clearly in his lectures and is super accessible whenever a student has a question to ask him. I have been to his office hours and we talked about some interesting stuff! Definitely a good professor to reach out to and Astron C13 is a great class!!!

Professor Quataert is passionate and knows everything he is teaching inside and out. He is approachable and kind during office hours, always appreciating a good talk. He takes questions throughout the entire lecture, which is helpful. He speaks slowly sometimes though, so watching course captures on 2x speed is a lifesaver. Exams are all lecture.

analysis.name: Rhonda Righter
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I took her for 173, and would not recommend at all. Lecture is mandatory and she is SO hard to follow. She puts her notes on the board before class starts, and then starts lecturing unclearly. For the amount of effort I try to put into this class, it makes no sense, and then she gives long HWs which you have to teach yourself how to do.

Righter is a very good lecturer, so keep up with her notes and make sure you understand them! She's friendly and very helpful when you ask questions. IEOR 172 starts out pretty manageable but towards the end of the semester gets very tricky to grasp. Exams aren't too bad, pretty straightforward, but require you to think deeper on some questions.
Best professor I have ever met!

The work is very manageable, and she is super nice. Just talk to her outside of class! No ego, wants students to learn and succeed. Exams are very fair. While I am not the strongest student, I found probability very intuitive. She gives great examples. I wish I could have taken more classes with her...

While Professor Righter's lectures can be a little chaotic sometimes, she is the most caring professor I've had (she even introduces little games to keep students involved). She is a little old-school, but she makes sure every question is addressed and the course material is quite easy.

analysis.name: Robert Sharf
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 54 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I took this class for my philosophy breadth. Mr. Sharf is passionate and knowledgable about the subject, and the lectures were engaging and interesting. Most of your grade is reliant on one-page essay assignments on the readings due every Monday. The midterm study guide matched the midterm. I'd recommend this class!

Professor Sharf is great, but know this first: lecture and discussion are mandatory, with no slides or recordings. Laptop use is limited to note-taking and only allowed in the first three rows. There's a quiz every week which can be stressful. Grades may feel low, but extra credit later helps. If you put in the work, the course is transformative!
Very Western theoretical.  Not too different from a Cultural Studies theory class, my major.

Sharf is a good professor. course was interesting and despite never having learned this I found myself considering to minor in it. However, the workload was a lot. Readings every day, quizzes every week, and midterms and finals were basically straight essay writing. He asks niche questions on the exams that I did not realize were important to learn

honestly nothing against Professor Sharf the class was just a lot more work than I originally expected. definitely what tanked my grade was my GSI who graded like I personally murdered their family and spent most of our discussions talking about their own research instead of helping us

analysis.name: Raluca Scarlat
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Going to lectures made the material more confusing, riddled with errors in derivation and wasted most time micromanaging attendance/seating charts than teaching. Homework long, repetitive and unrelated, forced to do it in randomly assigned, incompatible groups of students. Overall disrespect of our time and effort, constantly moving goalposts 🐬 🌻

Scarlat is very kind and clearly into the material, but the class is so poorly organized that it is next to impossible to get a good grade. I got one of the top 5 scores on one of the midterms, and above average scores on the others, but failing avgs+no curves meant everyones grade was entirely determined by her impossible tests.

Pretty strange class. We had a seating chart so we would all sit in the front of the room, and there was a mountain of assigned readings each week. No exams, all projects. A lot of your work will come from your discussion sections, so kind of a gamble with the GSI you get. I will also say that the Canvas page was a MESS the entire semester.

Very disorganized and did not use time well. Has 4 different grading schemes to try and maximize our grades instead of curving, but just adds confusion. Had 3 exams all with failing avgs. Gave us 30 "practice" problems for a final that had nothing to do with the final, and final wasn't cumulative, basically a 4th exam

Class is super disorganized and emphasizes proofs in lecture vs. problems on tests. Homework is long, diabolically complicated and not helpful for exams. THERE IS NO CURVE! This is the only class I've ever had to read the textbook front to back. Prof is very kind and passionate, just can't run a class well.

analysis.name: Thomas Schutzius
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Thermodynamics is intimidating. It is quite a lot of material to cover. But Prof. Schutzius takes a very sensible approach to this subject: as long as you keep up with textbook and office hours for example, you will do very well in the course. The course is also structured so that you have many opportunities to catch up. It's fast but a ton of fun!

One of the best professors I've had at UC Berkeley. Lectures are engaging and strike a great balance between foundational practice problems and additional context. The grading policy is very fair, scoring above 90% on a midterm problem allows you to skip the corresponding section on the final. Lectures are also recorded and posted online.

Schutzius is passionate about thermo, but his lectures don't cover the material. You need to learn the material on your own by reading the textbook and/or watching online videos, and then if you go to class, it's just to see him do some long practice problems. Midterms were fairly difficult but fair. The final was exceptionally difficult.

The class was taught with passion but lectures were hard to understand without reading the textbook first. He was doing mostly long practice problems in class and often losses people during the question. Homework was flexible but tests, especially the final, was really hard and also not very related to homework and lecture.

Schutzius is a passionate professor who is great at answering questions. Lectures are mainly practice problems so most actual learning of the concept has to be done by the student reading the textbook outside of class. Tests are difficult and include problems not found in the textbook, so a true mastery of the material is required.

analysis.name: Cihan Tugal
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Poorly organized lecture with boring and tedious style. The load of obscure readings would crash your aspiration. In short, hardly learn anything for the whole semester.

This was a way harder class than I had expected (and we're not even halfway through yet!). I wouldn't recommend taking this class with Professor Tugal if you don't have a lot of prior knowledge on historical social revolutions. Heavy readings and lectures, but not necessarily all helpful or substantive at time. Considering taking it p/np.

Class was structured very poorly at first. Did not have a good sense of the theorists until the first midterm. He changed it up and I did learn a lot - mostly because of a good GSI. Your writing will get fine-tuned, readings are long and hard often, and lecture is confusing. Getting a B+ or A- isn't too bad but a solid A is real work

This class was much harder than it should've been because of a lot of disorganization. Concepts were never fully explained or clarified and I even found a lot of disconnect between lectures and the readings because he taught off the assumption that we already knew material from other classes.

Professor Tugal's biggest strengths as an instructor are that he is incredibly passionate about the content of the material he teaches and he respects his students' interests and curiosity. His lectures are incredibly engaging, and he encourages critical engagement of the texts and never disregards a student or their opinions. Take his classes.

analysis.name: Satish Rao
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 124 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Rao is SO CONFUSING in lecture!! He is all over the place and never coherently finishes any of his sentences when he talks. He just is just way too hard to follow. Concepts like these need clear instruction from the teacher!!

This is a difficult course and Rao is not a good professor to teach it. He's scattered in his lectures, goes way too fast through the slides, and he assumes that you know various math concepts before starting the course. If you're comfortable with solving math proofs, you'll do well in this class. If not, take it with another professor if you can.

A scatter-brained lecturer. He is smart but he seems to have a difficult time conveying his thought process and concepts to the class. He will jump around a lot during his math proofs. He will skip steps, goes too fast during critical proofs, or mentally compute/assume things without explaining to us. Class structure is very disorganized, chaotic.

Rao is a poor lecturer - he can't seem to clearly explain things. He trails off easily and is extremely hard to follow in the first place. Basically, he is all over the place during his proofs and explanations, sometimes skipping essential details altogether. For a class that is so theory-heavy, it sucks a lot to have such a bad instructor.

Good attitude, but painfully awkward jokes and awful at teaching. It's obvious that Rao gives lecture on the fly by literally reading every word off of the slides and getting lost during his own lectures. Teaching is his last priority, so if you take it with Rao don't even go to lecture and just read Sinho/Alvin's notes.

analysis.name: Chen-Hui Tsai
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Not only did I learn so much Chinese from her that surprisingly stuck with me years later, but I also learned so much that I found helped me in my future teaching career. Super engaging and has a way of making everything stick in your memory. One of my best professors.

She is the best professor I've had here. I've never once been bored in her class. She is an incredibly effective lecturer. On a daily basis, she takes our group of tired, jaded students, and immediately engages us. She's one of those rare people who can fill a room with positive energy, just by speaking. I wish more professors could be like her.

Tsai Lao Shi is one of the best Chinese teachers I've had. She's extremely passionate about teaching and it shows every day with her enthusiastic energy. There's a fair amount of work that has to be put in her class, but if you put in the effort, she has no problem helping.

Tsai Lao Shi is the best teacher I've ever had in my life. Very passionate, very helpful. Never had a bad day with Tsai laoshi. Awesome! Wish I could have more classes with this amazing teacher. Xie xie ni Tsai laoshi.
Tsai Laoshi was a very intense teacher, and we really flew through the course, but I felt progress nearly every day.  She was well respected and is extremely approachable about anything at all.

analysis.name: ChengXi Tang
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: His lectures were super engaging and organized, and I felt like they really improved my understanding of the course material. I don't really get why the other reviews are saying he's disorganized when it felt like the exact opposite in this class. I will say he sometimes uses complicated wording, but it didn't personally impact my understanding.

I took HUM 10 not German39P!
He is very enthusiastic when he lectures. He has a heavy accent which kind of makes it hard to understand him. The material was very interesting. He also assigned for the discussions to do a student showcase at the end, where we all put all three modules together into one creative piece. It was fun not gonna lie.

The professor is very unorganized. I think it's an easy class, but it is so easy to dissociate. You write a couple of essays throughout the semester, but he isn't clear on what he wants you to write or the basic instructions. You can survive, but its wasn't a hard class, but not a fun one either. And he goes on random tangents.
Quite disorganized but an easy grader. Only takes attendance when he remembers to, which is rare

I acknowledge this is largely out of his control, but I found his accent made lectures somewhat difficult to understand. Plus, his grading criteria and attendance policy is unclear (we don't know our attendance score ever!), in addition to the GSI's for the course being ok. tbh the subject matter is good but there are better R1B's out there

analysis.name: Doris Tsao
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This is for Neu 100B. The lectures go all over the place. The slides are complex, and she goes off on tangents. Information overload constantly, and there is never any indication of what specific things we should study, she just assumes we will absorb her slides in their entirety. Easily the worst experience I've ever had learning neuroscience.
her lectures are disorganized and she has trouble explaining difficult concepts clearly. lots of tagents and information that does not help the student and only further confuses them

Shows up late a lot, disorganized, doesn't articulate very well, and loves using very abstract odd-angle fMRI diagrams then talking about these blobs for 10 minutes while 100 students gaze on uncomprehending. I wish somebody else, anyone else, was teaching this unit.
The basis for much of what we were learning was not provided. A lot of photos on the slides and not nearly enough text, making it difficult to go back and study at times unless you write down a lot.

Bad professor and uncaring person. Lectures didn't cover majority of exam material and explanations of topics she should have been highly knowledgable in lacked all necessary details. Has no compassion for students that are ill and doesn't respond to student concerns over email or on discussion boards in a timely manner.

analysis.name: Edward Tyerman
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Amazing professor who cares about what he is teaching, he will go on tangents at times but it adds to the class and makes it better lowkey.

Brilliant man! So caring and passionate. Often went on tangents, but they were fascinating and thrilling. Much more of a seminar than a lecture-heavy class, encourages participation. Really interesting reading list. Two papers, take home midterm and final. Spends lots of time grading but gives incredibly thorough feedback. Highly highly recommend!

This was by far my favorite class at UC Berkeley. We covered some authors that I would have never read if it wasn't in this course. Edward encourages everyone to participate (more a seminar than a lecture) and always gives brilliant feedback. The movies/books/ songs/secondary readings are really interesting; I was amazed by the sources chosen!

This was one of m favorite classes I've taken so far. The class relied heavy on participation. He always made every comment feel like it brought something to the conversation. He often would go on tangents, but it was filled with important information and other context relating to the readings. He was a great professor and highly recommend!

analysis.name: Ussama Makdisi
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Very mixed about this professor. On the one hand, very well spoken and gives a lot of good insight on the topic if you have never been educated on it. On the other, lectures can fluctuate wildly from absolutely necessary to attend or a complete waste of time. Quizes were easy, just be prepared to talk about the same thing over and over again.

Makdisi is THE GOAT!!! In a class dealing with such sensitive subject matter, he never failed to offer an open space where students can freely share their ideas and let us come to conclusions ourselves. While the class is long-reading heavy, the important sections are covered in discussion so u should be chilling. Everyone should take this class!!

I do think sometimes the lectures were very repetitive and concepts were overused. At least for history 12 (admittedly lower division), he taught how to study history, especially in the Middle East. I think non-history majors might get more out of his class.

He has passion but I didn't feel like I got much out of his lectures (he has a very soft voice that put me to sleep at times). Cares about his students and grading was not bad. Shout out to the GSIs, learned the most through weekly section.

Makdisi is an incredible historian and I'm grateful to have taken "Palestine and the Palestinians: A Modern History" with him. He assigns engaging readings and is a captivating lecturer. There was a LOT of history to pack in this semester-long class, but Makdisi synthesized immense amounts of information in an understandable format. TAKE THIS CLASS

analysis.name: Ugo Nwokeji
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: No instructions on format for midterms until the night before. Randomly gives you language to memorize on tuesday, test on thursday, then its never spoken of again. Grading is unclear and confusing. No instructions given to gsi's so they never can answer a single question. Classes always start late or are cancelled but godforbid you don't show up

This review is for AFRAM 118. I respectfully believe it is time for Dr. Ugo to retire or pivot in his career. He is not tech savvy, so when his lecture slides supposedly did not work at the onset of the semester, he just gave up. Thus, resulting in a highly ineffective lecture style. He is precariously late with grading and poor at giving feedback.

I do not recommend this class at all!!! the GSI never knew what was going on in that class either. Random quizzes. only mentioned about quiz once and never said what to study for!! mind you he mentioned this quiz a day before it was due!!! no format for midterm or final!!  our essays and finals never got graded and they passed the students!!!

This professor is a mess. We had a map quiz when he never taught geography, we had to memorize words in IGBO for a language quiz worth 5% of our grade, our paper and final were never graded so they never went into the gradebook and the GSIs never knew what was going on in the class. This was a horrible class. Dont recommend it.

He is very endearing.  Cares about students.  HOWEVER, he lacks professionalism.  Some lectures, he did not show up (unexpectedly) or he had seminars to attend instead.  Other times, he could not figure out how to put on powerpoint so we would start 40 minutes into the 90 minute lecture.  Didn't learn too much, but I did learn.  Very light load.

analysis.name: Ken Ueno
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Ken Ueno's class is mostly about him. He once spent 30 minutes on a Facebook argument, assigns readings about himself, and reuses his comp class's material. Uses AI art but calls it his own. No focus on notation, just avant-garde noise. Praise him or make bad music for an easy A. Another prof told me the content he teaches is "useless in practice"

I have no idea why Professor Ken will get a 2/5 here. He's an amazing composer and professor, changing the way I look at the world in a more comprehensive, lenient, and poetic way. He's class is all about his student, I don't know where else will give the opportunity to student to work with 5 world-class musicians and write for them in a semester.

Took his analysis class, felt like absolutely no planning at all, every class he just talks about whatever he's in the mood to talk about. Assignments and quizzes were sporadically given, and the grading felt pretty arbitrary too. He is clearly very knowledgable, but due to his lack of organization for this class, I learned very little from it.

He digresses a lot in class and the entire class feels sort of monotonic and gloomy. He is not the worst kind of teacher you can have, I feel like he is pretty polite, but still can make you a little bit uncomfortable. He focuses on avant-garde kind of music so if that is not your type I would suggest you to go find someone else.

Prof Ken is interesting and knows a lot. However, he's a poor teacher and honestly not sure why he's allowed to teach w/o changing. He just talks randomly without bringing the class along for the ride. He didnt care much. The guest lecturers can be really cool and neat. Also the project compostions are very avant garde.

analysis.name: Hendrik Utzat
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Organized and well-articulated lectures. Able to present the same concept in many different ways. Impeccable lecture notes (color-coded to emphasize important concepts). Kind and accessible during office hours. Problem sets are challenging but doable if you first try to understand the lectures. Very responsive to feedback.
Just a mess. He's nice but he manages to make simple concepts so convoluted. Lectures are all over the place. The hw is really not that bad but I literally hate how he explains things

analysis.name: Gaston Sanchez Trujillo
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 64 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: It's just weird... He looks very nice in person except being a boring lecturer. However, his policy and curve are ridiculous. I can't relate the evil policy and grading with a person who seems to be pretty nice.......

He is not a good option for this class. Although its 3 units and the assignments do not seem like much work, the grading is vague and inconsistent, costing many points. He also blames any trouble on the students even when its clearly staff fault. I had near 100 in assignments but still got a mediocre grade because of his class is structured.
Very unclear with his rubrics and gives boring assignments. His quizzes focus on  R/RMD syntax rather than actual programming or data processing. Oh, and he also doesn't curve.
Literally the worst professor I have ever had. Absolutely useless lectures and a horrible grading scale. He is one of the few people I actively dislike

Mandatory lectures that are utterly useless. If attendance wasn't mandatory, you could get by without ever attending lecture or doing any reading. Assignments are easy, but points are docked for trivial mistakes even if it's obvious that you understand the content being taught. The class isn't very useful or meaningful, but Sanchez makes it worse

analysis.name: Elcin Unal
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She was a good lecturer and is consistent with her OH. I liked that she gave us extra practice questions to study. Her exam questions are super hard tho so watch out! She didn't give us much info about what we should expect on the exams, and she puts a lot of easter egg details on the questions which if you don't notice, you may as well get a 0.

Clear, enthusiastic lecturer. Definitely cares about her teaching quality. Posts amazing, almost word-for-word lecture notes that explain all concepts well, and could substitute for any textbook you'd need. Her midterm was moderately tricky and harshly graded, though, so don't underestimate it on the basis of the quizzes (both "big" and "mini".)

Elcin is an AMAZING professor, one of the best. Everyone loves her and we wish she could teach the entire class! Lectures are very well planned out and the logical flow is on point. She is great at explaining and laying everything out in a simple explanation. Also gives lecture notes and outside resources/practice. Would highly recommend.

The best of the three, although her concepts are also the easiest, review of Mendelian genetics from bio1a. Lectures are very clear and organized, she uses the chalkboard unlike most MCB profs. Exams are similar to practice problems and past exams, but still require thinking. Highly recommend.

One of my favorite professors at Berkeley! Amazing lectures with clear chalk work, she also has very detailed lecture notes uploaded for reference. Very willing to help students both after class and during office hours. 10/10 recommend.

analysis.name: Umair Khan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This is the ONE class you need to take before you leave UC Berkeley. It is life-changing and so inspirational. Professor Umair Khan is a one-of-a-kind professor who genuinely cares about teaching and inspiring students. He's funny, inspiring, and cares. It's so amazing to walk into class each week and hear from such amazing people. A MUST TAKE!!

I would leave Umair's class every Wed buzzing. Getting to hear from the founders of companies that I grew up with (GuitarHero, Rotten Tomatoes, Khan Academy, etc). was one of the best experiences I could have had. It showed me starting a company was actually possible, and gave me to playbook to actually go and and start my own company. Take it!!

Do not take this class if you are an creative in any way. The class says it's for everyone, but is so heavily pro-AI to the point where AI generated prompts will beat out all the creative ideas. There are many students who can't do anything but chatGPT. Other than learning about VC terms, this class does not teach you how to actually run a business

Hum 120 is by far the best class I've taken at Cal. Highly recommend it to anyone interested in entrepreneurship. This class builds a solid foundation for anyone interested in building a company. Plus the network Professor Huang and Khan brings to class is truly unique.
This class helped me grow and learn alot of things professor Umair has been supportive throughout. I wish I could take another class with him

analysis.name: Aleksandra Utiralova
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Great professor. The notes she provided were very helpful and made understanding the material much easier. Always happy to answer questions. The lecture pacing was a bit fast so I did have to go and reread the textbook/notes quite a bit. Practice exams are literally just like the real thing. However, the HW is hard and worth a lot of your grade.

She posts her lecture notes online, which I thought were far better than the actual textbook itself. In fact, I pretty much used them as a substitute for the lectures itself (which I could not attend due to a time conflict). Homeworks are tough and exams are fair. Would definitely take another class with Prof. Utiralova in the future.

I learned so much from this class. Utiralova has her lecture notes freely available so you can read ahead and she records her lectures. Homework gives you enough practice to understand concepts but also throws in some tough questions - good balance. Exams are extremely fair, and mirror the practice exams fairly. I would definitely recommend!
the homework was HARD and time consuming but I have a lot of respect for her, she is very nice and smart, after all she went to MIT
Great Professor, her exams are similar to mock

analysis.name: Uros Seljak
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Lectures hardly related topics to their applications in the homework, and his homeworks either held your hand so much that you effectively just translated an equation into python, or gave you no instruction. Assignments seemed rushed or reused (404 not found errors, incorrect versions in provided code...). Slides were rushed and crowded. Don't.

I wanna give 0 if I could. Basicslly speaking, most flip classes trail would fail and the Physics 188 is a good place to improve your ability to teach yourself. The most time, you would learn nothing from class. And you cannot get too much beneficail help. The professor and TAs don't seem like to teach. Go to CS189, that is a good contrast.

Uros seems like a decent guy but simply cant teach. 188 is a primarily ML application based class but he tried teaching the theory with poorly made slides. Our GSI, byeonghee, was absolutely terrible too and made the homework harder from last year. We were expected to use ML libraries without being taught and with no prior exposure.

Professor Seljak was a moderately clear lecturer, and wrote interesting homeworks and exams. However, the homeworks did not adequately prepare one for the exams, which were some of the hardest I've taken at Berkeley. The grading was very harsh on minor algebra mistakes, etc. as well.

He writes interesting homework and tries to help you but nothing he does in class or on the HW's will prepare you for his tests. I know most of the people in the class and most of us learned close to nothing.

analysis.name: Valerie Zhang
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I showed up to class a total of 4 times (2 being for the midterm and final) and just used the ugba 102 goated website and did completely fine. Professor seems very chill and so did the (two) lectures I went to. She also provides very useful practice exams.

Goated professor. Clear lecture slides that teach you everything you need to know for exams. Exams are MC, and are similar to practice exams she provides. Homework is useful and solutions are posted to help you learn the material. Final group project is a trading simulation game based on reading financial statements. Easy A as long as you study.

I hated this class, she did an awful job at helping kids who didn't get it on the first try. Final ended up being completely different than what anyone was expecting. Instead of making jokes in class, she could've spent more time making sure the content was clear. Also, made it hard for me to get accommodations when I had a family emergency.

Valerie is fantastic . She is excited about the topic and is unintentionally funny. Her lectures are content heavy but she tries to make them as manageable as possible. She is also fairly accessible outside of class and was very understanding about the difficulty of the course and of being a student. She genuinely wants everyone to do well.

Accounting itself is boring, but Valerie tries to make it at least a bit enjoyable. She is unironically funny while providing a decent overview of each topic. The reason she is receiving a low mark is because her teaching is not effective during lecture. Be ready to teach yourself most of the content as your grade is dependent on exams.

analysis.name: Alex Von Rospatt
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Course was interesting and was a good introduction to sasian studies. But his lectures were only supplemental to the readings so I learned most at home and discussion. He knows a lot but he also has a thick accent and didn't really do anything for the course. saving grace was GSI (my goat Tanner McAlister). Assignments were fair, weekly 1pg essays.

Professor was somewhat interesting, but like someone else said, midway through became very tangential and was uninteresting coming to class. Had a habit of calling people out throughout class; first week he would make a big scene of people who came to class late. As the semester went on, would just make sly comments to single people out.

First half of course was very interesting, but once we reached the section on nepal lectures became full of tangents and were overall uninteresting. Professor is fair, but attendance is mandatory and will randomly quiz students in class. Makes fun of students for getting problems wrong and for coming in late.

Idk why people are lying on here lol his content is interesting but he is insaneee. He doesn't know personal space and gets off on embarrassing you. Yes, I get pushing your students but sometimes its so unnecessary and takes away from our learning. He's funny at times and seems like a good guy personally but very strict and disrespectful honestly.

Rospatt drones on and on during lecture and technology isn't allowed so be prepared to be bored as hell. Grade cutoffs are also super harsh, but I will say that he's pretty generous with late work submissions (probably because he doesn't grade them, the GSI does).

analysis.name: Fyodor Urnov
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 141 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Urnov is my fav professor at Berkeley. i would've loved 2 be taught by him earlier in my undergrad. he's such a sweetheart+mad inspirational. always related course content to the Real World, the past and future. encouraged ALL questions in lec. only thing is he's hard 2 reach out of class (does NOT answer emails rip). genome editing king, 1 mil/10.

Dr. Urvov was by far and away my favourite professor I've had (and I'm a senior!). His section has material that is so new there is no textbook for it. Fyodor is very intentional— he wants students to pay attention and makes lectures unbelievably interesting, letting his humour and passion for the subject come through. Take any class he teaches.

Hilarious professor who will emphasize a) why the material you are learning was important to the past and b) to the future. He keeps the class exciting by updating it with current and relevant research papers. Pretty lively and passionate guy

He's Sarcastic, Bitter, has his 12 old daughter teach a class on the Jonas Brothers, lies about his office hours, loves politics, cancels review sessions, refers all difficult biochem questions to the GSIs, NEVER responds to emails, has little to NO knowledge of biochem, very arrogant, mocks students who care about grades, that about sums it up.GL!

Most inspirational bio 1a prof.  People didn't like the question phrasing on his tests, but that's probably because they didn't study enough.  Honestly, the tests were very very easy if you study the lecture slides. Would definitely recommend.

analysis.name: Sarah Vaughn
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Her classes were my favorite at Berkeley. The readings can be dense but super interesting, and her lecture portion can go by fast so be sure to stay engaged. Go to her office hours, she is very helpful one on one! She is brilliant and a great resource if you are interested in this area of study.

Professor Vaughn is a really excellent lecturer and very approachable. She's extremely knowledgeable and explains complicated theory stuff clearly. There's a lot of (interesting) reading and you must participate in discussions online/in class. She will occasionally single people out in class to get them to participate (but not in a mean way).

Take this class if you actually want to learn! It's not the easiest but she's approachable and wants you to succeed! One of the best classes at Berkeley. Just do the reading and it will come together.

Really great lecturer. Explains things using common examples to help students understand. The advanced topic for this class was on the anthropocene, she switched off with prof. collier from time to time. Class was relatively easy, just two papers. Reading was unnecessary really, but interesting.

analysis.name: Daniel Viehoff
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Great professor. He truly enjoys the material he teaches and provides excellent feedback on student contributions in class. He truly wants people to participate and succeed in this class. Grades are based on lecture and section participation, as well as weekly questions, a midterm, and a final. Truly not hard to succeed in this class just be curiou

Professor Viehoff is a great lecturer and his course is designed to learn the material. Only homework is reading, and he assigns a very reasonable amount. There were two midterms and a final, but no essays. This course was well taught, and very interesting! Participation matters - comprised of section and emailing reading questions throughout sem.

He's a great lecturer and the class is beneficial, especially for those interested in law and politics. As a lot of philosophy classes are, it was kind of boring at times. The lectures are repetitive, which I liked because you could kind of go to every other lecture. Easy A.

Professor Viehoff chose some exceptional readings for the class. All of them were super interesting, if not sometimes dry. The lectures tend to cover the papers assigned pretty well anyway. The midterm and final were more about arguing your view and supporting it rather than just reciting papers. This class made me question my views and I loved it!
