Expect a survey of architecture & planning ideas through history.
Great course! Grading criteria for assignments was pretty specific, reading assignments were interesting. Lectures were mandatory through iClicker attendance.

I took CP110 with Yanin over Zoom and over the summer; I think they are a good lecturer and a very supportive educator, although it was hard to stay engaged online. Large assignments were graded fairly leniently, although quizzes were a little bit harder. Readings weren't excessive and Yanin does a good job supporting in class participation.

Yanin is a great instructor who makes everyone feel comfortable and has a great energy during lectures. The class consists of 10 weekly reading reflections and 3 larger assignments on a planning problem of your choice. Overall a straightforward and not too challenging class as long as you attend lecture and put effort into your assignments.

analysis.name: Yuriy Gorodnichenko
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
90% of the grade came from exams. If you missed/skipped any of the midterms, that weight would be shifted to the final exam.

Really difficult course, and there weren't many resources outside of (rather boring and monotonous) lectures; the same could be said for section.

Don't be like me and skip the midterms. You will fail, as I did.

Really good lectures, spends lots of time connecting class concepts to recent and/or fundamental research in economics. Homework isn't so bad, and exams were EXACTLY like homework and the practice exams given. I think he copy-pasted a question verbatim into our final from the practice. If you just show up to class and do the work, it will be fine.

caring guy and did learn some. Lectures were monotone and he does not record them Did not find discussion to helpful AT ALL led to a lot of self learning and stress. Little hw but was EXTREMELY stressful not to have any practice material and the class felt poorly structured in this manner. Bad curve, and don't know final grade till end
great professor. super knowledgeable and lots of great content in class. not that hard tho

Really inspiring guy who is clearly an expert in his field, but this unfortunately did not translate into effective teaching. Not enough resources to succeed in the class -- lectures were rather monotonous and only one practice exam was provided ahead of each exam.

analysis.name: Yuriko Miyamoto-Caltabiano
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Very nice teacher, I was able to keep up relatively well, although there definitely was a lot of coursework (it's a language course after all). Do your homework though since I did well on all the tests but I kept forgetting to turn in the homework on time so she lowered my grade :P… grades are non-negotiable so keep that in mind.

miyamoto sensei is such a nice person. i am just not cut out for the japanese language i fear.

beware of forgetting assignments, there are a LOT.

Miyamoto sensei is the definition of caring. She is supportive of students, remembers who comes to class, and is always giving good feedback (esp for the semester paper). Class is super heavy on participation, even moreso than J1A, but Miyamoto sensei makes the activities really fun.
I had a great time in class everyday with her.

She is very caring of her student's success and leaves useful feedback on homework. She incorporates fun aspects into her class that makes learning Japanese more interesting. She is really friendly and low-pressure in making mistakes. She asks leading questions that allow you to get to the correct answer which I think is really helpful.

Loved this class! Miyamoto-sensei is very understanding and patient which is very helpful when learning a challenging language. Also very accessible outside of class and there are many opportunities to improve your skill outside of the tests/quizzes. Class was fun every day and never felt boring. 100% recommend.

analysis.name: Stephanie Zonszein
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I took her 138Z class. Its hard to follow along with lectures only if you dont do the readings. If you do the readings and actually learn the concepts she teaches the class should be relatively easy. Had never actually coded before this class, but the R coding was relatively easy if you follow along is discussion. Would def take again

PS138Z: Great class overall. Professor Zonszein is very knowledgeable and caring. I learned a lot from both lecture and section. Her slides are actually super super helpful. The R coding assignment was manageable thanks to the GSI, who was also extremely knowledgeable and came to section always very prepared. Would definitely recommend this class!

138Z: Prof Zonszein is one of the kindest professors I have taken at Cal. Yes, the R coding part was annoying, but she is there to help you as well as the GSI (who was also amazing). Class consists of two short assignments, midterm and a final. I am not a good test taker but the test is designed to help you genuinely do well in the class. Take her!

An informative course that covers a wide range of Latino history in the U.S. The readings are substantial but not overwhelming. The R project is generally manageable, though it may be challenging for students without prior experience in basic programming. Overall, I would recommend this course

Professor Zonszein is an expert in her field. I think she's still new, by professor standards, to teaching and is feeling out how to make lectures more engaging. She can get flustered and easily distracted by student's arriving late or leaving early, but is also a very competent, knowledgeable, and easy going. I highly recommend this class

analysis.name: Zachary Johnson
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is amazing, super nice, has useful office hours, and picks some of the most interesting book content I've received from a class. There's a 1% extra credit towards the end of the class for attending a movie. The only downside was it was very clear a lot of students used AI for their two 1-page writing requirements that had to be shared in class.
He made me like writing again and cares about everyone's thoughts without bias. The books were also very interesting

His class gives me the best learning experience so far at cal. He genuinely cares about students and is accessible outside the classroom. His lectures are great cuz beyond just teaching literature stuff, they are more about inspiring my own thoughts and opinions. His class also has super comfortable environment for discussion.

I love this class and Professor Johnson is truly such an amazing person. He actually cares about helping his students learn and grow, rather than just going through the motions of teaching like some of my other professors. You can tell he is super passionate about teaching and genuinely wants his students to succeed.

Best professor at Berkeley. Inspired me to become a Russian Lit minor-- that's how good his class was. such an understanding, kind, and friendly professor. I was struggling with personal stuff last semester but I would get up to go to his class. lectures were always super fun and I learned so much, not just about Anna Karenina but myself. 1000/10.

analysis.name: Zehlia Babaci-Wilhite
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr Babaci-Wilhite led the graduate seminar and assigned a variety of scholarly articles or book chapters that we could download using bCourses. Students had the chance to present their own research and improve their presentations due to her excellent feedback. The best part about the readings were that they were all RECENT research-based findings.

This professor makes interdisciplinary course material useful and discussions enlightening for student learning. She welcomes a diversity of perspectives and encourages everyone to think critically and reflectively about complex, relevant issues. She is genuinely responsive to individual needs and shared interests. An objective, supportive mentor.

This was a wonderful, dynamic course, with just the right balance of lecture, seminar discussion, and student led content. Prof. was always well prepared, full of enthusiasm and great energy, provided access to all the literature, lead great discussions giving real life examples of theory, and was always available for further discussion and help.

The professor was a helpful mediator in the course discussions. As a graduate-level course, I deeply treasured the interdisciplinary perspectives she brought in, which effectively widened our understanding of related fields, as well as context-specific knowledge. The course was also flexibly organized, as participation was welcome at any points.

I had a headache sitting in this class and listening to the prof brag about parts of her life irrelevant to the course. She got aggressively defensive when we asked her questions about her unclear syllabus and assignments. It's easy to ace this class, but you'll leave each day knowing more about her ability to speak French than any applied language

analysis.name: Darren Zook
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 247 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Its scary how different Darren is when you interact with him one on one versus how he portrays himself to be in lecture. In lecture, its all corny jokes and smiles. But one on one, hes awkward, cold, short, and unencouraging. Seeing through the facade made his lectures feel really inauthentic and uncomfortable.

Honestly an easy class, but I'm going to go against the grain a little bit here and say I'm not the biggest fan of Zook's lecturing style. The PS 149 lectures were very much a "pop culture" style of lecturing about each area, with constant cliches mentioned regarding celebrities, music, and VERY oversimplified discussions over political science.

While Professor Zook is a hilarious and inspiring teacher, the methods in which he and his GSI's grade is not consistent with what's portrayed in class. He spends much of his class re-assuring students that if they follow directions they'll get good marks. However, after spending over 24 hours on my paper, I received a B- on said paper.

Zook is the pop music of UC Berkeley lecturers. Though engaging, his class is extremely easy. This may be great for those taking a breath class, or people who prefer to spend college partying on Wednesday nights, but for a person serious about Global Studies, not so much. At times, Zook seemed more worried about amusing his students than teaching.

149E in Hearst Field Annex was hellacious. Pouring sweat listening to a lecture that should take 45 min. not 90. Power points are not available and consist of lazy bullet points that help the lecturer more so than the student. Gsi's were unwelcoming, adversarial, and had a negative vibe. Grading is based off of a vague rubric. Overrated...

analysis.name: Zheng Huang
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 50 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This class is difficult. Avg for midterm/final is 30 which is because they are quite difficult. She crams so much information into 1.5 hr lecture that it's not possible to keep up in class, but i must say she explains concepts clearly. if you lock in / on top of your work it's doable. if you don't think you're a top student at berkeley, avoid tbh.

Effective and caring lecturer for game theory. Went out of her way to demonstrate concepts with engaging in-class games. The class was way harder and more technical than I expected, but I learned a lot. She was helpful in office hours and generally fair with grading. Exams and homework sets were pretty challenging. I wasn't a fan of the iclicker.

i went to every single lecture, no absences, took notes, and had no idea how to do the homework or exam. the midterm averages were a 40%, 30%, and i think the final was around the same range. I wouldn't say she's a good professor, but i think she tried to keep lecture engaging and entertaining. would not take again, i hate econ courses.

Exams are absolutely brutal with averages around 30% even though she curves at the end. Lectures don't prepare you for the exams and while practice exams and problem sets helped for midterms the final was just another level. Homework took hours to complete though was graded fairly. Attendance was also mandatory, but overall avoid at all costs.

Teacher was great at explaining everything, and honestly was one of the more entertaining lecturers I've  had at Berkeley. The curve for the class is fair, and she does give a lot of practice so if you just do all the worksheets and hw, you prob will get an A, just watch out for the algebra since the numbers aren't super nice in this class.

analysis.name: Dora Zhang
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Her lectures were very uninteresting. Never calls on students in the back- sometimes made eye contact with students in the back and then moved to call on someone who just raised their hand in the front, despite waiting in the back for a while. Really unmotivating to engage in lectures.

There was a lot of reading, but it wasn't unmanageable, and her philosophical, analytical lens through which we examined the texts in class was helpful in deep engagement with each text. No reading assignment felt pointless, and each lecture felt important and engaging.

I'm only one lecture into her class and she seems fine but there's clearly someone with a vendetta against her on this site who keeps spamming 1/5 reviews so I'd like to balance it out. Go ahead and read the negative reviews under this they're so pretentious and funny. I like the no electronics policy because I do not have a laptop.

good lecturer, covers a lot of context/background stuff, but for me the discussion sections covered much more of the text itself. There is limited content on the slides so listen in class! There are also reading quizzes every week.

This was probably one of my favorite english classes I've ever taken, the book selection was really enjoyable. Her lectures are interesting but not necessary to attend to do well. GSI's definitely were tough graders on the paper so I won't say this is an easy A but if you get help early on your papers and ask for feedback you will be fine.

analysis.name: Aaron McDaniel
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The professor is extremely pretentious and is not qualified to teach the course. One google search for "Aaron McDaniels Shark Tank" and you will see why. His views towards starting a company is extremely fantastical and the work is akin to a 5 unit , when the course is only a 2 unit class.

While the class was definitely more work than 2 units, it was undeniably worth it in the end. McDaniel is one of the most passionate, engaging professors I have ever had. Very open to critiques, improvements, and always down to help anyone who takes initiative to ask. The very hands-on nature of the course is challenging, but so rewarding.

Professor McDaniel's entrepreneurship course is very hands-on and practical, focusing on real startup processes rather than theory. He is patient, supportive, and genuinely cares about students' growth. On the last day of class, he even said his “office hours are for life.” He also brings strong real-world experience and great guest speakers.

Aaron is one of the best professors I've had at Cal. He is very accessible outside of class and always willing to give advice. The curriculum is incredibly well-designed and covers the entire entrepreneurship journey in great detail. If you want to learn how to build your own startup or entrepreneurship in general, take this class!

The professor encourages students from different backgrounds to share ideas, challenge assumptions, and think like real entrepreneurs rather than just students completing assignments. Feedback on projects is detailed and constructive, which really helps improve both thinking and execution. The workload is quite reasonable.

analysis.name: Zvezdelina Stankova
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 414 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Great class if you want to learn Math 54 materials. Good at first, but slowly the class got more centered around her than the students. O chem tutor replaced lectures for me. Threatened to withhold lecture videos, and ACTUALLY withheld FINAL REVIEW MATERIAL, we had no access to solutions of past exams and thus couldn't learn from their structure.

Prof. Stankova is not an ideal lecturer. As many others noted, her ego affects her teaching. She delayed material due to "unsatisfactory attendance." Homework assignments are also VERY heavy; with roughly 36-40 questions a week. Her expectations are strict and expect to get an earful if you ask something that was "answered" on the 15-page syllabus.

On the final, I received a 0/20 on a question that I got correct.  The grader deducted full points because I used an alternate method of solving the problem.  I have to take math class next semester for my major, and I am electing to take the more difficult math class just to avoid having her for a second semester.  plenty of review materials tho

Zvezda is passionate about math but WAY too much hw, too high of expectations for how much time devoted to class, notes are difficult to decipher bc lack of structure. I had a good GSI who was super helpful but I learned the material independently besides that. good things: ton of review materials, course captures uploaded, final clobber policy.

The most unbearable professor I have ever experienced. Her ego is through the roof but so fragile that people not showing up to her 9 a.m. lecture hurt her feelings to the point she delays necessary class material. Quizzes are much harder than homework & midterms. There is a quiz every week, only 10 minutes long. The homework load: HEAVY AF!

analysis.name: Aaron Fisher
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Personally, I felt that I needed the lectures to help me understand the readings and slides. I was surprised to end up with an A. I thought the class was challenging and I did really badly on the second exam. But he drops the lowest test grade and the final was pretty easy. Great class!

Honestly Fisher is one of the best professor I have had at UC Berkeley. He is a very kind and compassionate human being. Also had an amazing GSI - Peter. Reading the textbook is helpful and necessary to get an A in this course and attending lecture is always fun as Fisher makes the material fun and interesting to learn with personal  anecdotes.

Wow. Definitely in my top 3 all time favorite professors. The class is constantly laughing, tests are basically lecture-based (text will solidify material), and the material is organized and easy to understand if you pay attention. Aside from that, Dr. Fisher has demonstrated his compassion and humanity again and again. 10/10 Highly Recommended.

My favorite professor I've taken at berkeley. His lectures were as interesting as Ted talks and he has a great sense of humor. You feel like you're going to get a worse grade than you do because the tests are challenging, but there are easy ways to make up your grade. I will miss this class!

Fisher is definitely knowledgeable in his field but that's really the only positive thing I have to say about him as a professor. He goes off on many side tangents during lecture and if he is angry about something he brings that energy with him to class. Fisher frequently warns us anger is bad for the heart, but he needs to take his own advice.

analysis.name: Ron Loewinsohn
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Ron was a great, serious teacher. Going to office hours was a great way to get his personal feedback on the reading and my student writing. His written final exam was tough, but fair. Ron Loewinsohn raised the level of my writing and thinking at Berkeley, and for that I am grateful.

Prof. Loewinsohn has impeccable credentials. However, his time in the Ivory Tower has made him unbearably dull. His lectures seem to have remained unchanged since they were written on his typewriter some years ago, and he repeats himself constantly. Don't take his class if you enjoy reading the Beats. Do take this class if you enjoy namedropping.

Very nice and humorous. Lectures were very organized and clear. His lectures were mostly summaries of the books, which I thought was sort of pointless, since I read the books as we were supposed to. Grades were made of 2 essays and a final. Also, he was very helpful in Office Hours. Would recommend

For someone with such an illustrious carreer, he has no self-esteem. Humors the stupidest questions and wastes obscene amounts of time. I got an A+ on my first paper and a C- on my second. Very hard to figure out which way he's going to go and what he's looking for.

Very interesting and engaged.  His last lecture class at Berkeley was unfortunately tainted by incompetent readers, but Loewinsohn's mastery of the subject shined through. His presence will undoubtabley be widely missed.

analysis.name: Aaron Streets
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: homeworks are hard! and graded on accuracy. Lectures are amazing and he is a great teacher. his powerpoint skills are through the roof, hes like a powerpoint wizard. but hes usually pretty busy outside of class.

Hardest BioE class. Prereqs needed. Not accessible outside class. Clear lectures, knowledgeable. Homework is extremely hard so go to OFFICE HOURS. Exams easier than homework. Final is group project that needs effort. Compare answers with classmates or upper-class men. NO CURVES on exams. Exam 1 hardest. Difficulty drop right after. No extra credit

He is a great lecturer and always willing to help, but his course content is rather difficult.  Go to office hours for the homeworks and study hard for the midterms because those will make or break your grade.  Group project is also hard, but you receive relatively well-constructed feedback and if your group is good, you're set.

analysis.name: Ron Amundson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 62 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Very thoughtful and nuanced. Takes many perspectives into account and cares about linking lectures to current events. Has a positive outlook which is nice for a change. Lots of slides, make sure to take note of important people and diagrams for midterms. Easy if you study. Title sounds boring but Professor Amundson makes it interesting. Great guy.

Ron was a very nice guy, but his lectures were a bit stale. The topics were somewhat interesting, and the videos he showed were very informative. The readings he assigned were almost useless, since he summarized them in lecture. The tests felt very random when compared to the study guide. Discussions were easy, but boring + attendance is mandatory.

Very advanced information but professor is always willing to help. Group work is encouraged on homework. Learned a lot about soils, something I never thought I would have found interesting. Wish there were more field trips

Took it in my freshman year, I accidentally missed 2 quizzes, but he let me make them up. He can be hard to reach by email, but luckily my GSI that year was helpful. The exams and quizzes were pretty easy and online. Participation in discussion sections matters. Overall, it was an interesting course.

as a first semester freshman, this was a nice intro class. lectures were straightforward and easy to follow. a lot of content/memorization involved.

however, tests were a joke. nearly all multiple choice, online, and some questions were difficult to interpret. he was prone to making errors. 

sweet guy and easy class, but could be more organized.

analysis.name: Aaron Lopes
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: It was a pleasure taking his class. He was very concise with his lectures and gave very practical advice.  Tests are not as difficult as everyone makes them out to be. He also isn't too bad to look at!

I wasn't excited about taking o-chem over the Summer, but I'm glad I did. Aaron made the class enjoyable and very manageable. He makes the homework very hard and long, but if you can figure out the homework, the quizzes and tests are a breeze. He's also super approachable and determined that everyone can succeed. If you can take his class, DO IT!
Aaron is able to take difficult material and make it easy. He is always willing to help students and always comes in an hour earlier to help us. Take it from me. If you are bad at chem, take him.

This is not an easy course. Thermo is a beast, and he tells you this on the first day.  Attending lectures is helpful because he breaks down the material into essential and non-essential material for exams. I'm not sure how he grades because I was in the bottom half of the class and still got a B-. He's a good guy and I would take him again.

Super easy class. Exam questions are directly from the back of the book and variations from class examples. Dr. Lopes can be hard to understand at times, but his effort to make the class enjoyable, interesting, and achievable for everyone makes it worth while. Helpful during office hours.

analysis.name: Dor Abrahamson
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dor and his GSI are very passionate about what they teach but sometimes expect too much detail. Its a good amount of reading but class is pretty engaging with him. To be honest you don't have to attend every class
GOATED! Caring, and inspirational

analysis.name: Aaron Edlin
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class was very easy if you have any knowledge of calc. I got an A+ just by using what I learned in Econ 101a a semester earlier (and not going to class after the first 5 weeks). If you know how to maximize profit and minimize cost functions, you will do well with very little work.

His background is in both economics and law, and he's both worked in the White House and started his own company! His lectures are intriguing, though slow, and he is passionate about piquing your curiosity!
Edlin's a really nice guy and lecturer who's usually always available in office hours. Textbook isn't needed so go to every lecture! Tests are also really difficult (calculus-heavy).

This class is the reason why I'm going to graduate with only High Honors instead of Highest Honors and I am going to be mad about it. Loved the class content and especially worthwhile if you're interested in the intersection of economics and law. Beware of a group project worth 20%t (what took me out). Earned an A but curve put me at an A-.

Edlin is a fantastic professor.  His lectures were pretty engaging and he is a kind, understanding guy if you go to office hours.  The scoring breakdown was weird, where homework and just showing up to class was worth like 50% of the grade.  So if you put decent effort into homework and show up to class, you're halfway there.  Tests are easy too.

analysis.name: Brooks Abel
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Very passionate about his research and great to talk to in office hours. Lectures were mostly basic material that's explained well in the textbook (ok to skip); doing the problem sets which have the most challenging examples is when you learn. Writes a ton of extra practice that is very informative and good exam prep. Incredibly generous curve.

The professor is effective at conveying the material to students, primarily by providing extra worksheets, old exams, and review sheets that help prepare for midterms and the cumulative final. Nevertheless, the course is challenging as there are problem sets every week and lab work to complete. His assignments are similar in difficulty to exams.

Very solid professor & huge polymer nerd. He designs the PSets to be "the hardest version of the questions that you'll see," so the tests don't contain any surprises. Offers generous EC, such as Exam Wrappers (corrections) on tests for +5 bonus points, and is very active on Ed to answer any questions. Lecture slides are very useful and organized.

very fair psets and exams--lectures can be dense but he's incredible in office hours (he tends to ramble but drops a ton of useful info in there). labs are long but doable. go to prof and GSI OH often and you'll be fine. kind and caring and genuinely wants us to succeed; def don't be afraid of this class (about the same as difficulty as math 53/54)

Tbh one of the hardest classes I've ever taken. I don't even blame bro for it being THIS hard. He's a chill guy. Lectures this fast (with the ton of contents) expectedly only cover the basic; to really understand be prepared to grind thru his PS with excessive YT/OH/textbook…overall a special muscle memory is required for exams. Sadly no shortcut.

analysis.name: Abhishek Kaicker
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Kaicker is incredibly engaging. In his modern South Asia class ("Gandhi's India") he made historical figures come alive. He's kinda intimidating and he will occasionally randomly call on people about assigned reading, but highly recommend his class if you have an interest in South Asia.

There are only few classes that you look forward to attend and his class is one of them. After math heavy and dry technical lectures, his class and the readings would provide you comfort even if you don't have historian-like intellectual brain power. Take HIST 114B and HIST 39T, please do. - This would be my last rating for a Berkeley professor.
Great professor! Very helpful, caring, interested in students ideas and opinions on whatever topics. Lots of guest lectures. Take his class!!!

Professor Kaicker is great! Super interesting class that challenges your preconceived notions of what history really is. Kaicker is a cool guy and a good lecturer; he also checked in during zoom classes which was always appreciated. 70-100 pages a week plus 4 essays. Definitely try to get a class with him if you are at all interested in history!

Professor Kaicker not only changed my view of Indian history but of history in general. Through his reading assignments, he teaches critical reading, ensuring you learn how to dissect a source. His lectures are brilliant even if you're someone far removed from Indian history. He's the best professor I've ever had, and a true mentor.

analysis.name: Abhijeet Paul
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I took this class at Laney College. This class is good for gen ed. A nice professor and assignments due each week are very interesting.

He is by far one of the greatest professors I have ever had at Berkeley. He really made the lectures super fascinating and for that reason, I loved going to lecture. Be sure to participate because that's key in that class. Since I took the R5B based on film, we watched interesting movies with lots of social commentary which I loved discussing.

A very inspiring and caring professor, Abhijeet Paul made sure to make classes entertaining and informative, but most importantly he always tailored to what the class wanted to talk about and focus on. He tended to go on philosophical tangents in accordance to the novels that we read, that made this literature class very fascinating.

This class is pretty easy. If u need to fulfill ur r&c a, this is the class to take. As long as you read the main books that he assigns, you should be good (he only assigned us 2). Weekly reading responses are graded on completion. He's a super great professor who's very passionate about his work, and you get a good overview of famous Indian myths.

Professor Paul is a very interesting person to be taught by. His Global Studies course really enlightened me this semester on many problems with media worldwide as well as new perspectives on issues such as racism, sexism, and classism. The midterm and final are both group projects - choose wisely.

analysis.name: Abbye Atkinson
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Assigned quizzes every week that made us look for the smallest detail in the readings. Lectures often contradicted the answers on the quizzes and when this was brought up we were told to resort to the readings instead of the actual lectures. Lectures were very boring and hard to sit through. I felt that my GSI taught better than the professor.

annoying prof and talked too much, class was boring, and put people to sleep. mandatory attendance sucked, best part of class was when it ended. dont reccomend

Worst professor I've had during my time at Cal.

The most unfair and nontransparent professor I have come across at my time in Berkeley. Also had her for MCB104, and MCB133L is just as bad. Class is good for people who want to be well rounded. The people complaining are probably just the poli sci majors that arent interested being well rounded. The guys professional

Overall, a good Professor. He likes to boost his own ego and sometimes makes rude comments, but he's very passionate and makes you want to learn. I'd recommend having a backround in int'l poltics/econ before taking the class. Don't be scared off on the first day-Stick around and you will learn a lot. One of the most informative classes I've taken.

I was first skeptical about taking the course since whoever rated him before gave him a bad rating, but the class was so much fun and the material so fascinating that I stayed. ABSOLUTELY AMAZING. Lectures are so hard to follow and she makes even the simplest of topics super confusing — nice teacher tho. If you have an option to take another teacher I would for sure recommend doing so.

Agol is pretty underrated. He's a funny, nice guy and can be very helpful if you ask him questions. Nevertheless, you must work for your grade. My GSI, on the other hand, was neither helpful nor clear.

One of the worst math 1A prof. i have ever seen in my life. For the most part lecture is a going over the textbook so focus on homework, do that and you'll do well.

Very interesting if you wanna learn about monkeys and forensics!

Prof. Salim is incredible - you can tell he cares deeply about the material he is teaching, this has allowed him to deliver some of the most engaging and thought-provoking lectures. It is becoming difficult to find professors teaching about Rumi's poetry that come from the same land of the material being taught themselves. Please sign yourself up!

AMAZING professor who makes something as difficult as Rumi's poetry approachable for a non-poetry expert. He is very accommodating and engaging in class which is always nice. The material of the class is difficult but he makes sure all his students feel heard in their contributions and always pauses during readings to check our understanding. Love!

Professor Salim is amazing! He is able to engage the students with the materials and create a welcoming environment within the class. graded by 4 things (2 essays, 1 midterm, 1 final)
Can skip class and not do readings cause not emphasized in class.

Ahn was a pleasant instructor personally, but he didn't give a clear enough idea of how we were to be graded. Prepare to be surprised. This should have been a relaxing pastime; it ended up being difficult and I had minor injuries camp at times (but that may be due to our demanding TA.)

Professor Ahn is a very sweet and supportive person. She can be unclear when it comes to grading expectations, but in general she is very accessible and caring for her students. The only thing is she doesn't have a lot of office hours. Create study groups with classmates.

Not gonna lie, I was kind of intimidated of this class bc EVERYONE has to participate (ie singing in front of everyone), but after a couple of weeks I eventually calmed down and really started to appreciate Jean's approach to teaching. She truly cares about helping her students and is super understanding, so the class is a very safe space to learn.

My academic life was transformed and defined by the presence of Professor Ahmadi at UC Berkeley. He is a scholar of the highest caliber and I have learned so much from him. A real gem. Hes well-versed in Persian literature and pretty much most other things - history, critical theory, politics, religion. Classes have an active role for students. great class.  he has reasonable expectations since its only 3 units.  he usuallly throws in random lectures where he just talks about interesting random things.  very worthwhile if you want to spend 3 hoursa  week learning really cool things with a chill professor take this class.  he's laid back and funny! textbook got low rating cuz we dont have

Very cool professor! Ahn explains well.  He's relatively young for a professor which helps him understand our confusion and frustration. He's also pretty funny.

One of the best lecturers at Berkeley. He's super articulate and if you pay attention you only need to do la light review.

Worst class I have ever taken. Lectures are extremely, extremely disorganized, and key concepts are skipped over and not explained well. The whole course staff was in shambles. This really didn't even feel like a class at all. Don't expect to learn much in this class. UC Berkeley please look into this class.

His lectures have nothing to do with the content that is being tested. We are expected to know all this stuff that he doesn't teach without the help of external resources. He has the audacity to say that we cannot use AI.. if he taught it wouldnt be an issue. He tries to be funny and relatable but hes not. He needs to reassess his teaching strategy

He is one of the worst prof ever. Doesn't do anything, the GSIs do everything for the class. All he does is show up to lecture and make jokes. Learned nothing from his slides, have to learn everything myself. Unfortunately have to take another class with him next semester, don't know what I did to this school to deserve this…

analysis.name: Anna Eng
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 39 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Lectures easy to understand and Prof seemed passionate about the class. The readings are pretty long but do them. The grading is all over the place, so don't trust the syllabus. There were only a few "weekly" assignments and was 35% of the grade. Also all multiple select questions are all or nothing, so you pick the right choices or tank the 0.

Professor Eng was one of the best educators I've had. She is so passionate about the subject that I felt that I was truly learning not just reciting meaningless information. There's A LOT of readings,  but you can get away with skimming or not reading all of them. But the field trips were especially amazing and made our class feel like a family. :D

I really enjoyed Professor Eng's class. The slides, films, and readings given really show the amount of care they put into teaching this class. The readings could be heavy, but were still illuminating and provided deep insight into the topics at hand. The field trips were also great, providing an important dive into local history and culture also.

Relatively easy course but a lot of longgggg readings per week. Supposed to have weekly reading responses but we stopped after a while.  Attendance was required but you could just get the attendance quiz code from a friend. Eye-opening course though. Easy A as long as minimal effort.

I enjoyed this class a lot, and think the readings are very interesting. Pretty easy class since everything (including tests and the final) is take home. Not a lot of assignments, which is both good and bad since it creates limited things to grade on. Truly appreciated what I learned!

analysis.name: Schaab  Andreas
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Without a doubt, Professor Schaab is the best professor I have ever had the pleasure of learning from. His lectures feel like movies. He uses storytelling and lots of visual examples/graphs to teach the material. He caters to students of all learning preferences. Straightforward grading. Show up, put forth effort, you will be good and learn a lot.

Other reviews saying negative things about this professor just didnt go to lecture or do homework lol. He specifically stated multiple times that he would introduce new concepts in the homework. If you understood the hw assignments then you WILL do well on the exams. Best way to prepare for the exams is to review hw and do the practice exams.

The lectures were engaging and interactive. The exams were pretty math-heavy, so you really need to go to the discussion sessions to understand the material. The course had a strong focus on historical analysis. The professor was humble and polite, though I wish he provided more study materials. Overall, he is a very good professor.

There were no textbooks, no notes, no tutoring, and the lectures were completely unrelated to the exams, mostly consisting of historical stories. The exams, however, included a large amount of math, and there were no review materials available. Yet, this course was a required course for many students' majors.

The class material isn't hard and most of the lectures are just history lessons which makes it interesting. He is an amazing lecturer and wants you to do well in the class. Best way to learn is by studying the homework. The exams are math heavy but fair.

analysis.name: Alexander Appleton
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Don't take this class unless you absolutely have to. I would have been better off going right to Calculus. Thought I'd take Pre-Calc as a refresher course, huge mistake. Alex means well but really overcomplicates the material. The midterms are never what we learned in class and the class average floats around a 40% until he curves the grades.

I think Alex had really good intentions and tried to do his best but the course was awful.  The class was 1000x harder than the previous PreCalculus class I had taken.  I felt that I did better on the homework by teaching myself but this got really hard toward the end of the class.  The tests were brutal.

Extremely hard midterms and final. Impossible to even study for. Do not take this class if you don't have to. He overcomplicates simple things like the area of a normal right triangle. Write his "g" like "9" and vice versa. Worksheets are impossible and often are the same level as his exams. Little communication with his GSIs. Although a nice curve
Horrible professor, you can't understand what he is saying due to his heavy accent. Wouldn't recommend to take this course if you have no previous knowledge with Trig or Pr-calculus.

Appleton taught Math 32 (College Precalculus) and made this course 200 times harder than it needed to be. My friends in Calculus couldn't even complete the difficulty of problems he assigned. The curves in the class were so heavy that a 50% turned out to be a B-. Nobody could pass the tests, he was terrible at lecturing, honestly try to stay away.

analysis.name: Apara Nanda
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 31 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I've taken Nanda's class the past 2 summers to fulfill my reqs, I love her. She is a relatively easy grader, offers any support 24/7 as long as you reach out, but has a thick accent and bad mic quality. She's very caring and genuinely wants to help as much as possible, and is passionate about her work! Better than semester professors.

She is so nice! This professor just wants everyone to be happy in her class. We had to read three novels, write three essays, write two film responses, and write one research paper. It wasn't that much work. She rarely gives negative feedback in class, though, so sometimes it's difficult to understand what she wants. Great professor overall!

Professor Nanda is amazing! She cares for her students and is very supportive and accessible even though it was an online course. Grading criteria was a little unclear; she has rubrics but doesn't give super constructive critiques. LOTS of reading and writing. But easy class as long as you don't fall behind (easy to if you do it online, so don't).

She is a wonderful professor. She is hilarious and super passionate about what she teaches. She gives great feedback and is willing to help her students. The in-class discussions are very helpful and also very fun. You can greatly tell she cares about her students.

Definately one of my favorite professors.  She has a true passion for her students and the courses that she teaches.  In addition to being extremely passionate about her students, she was also very insightful and had a clear grasp on the books she was teaching.

analysis.name: Amanda Goldstein
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Currently teaches at Cornell. Had her for FWS, and she was amazing! Very well prepared and energetic, perhaps too enthusiastic for people who are not genuinely interested in English. Leads great in class discussions because she is very knowledgeable. Also very flexible and understanding.

People who say this professor is too fast just proves that these students are too slow and didn't deserve to be in UC Berkeley in the 1st place. I enjoy her talking too fast because I am a fast learner.

Very sweet and accessible professor but was fast talker and sometimes hard to understand since she seems to go out of her way to use hard words. The assignments during the year were pretty easy and as long as you are creative with your projects you will do well. Only thing I struggled with was studying for the final exam which is all encompassing.

ENG 177A- there is SO much reading, and the final is all FACT based from the materials from the entire semester. If given the chance to take this professor, I'd avoid it. Long lectures with scattered thoughts, makes you feel guilty for not attending an optional field trip the Friday before thanksgiving, and pop quizzes to ensure you read.

Professor Goldstein is simply brilliant. Each lecture was extremely engaging and packed with provoking ideas. She clearly took immense in selecting each reading for the course- incredible variety and content. Easily the most passionate and inspiring professor- and person- I've had at Berkeley. Truly fantastic

analysis.name: Amy Lee
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Very relaxed professor with manageable assignments and a reasonable reading load. Most class time is spent discussing the readings, so it's important to come prepared and complete the assigned chapters. Grading criteria can sometimes be unclear, but she offers helpful guidance and advice both in and out of class.

She assigns a lot of reading, but it is manageable. She does not have a very clear grading criteria. She is very accessible and holds lots of virtual office hours. She has a no-technology policy, but was not too strict about it.
Very understanding professor. She has clear grading criteria and is very lenient. Easy to do well as long as you complete the work and pay attention in class. Overall great professor.

analysis.name: Ameer Loggins
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Loggins is a passionate, authentic educator. Each lecture was a mix of structured material and powerful lectures, tying it to the real world. He has a "pull-up" policy, inviting you to bring a family member or friend to the lecture, turning the class into a community. Graded on a few short papers, MT, and the Final paper/presentation. Take it!

Meeting Dr. Loggins and having the pleasure/privilege to take this class (Fall 2024) was truly a one-of-a kind experience! He is unapologetically true to himself and his pedagogy is inspiring as a prospective educator myself. I still find myself returning to the literature posed on the syllabus and the course workload is highly manageable.

Such an amazing professor. His class felt like a high school class in the best way possible. Great sense of humor, makes the class feel like a family, and great lectures. We only had like 3 assignments, one take home midterm, and a take home final. Best class and professor I have seen here by far.

Every single second in Ameer's class pays off. This former rapper speaks in such a colloquial and approachable way that sometimes I think he is cooler than me. What he discusses is never in the media. I can guarantee that you will understand what kind of music you consume every day in a totally different light. 1 short paper and 1 final paper.

Professor Loggins is by far the best professor I've ever had. The two hours of class flew by every week because of his passion and dedication for the subject matter. Learning from him was truly eye-opening and it challenged us all to embrace "touchy" subjects with open discourse. If you ever get the chance, take one of his classes!

analysis.name: Amitai Shenhav
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Had him for C127--Cognitive Neuroscience. He's very passionate and cares a lot about the topics and his students. Lectures can get very dense but he's great at breaking down complex ideas and uses good examples to do so. Also features his kid in his slides which was adorable.

(CogSci C127) Amitai is an amazing lecturer and speaker, and it is clear that he is very passionate and puts a lot of effort into this course. Much of the grade is exams, which were relatively hard, but the questions were fair. GSIs were amazing as well. The class takes hard work, but I highly recommend taking it.

Took COGSCI C127. He genuinely cares about his students and knows his stuff. Expect dense presentations on tricky cog sci topics—needs time to digest. Classes can feel a bit dry, but the material is clear if you pay close attention. Not an easy A—takes effort and passion for test, but he's fair and understanding overall.

analysis.name: Amy Gurowitz
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 135 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Lectures were a very dense 1.5 hours of Amy talking really fast, but she's a really good and entertaining lecturer so I didn't mind. No notes or slides or anything posted, so missing lecture is a really bad idea. Essay on theory wasn't too bad, and the exams were pretty easy as well. Do the reading, and get Deirdre for your GSI, and you'll do well.

Hands down the best lecturer I have had so far. Given that I am only a 2nd year, it's a small sample but she is very engaging and the content is interesting! ATTEND LECTURES, the content is on the midterm and final. Understand the main points of the readings and take notes during the lecture! 1 essay, 1 midterm, and 1 final.

The semester hasn't ended yet but I LOVE Amy Gurowitz. She is the best professor I've had so far, she knows her stuff and is very funny. I always look forward to this class. Reading heavy and lectures teach you a lot, quizzes are seldom and very simple as long as you do the readings. Take Gurowitz above anyone else, she is the best!!

Good and efficient lecturer with a very clear, direct and organised style. However, class is very heavy in reading, and most are long and dull. Lecture recordings are also not released online and the slideshows are pretty basic, which basically makes attendance mandatory.

I've had her twice and I think she does a really good job on her lectures. She reads off the slides, though, so if you don't want to go in person you don't have to. But i do recommend it & she's super nice in OH

DO THE READINGS!! i credit my A to that

analysis.name: Arash Jamshidpey
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I think that he's over hated, I've taken a lot of different stats professors here and his lectures are pretty average. I think the grading was relatively generous, towards the end he curved better than expected. Overall he's a generally nice dude, and he adequately prepared us for his exams. He definitely deserves better than a 1 imo.

I love him, lowkey the best professor I've ever had. Very funny, does not know how to record for notes on his ipad. Every thing is TBD, he loves the word TBD. Looks lonely and answers students questions precisely. Was never late and gives great feedbacks for emails, not yet received any email back from him. Seriously, take this guy!!! :)

The teaching style didn't work well for me and lecture notes weren't made available. The course structure relied heavily on student responsibility without adequate resources. While I understand professors have different approaches, this particular style made it very difficult to succeed. I would not take another course with this professor.

extremely convoluted lectures and often goes on tangents. He tries to be nice but honestly the curves are brutal, curving exam averages to around a C- which is pretty insane. the final had typos on it. No ed or canvas discussions. Honestly put insane amounts of effort into this class and the effort doesnt match the results for this class.

Lowkey he worst professor I've ever had, I will avoid any class he is teaching. Late, very unorganized, very late and little feedback. Uploads solutions a day/night before midterm. Notes in class are not clear. Often loses notes or they get deleted during class. Super complex and weird grading calculations for final grade.

analysis.name: Arpad Horvath
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Humorous lectures, truely cares about the topics. He tells you what questions will appear in the midterm/final in lecture. Also your grades dependent on how well you make your cheatsheet. Generous with partial credit and fairly easy midterms. Final was definitely hard; if the question wasnt on ur cheatsheet, you basically got no points for that.

Great in lectures. Accessible outside of class (office hours, personal meeting set ups). Course itself is generally light (5 homework assignments that are fairly straightforward). Cheat sheet can be used (and is most definitely necessary) for both midterms and final. Must write everything on cheat sheet, but prof goes over all possible questions.

Professor Horvath gives minimal homework (5 for CE11) but all assignments are fairly dense. Attendance isn't mandatory but I'd emphasize showing up to lecture because he's quite literally gives you questions that will be on the exam as he's reading the slides + lectures aren't recorded. If you do everything right, it should be an easy class.

The class was elementary as long as you did the work and put every little detail of the lectures in your cheat sheet(s). Although I love “easy A” classes, I cannot say I particularly learned anything, nor did I feel myself utilizing my knowledge during exams. Either the question was on your cheat sheet, or it wasn't; there was no in-between.

Horvath, although a dry lecturer, is an excellent teacher. His midterms and homeworks are straightforward. If you attend class and spend about 2 hours per homework (we had 6 homeworks in total) you will be in a very good position to get a good score. He cares deeply about the environment and possesses a wealth of expertise in environmentalism.

analysis.name: Arpita Roy
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 68 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Arguably the best course I've taken at Berkeley. If you are a CS/DS major, PLEASE TAKE IT. Prof Roy is an amazing lecturer, and does a phenomenal job of connecting Phil/Sociology/Anthro with CS that many students never get the chance to learn. Prof Roy cares deeply for students. One of the few classes I genuinely loved. (Class also goes by CDSS 60)

Professor Roy is a fantastic instructor! Her energy, deep knowledge, and genuine care for students makes the class enjoyable and engaging. She encourages questions, supports creative topics for the panel presentation, and gives clear instructions. I learned a lot and always felt motivated to participate. Highly recommend her anthropology class!

Professor Roy is an invigorating lecture that has the rare ability to take abstract material and make it feel urgent. Easily the most though-provoking courses at Berkeley and should be required for CS/DS majors the way that it connects to debates on human values, AI and technology. She is kind, accessible and genuinely listens to her students.

HIGHLY recommend this class — covers a great deal about philosophical ideas and its intersection with modern data and ethics. Prof Roy is amazing, loves to chat with students in OH about anything in general! Classes and readings are highly intellectually stimulating and have genuinely inspired me to continue learning philosophy alongside my major!

Amazing professor, she taught a lot of real world examples that relate to current society. I know she put in a lot of efforts on preparing good and interactive slides for us. Also all of the class readings are the ones she carefully choose, really inspirational. If you have any personal connections or even the concerns, don't afraid of asking!

analysis.name: Ari Edmundson
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Breathtakingly smart, humane and kind and incredibly caring. Even in such a big class, if you attend office hours he will know you as a student and person. Inspirational scholar deeply invested in his work. He includes a huge diversity of readings to engage students with ethical themes in the tech world and beyond. Wish I could take him again.

Tries so hard to artificially engineer rigor into this course, when in reality it is some of the easiest braindead simple concepts just convoluted behind flowery jargony language. Weird rubrics that makes getting an A super subjective. Guy would not survive anything that requires actual brain power. No curves by the way.

It's a pretty interesting class but the profs make it difficult for no reason. Make sure to do all the readings and read all the lecture slides because they are looking for particular answers on the midterms/finals. He is a super nice guy though and really smart, but the lectures are very convoluted for rather simple concepts

I loved having Professor Edmundson for Data C104! Im a DS major myself and didnt know anything regarding the contexts and ethics of data. Very insightful lectures as well as readings that opened my eyes to how important it is to have a class like this. Although the reading notes weren't clear rubrics, the class itself is awesome and Ill miss it!

Professor Edmundson is incredibly knowledgable and cares deeply about his students. Data C104 was writing-heavy and conceptually challenging, especially for me as a data science major, but the content was extremely valuable and Edmundson's office hours were incredibly inspiring, comfortable, and helpful. Highly recommend

analysis.name: Arun Sharma
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 332 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: He turns 16A from one of the easiest classes at Berkeley to one of the hardest. WAIT UNTIL MAIN CAMPUS TO TAKE THIS CLASS. His quizzes are okay, but the midterms and finals are crazy hard. A lot of the people in the class, including me, have prior calc experience and find this class really hard. WAIT UNTIL MAIN CAMPUS. AVOID THIS CLASS

Worst professor ever. I hadn't taken calculus before,& he said that he'd go through all the concepts sufficiently. HE LIED. He is brief&unhelpful! You can study hard & go through all the material he ever provided, BUT YOU WILL NEVER BE PREPARED FOR THE MIDTERM. I don't even have enough space to explain. He's a jerk. Wait for main campus to take 16A

He is simply the worst teacher I have ever had. Most students at Berkeley have already taken Calc so they do okay in his class, but if you have not I would recommend skipping until its offered with another instructor. He makes the exams extremely difficult and very different from what he teaches in class. He's clearly a smart guy but can't teach.

Sharma's quizzes were definitely more difficult than the homework but not to the point where they are unmanageable. If you study the material and attend lecture/office hours this class will not be too bad. He was always very accessible, especially during midterm/finals with extended office hours.

This is the worst class I've ever taken. I've never been more unsupported by him and the GSI's. I got hit hard with a terrible GSI, who unfairly graded. He spends the whole lecture talking about how you are wrong to solve a certain problem, rather than teaching how to do it. He's a good person and is usually nice, just bad lecturer.

analysis.name: Arash Farahmand
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The class was curved 33 A 33 B 33 C. A couple of students used ChatGPT on the final exam and took some of the A's. It was upsetting to see no action taken against students openly cheating on the final in class and (I heard) at the DSP as well. Also, the tests are open-note, so he's testing your reliability, not your course knowledge.

Math 53N (summer) had lots of homework and open note tests, and the homework problems were very similar to the tests. Despite this, it was somewhat difficult due to how it was fast paced, and that lectures didn't completely cover what's on the homework.
Awesome professor if you let him know about you by talking to him.

I took Math N1B over the summer. The class was structured very well and we knew exactly when we were learning what and how much it was worth. He tells you which sections of the textbook are going to be covered on each question of the exam as well as similar problems so as long as you do a ton of practice problems, exams will be a piece of cake.

analysis.name: Arman Catterson
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 138 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Literally my favorite professor and favorite class at Cal. Dr. Prof. Catterson is so personable and so good at explaining psychology that I learned like a sponge. He was always prepared and, although he makes you truly work for your grade, you will get out of it what you put in. I loved every activity and every lesson. He makes you think.

If there was ever a professor who embodied every single godly attribute a professor could possibly attain, it would be Professor Arman Catterson. What an absolute legend, holy moly bro, this guy is the definition of peak. Genuinely the best prof I've ever had, would 100% take again. He and his class were such an awesome intro to Berkeley.

Catterson is like the coding version of jesus christ to me 
ive never had a professor who more earnestly wants you to succeed - you get out of the class what you put in + he is so flexible with quizzes and exams. ASK FOR HELP WHEN YOU NEED IT, its so easy to get lost, you have to be proactive about getting support but its there for you!

HE'S THE BEST. He's so funny and he kept a THREE HOUR lecture entertaining. I had NO problems with him and would take his class over and over again. PLEASE IF YOU HAVE THE CHANCE TO TKAE HIS CLASS, DO IT. He's so amazing.

Such an amazing professor!!! Makes statistics and R code so easy. I took statistics in another class that taught a lot of similar topics and Professor Catterson explained something in 30 minutes that other stats class couldn't teach in a week. He's a really understanding professor and doesn't give much homework. Definitely take his class!

analysis.name: Arash Ng
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: An actual goat. I horribly failed the midterm and was well below the curve for an A (my fault). I started going to every office hour after that. He was fun to talk to. In the end he decided to give extra credit to anyone who would send him their notes for a chapter. P sure I failed the final but he still gave me an A.

Arash is such a great professor! I took his class over the summer @ Berkeley. His lectures are amazing. He makes them very engaging. If you have time to visit his OH, you definitely should! He gives great feedback on tests and exams.
Overall he is a very sweet person :) he makes me feel very welcome in his class.
Thank you, Arash!
Arash is one of the most friendly people I have ever seen!  His lecture is interesting and he treats students really patient in office hour.

analysis.name: Nathan Atkinson
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This was my second course with Atkinson, and not only was the content material incredibly interesting, relevant, and engaging, but he also brought in guest speakers and made the class very interactive. He is accessible outside of class and provides incredible feedback. If you can take his courses, do it! He is the reason I am a rhetoric major now!

Very cool class that involved several fieldwork assignments throughout semester and a capstone from that. Selected readings all tied into course and relevant to fieldwork and capstone. Had to do readings before class (participation grade) but he essentially synthesizes them during lecture. First rhetoric class and would definitely recommend.

Amazing professor. He breaks down the previous reading in his lecture, making it very comprehensible and fostering good class conversation. Clearly very passionate about rhetoric in a way that inspires.

Nathan is one of the best professors I have had. He is funny, an engaging lecturer, gives helpful and constructive feedback, and consistently maintains a well-paced course. His readings are incredibly diverse and interesting, and he is flexible with students who need extra help. If you get a chance to be his student, don't miss out on it!
Very interesting lecturer, only a few writing assignments for the semester

analysis.name: Atreyee Gupta
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: It was difficult to catch everything she said during lecture. Presentations only had pictures, no words or bulletin points at all. Lectures arent recorded so if you miss something it's hard to catch up. You get 10 points taken off every absent, even if you email before hand. Very unclear and overall unorganized class. Hard to understand the topics

She is a very soft-spoken and down-to-earth person who responds to your questions very quickly and cares about her students and their learning. The lectures are also interesting, covering a wide range of topics that are fun to explore. There was an in-class essay midterm and a take-home final. Overall, it's a pretty light class for breadth.

Gupta is one of the most intelligent and knowledgeable professors that I have had the pleasure of taking. Her courses are built around intense readings, lectures and long discussions. She tends to be soft-spoken in the classroom so make sure to ask the hard questions and really dive into the material. Do that, the class will be unforgettable.

Great class and would recommend, you can definitely tell that she's passionate and knowledgable of the course material. Don't miss lecture, the powerpoints are online, but are mostly made up of images. Hard to catch up if you fall behind on lecture.
I am glad I took this class and still go to her for advice. Go to office hours - she is very helpful and accessible

analysis.name: Alper Atamturk
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: the class seems really easy but professor atamturk can just make it really hardthrough his tests. his tests were not that bad but he really should be giving more time for his tests. ace the homework and come extra early for the tests.

162 with Atamturk is much more difficult than with other professors but I REALLY enjoyed this class. The material is fun and Atamturk really makes you think. He won't spoon-feed anything to you and that's what I liked about him.

this guy is a tool. he thinks he knows everything. homework gets hard towards end of the semester, midterm was really long but do-able, the final wasn't too bad, but his grading scheme is very out of wack. try to avoid this guy.

He gave intuitive explanations of the material in class and was overall a good professor.  His midterm was long (though not exceedingly difficult) and 4/5ths of his final was manageable.  I'd recommend him.

It is a loaded course. You have to learn the subject matter, do a research project, and manage portfolios in addition to homeworks. but it was worthed. Prof. Atamturk is very knowledgeable. Recommended.

analysis.name: Atilla Yilmaz
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: One of the best professors I've had. Crystal clear explanations; very helpful illustrations of abstract content and methods for thinking about problems. Homework was very helpful. Very well-written tests that were fairly graded. And near the end of the semester he even began making jokes. I give this professor an A+, and would highly recommend him.

Very clear, sharp, on point and engaging. He lectures from the book, or rather explaining the book, which is good when the book itself is so dense/difficult/good.  (This also minimizes the need to take notes.)  He tries to make his tests fairly challenging--sometimes everybody gets crushed.  But upper upper div curves can be more forgiving.

Great professor. Funny, approachable, helpful. Motivated the material with illustrations, brief discussions of applications, and intuitive thinking. Highly recommend him. His tests, although interesting & fair, were on the difficult side.

analysis.name: Atul Singh
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I have attended lectures by at least 50 different professors in various topics but this one is by far the best. Do not take his course in your first semesters or your other courses will become too boring. Most complicated definitions will be explained in the simplest terms. Absolutely no jargon allowed. If "you dare to know" this is the right one.

Hands down, Professor Singh's class is one of the best I've taken at Berkeley. He is a professors who actually cares about teaching in opposite to those who are solely focused on research. Don't be intimidated by Atul's extroverted style, you will see that he is really cool and smart . Also, the GSI Ti Ngo, is one of the best GSI's I've ever had.

Prof. Atul is an intelligent professor who values your learning experience more than simply giving you a grade. Be prepared to read and participate in class! My reader was a very fair grader and both Prof. Atul and our reader gave great feedback when anyone needed help! Don't be intimidated by his enthusiasm, he's just passionate about teaching!

This class challenged me to rethink my opinions about the world. Prof Singh will push you to critically look at social and political theory. I loved how engaged he was with his students; he makes an effort to get to know everyone and will constantly push you to make the most out of his class. He can be a bit scattered but is good with feedback.

This guy will rock your world. Be prepared to challenge your assumptions and think critically. The professor is very unorthodox but stick with it. You will find this to be the best class you've ever taken. Atul is also happy to discuss career options and grad school with each of his students. If you have the opportunity, take this class!!!

analysis.name: Asma Kazmi
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: incredibly torturous and boring. prof never entered a single grade into the grade book. the lectures suck, you have to turn in notes for hw. generally a very easy class that you can coast through. but jesus christ
Seems like a great person but is genuinely one of the worst lecturers I have ever met. Class was easy though, and there were a lot of guest lecturers which made it bearable.

Very friendly professor who almost never gives harsh comments. Soft voice may make you fall asleep in a warm afternoon. Well-experienced in her area of knowledge. Please be sure to read the materials before coming to class so that she won't be embarrased when no one answers the reading questions.

analysis.name: Ashley Reaver
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: While participation is optional you should show up to class! Professor Reaver is an excellent professor who is very well versed in her field. She is approachable and willing to work with you if you find yourself struggling. Definitely have to study for the exams and understand the content but the best thing you can do is just show up to class.

Professor Reaver is nothing short of fantastic! She is down to earth, matter-of-fact, and knowledgable and that really shows in her lectures. Expectations for the class were very clear: three assignments, two midterms, a final, and discussion attendance. This class really got me thinking more about my health and food choices. Highly recommend!

2 quizzes, 1 written assignment and 1 group brochure project. Grading is very generous, despite attendance being optional I suggest attending because it helps a lot with quiz material and it's also just really interesting content that can be applicable to life. Highly recommend!

She's a nice person, but the lectures are really dense. The class has way more chemistry than I was expecting. There's no discussion section, worksheets, or assignments, so it's hard to know what's important. And it's almost all memorization. We're only graded by 3 exams, 1 final, 1 project. Would have preferred more assignments to help the grade.
