Prof. Reaver is kind, passionate and interesting. You need to take her class seriously, but it is totally doable if you try. I found it pretty easy. Her assignments are very reasonable in quantity and easy to do. I really liked her lecture content as well!

analysis.name: Sholeh Asgary
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Shole is a fantastic teacher who makes learning fun and practical. He teaches in a way that helps us understand how things work in real life. She talked to us like friends, asking us questions and listening to our ideas. We learn from each other and celebrate our differences. She inspires us to think for ourselves and discover new things.
She is a very kind and understanding professor. She tries everything to lift the pressure off everyone's shoulders during difficult times.

Sholeh is a lovely artist who feels very deeply in her work. She does have a tendency to ramble, but our class was discussion heavy and everyone who wanted their voice heard did. I felt very affirmed in my own art practice, and more informed about the global happenings of the world after taking this course. Thanks Sholeh!

analysis.name: Richard Ashcroft
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 66 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Okay lectures, but he talks WAY too fast and tends to get distracted easily. Heavily dependent on readings (the course is basically just a summary of readings), and the content is way more political theory than actual American politics. Participation and attendance are mandatory, and prompts for the midterms and final are released beforehand.

His teaching style isn't for everyone. His slides are essentially word vomit, and he speaks incredibly fast in a loud monotone voice. He often goes on tangents and presents disconnected thoughts, which makes it difficult to follow a main point. The exams are quite easy, as although he presents his standards as very high, they are really reasonable.

Prof Ashcroft is one of the greats in the ps dept. Exams are intimidating because they require a LOT of prep work. Skim readings, attend lecture and review sessions & ur good. Has a witty & deadpan sense of humor, delivers great lectures, puts much thought and effort into teaching and is super helpful in OH. Challenging but super worth it

Extremely rude and condescending. Genuinely not sure what his problem is. Had him during the summer as a required class for an internship program. Perhaps he felt personally hurt because we weren't taking his class as seriously as he wanted, but realistically, why would we? Very unprofessional in his conduct yet will accuse you of being so.

Weekly Readings and you discuss them during lecture/discussion (open discussion style). Attendance taken with polleverywhere. You have 2 midterms and final and he gives you all the questions in advance. There was barely any assignments (just one precis, SUPER EASY), and a final podcast group project. As long as you put effort you'll do just fine.

analysis.name: Robert Ashmore
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 31 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Don't expect any clarity out of this one-he starts topics without finishing them, focuses a lot of time on irrelevant topics, and, while he talks ALOT and sounds good, he actually says very little. He knows his stuff, but I feel that that he's so into his academic world that it's hard for him to relate to students or clearly express his thoughts.

Hard grader, attendance in class is necessary. Must do a lot of work for this class to be able to get a good grade, especially essays. Lots of readings and lectures and discussions are mainly regarded to the readings you must do every few days. To succeed, attend lectures and office hours regularly and be prepared for the readings.

I've had three classes with him: Chinese 155, 110A, and 110B. A lot of students take his classes thinking they are going to be easy As. Guess what? They're not and that is ok! If you learn and respect the material, it is an easy A, if you don't show up or disrespect the material, you fail, simple. Truly a knowledgeable and funny guy, no regrets!
Hard grader, attendance in class is necessary. If he doesn't like you, you rae likely to get a low score even if you got correct answers.

This man is an amazing reservoir of Chinese history and literary knowledge.  His glib of speech never fails to impress.  I love him!  He does not explain essay writing too well and expects you to cut the crap before your write it.  Also, you have to be pretty interested in the material to do well.

analysis.name: Mark Asta
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Took his time going through lecture slides to ensure all students understood concepts and was always open to questions. Homework could be challenging but was doable, and all exams were fair. Weekly bCourses quiz that was kind of easy to forget about. Asta was always willing to talk after class about the course or other engineering-related things.

The lectures were engaging and Professor Asta always supplemented it with his own walkthroughs on the chalkboard, which helped tremendously. The material was a little lacking on the ceramics and polymers side, but overall covered everything you need for an intro to materials science.

Out of town a lot, so we had two professors for this class. I liked Asta's lectures a lot more, and I wish he taught us more and wasn't out of town so often, but I get it he's very busy. In terms of the class itself, the GSI is pretty meh and the grader (Andrew Sweet) is terrible. I've never had such a bad grader in all my time at Berkeley.

analysis.name: Stephan Astourian
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: My favorite Professor at Berkeley. This man might just know everything. If you listen, take notes, and do a good amount of the reading you will get an A. He is extremely fair, he tells you exactly what to study so there are no surprises. Astourian should also pursue a career in standup comedy; his sarcastic humor will surly keep you entertained.

Had him during the pandemic - he constantly injected humor into each class and even though it was all about genocide it was never overwhelming. He had a good mix of lecture to participation for the class. Requirements were simple- 6 books to read & we were graded on two 6 page papers (25% each), one 10 page paper (40%), and participation (10%)

Professor Astourian gives you his phone number, yeah, but he wouldn't need to if his lectures were clear! He goes all over the place and only gives us a board full of undefined terms each lecture to help organize things. He was funny, but I constantly felt like I was struggling and failing to understand lecture. Not a fun experience.

He is the funniest professor I've had at Cal and his lectures won't get boring. He is an expert on the topic of genocide and is very easy to talk to if you just want to drop by his OH. He is very accessible - will even give you his phone number; so he gives you a lot of resources to do well. He is not an easy grader but he is fair.

Tied for the best prof. I have had at Berkeley. He is intelligent and brutally sarcastic. Its also great to have an argument with him. the only downer was the rest of the class. As a discussion format, the class relies heavily on participation, but almost no one participated. You will get what you put into this class.

analysis.name: Astar Winoto
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class will be hard if you do not stay on top of all the lectures. It's not hard because Professor Winoto's difficult; it's hard because immunology is so complex. Go to office hours; he will be the one of the most patient professors who really cares about his students' understanding. Ask questions during class - very willing to answer Q's.

I really liked Winoto! He is very organized and really knows what he's talking about. He holds his students to a really high standard. What he talks about is really complicated, and he does a good job considering the difficulty of the material. I really felt like I was taking an upper division course with him (which was cool)!

I actully liked Winoto. the material wasnt easy, but I went to all the lectures and paid attention, did the readings, went to office hours when i didnt understand and I did great on his section. He was very helpful at office hrs and if you actually cared to listen to his lectures and understand the the topic you would. some ppl just like to whine.

Immunology is a very hard and Winoto just makes it harder than ever to me. I have been struggling all the time. You can tell he wants to interact with students and remember everyone's names. But his teaching style and slides could improve to make the hard knowledge more accessible. Problem sets do represent exam, but the exam is harder.

tries to get to know your name! and is very conceptual/experimentally focused, and exams reflect that. like ur asian dad type of guy. he's clear and has good board work but class is just dominated by nervous pre-meds so the atmosphere is kinda 'will this be on the test' a lotta the times

analysis.name: Krste Asanovic
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Lectures are dry, but reasonably gets main points across, although material covered in lecture is only somewhat helpful for exams and homework. Theres a lot of material in this class and some of the test questions test tiny details, so be on the lookout. Lots of projects too.

Very influential figure in the field of architecture, and very knowledgeable about the details and minutiae of hardware systems. Really enjoyed the tie-ins to the current state of research and industry practices!

boring, so so boring. Basically switched from MIPs to RISC-V because he helped make it, thereby inconveniencing all of the students by making us use a language that has exactly 0 online resources in comparison to mips which you could actually google something about and expect an answer. >:(

analysis.name: Austin Hedeman
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: There is no one that compares to Hedeman. He is the best in the department by far. Amazing textbook (he wrote), amazing lectures. The homework is fun, challenging, and you learn a ton. IDC if Siddiqi is teaching and he has a 4.8, NO ONE is better than Hedeman. Hands down, the best teacher you will ever have. The most you will ever learn in a class.

Hedeman is a great professor, and QM with him is currently my personal favorite course at Berkeley. What makes his class impressive is that it is so easy to follow and understand, the exams are dirt easy (AND he gives you extra time!) and he has an online repository of week-by-week lecture notes that are as clear as day.   RECOMMENDED!!

Professor Hedeman, what can I say? Super cool, really wants to help you learn physics, well-organized. His online notes are so good and comprehensive that you don't need to go to class, but I love how he explains things in lecture. Homeworks are super easy, very straightforward and pretty neat problems! Also amazing on Piazza and exams are fair

great lecturer with a clear passion for teaching and for the subject! genuinely cares about students and is willing to advocate for them. homework can be long but is very educational. exams are 24 hour open note, can be a bit long but still reasonable. totally recommend!

Professor Hedeman is genuinely one of the best professors I have had. He is passionate about teaching and cares about his students. His lectures are great and easy to follow. I would highly recommend!

analysis.name: Maximilian Auffhammer
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Max was the funniest prof ever and guides you as many times as you need to understand material. It takes a while to absorb and practice topics on your own, but GSI's were helpful with quick responses. He is a unique prof that is hard to come across and super funny. Grading was harsh imo, but it really made you learn and be prepared for future econ

What we went over in class was often not what we were tested on, rather the problems we went over in discussion. I am neither skilled at or interested in econ, and only took it because it was required for my major That being said, professor Auffhammer made it as compelling as it could be, he's an incredibly dynamic and understanding professor.

Professor Max knows how to teach economics to people who do not understand the subject at all. He will go over subjects clearly, and if it does not make sense to you, will answer your questions either in the lecture zoom chat or office hours. He is extremely organized, with a schedule of all reading and quizzes and projects and their dates.

He's really helpful and is always up to answering questions from students. His lectures are ok, he's a funny guy but his lecture pacing is really bad. Do the readings they're more helpful honestly. He kind of also procrastinates ngl and only gave us our midterm date a week in advance which was def not enough. The final date was always changing too.

Everything you've heard about Max is true. He's hilarious, knowledgable, passionate, engaging, and overall his personality helps make the lectures more interesting. Problem Sets are okay if you watch/go to lectures. Midterms/final were a bit scary and would've been tough if it wasn't open note (Might only have been open note because it was online).

analysis.name: Yim Au
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Au is very knowledgeable and full of wisdom. Class is a heavy workload but not necessarily difficult. An interesting class! Its a little hard to understand her sometimes though  shes from Hong Kong. The GSIs were also pretty nit picky with grading and seemed like theyd knock off points wherever they could. Forced me to get a makerpass though!

Prof is alright, but lectures weren't always engaging. In this group project class, I did most of the work, yet my concerns were forgotten. Grading was unfair when others did less work for the same grade. Excessive busy work. The class size is too large for the prof to manage effectively. I recommend other design courses such as info 213.

Prof. Au is one of the best professors I've had at Berkeley! She is super passionate about design and cares for her students. Her assignments and lectures really get you thinking about design in everyday products and life.
She also gives genuine feedback on group projects that can translate over to internships/jobs. Overall I highly recommend!
Nice teacher, class was easy. I would've gotten an A but my teammates in my group are liars and told her I did no work.

Professor Au is a good professor overall; however, sometimes she struggles to explain material effectively. Because the class is one 3-hour lecture per week, there is a lot of homework. It's not particularly hard, but it is long and you have to put in a lot of work. Once you do though, you will be well rewarded and the grade will be easy.

analysis.name: Benson Au
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Benson is a really quick-speaker but his lectures are actually quite enriching. You must pay 110% effort to attend the lectures otherwise you will have to go through the boring textbook by yourself. He can easily tell a difficult problem using language you can understand. He's funny and sometimes tells dad joke but that's what makes the courese fun

Really enjoyed this class. It's definitely not easy; homework and tests were difficult. However, Prof. Benson was super helpful during both OH and class. The class is also well organized and lectures are structured well. Lectures are not recorded but Prof. references specific chapters in the textbook, so it's easy to follow along regardless.

Helpful during OH. But, lectures don't reference the textbook so if you need to reference it, it is hard to know where to look. No practice midterms, no HW solutions until the weekend before exams, exams were not fair (he even admitted this both times), goes fast in lecture, starts writing before class, no recordings, take a different course.

Lectures not worth attending and textbooks chosen have tons of mathematically relevant typos. Material clearly not being taught well since exams were not that difficult, but the class average was extremely low. Benson is smart but he doesn't seem to care at all about pedagogy. Also, no recordings, no lecture notes, no way to attend remotely.

Benson is very fair. You can tell he knows his stuff and he gives amazing, well-motivated, well-organized lectures. Tests are very fair and easier than homework assignments. He's really nice and makes himself available in office hours. I really enjoyed the class but thought it was by far the most difficult class I've taken at Berkeley

analysis.name: Aurelie Vialette
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Aurelie is a great teacher.  Class discussions and reading are interesting and fun.  Workload is manageable.

She is very tough, passionate, helpful, and beautiful. I have to say, I have probably seen more progress in this class throughout the semester than any other I had taken in the past. She is always willing to help and loves what she teaches. If you want to work hard and learn a lot take this class.

Pay attention in class and take good notes. Hard quizzes. Easy tests. The books she makes you buy are highly optional. She expects you to read it, but fully summarizes it in class the next day. She cold calls in class so make sure you make sure you read the articles before every class.

Aurelie is one of the best teachers I have ever had. She is very passionate about Spanish literature and knows a lot about it. She is intimidating at first, but as long as you do your work and participate, you will be fine. She pushes you to learn. It was a very enjoyable class.

Professor Vialette is so sweet and caring, and in particular I enjoyed this course a lot. Learning about disability in a new way really opened my eyes. The readings aren't that heavy and her tests and quizzes are easy. I recommend this class.

analysis.name: Max Auffhammer
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 55 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Max is the definition of what teaching should be like, every lecture is a pleasure to attend. He explains every concept thoroughly and with humor. By far the best professor at Cal, with a great attitude towards life. He explains everything so well that the material is absorbed easily and performance on exams shows. Highly recommend!

MAX IS AMAZING!! Although he was only able to teach 1/3 of the course due to health reason, his humor and engagement capture every student's heart! If you get a chance, make sure to take his class! Although his tests are about the standard to a difficult level, he always offers a generous curve to the student and truly cares about his students!

I feel so sad i don't get to take his classes anymore! I wish he still teaches IAS 107. I'm so impressed by his ability to explain economic very  clearly. I wasn't an economic person until i took his class. His lectures, humor, and way of teaching style completely change my perspective on economic! you'll never regret having him as your professor!
If you want a once in a lifetime experience, take him.

Max is the definition of a good professor, his lectures are always engaging and he has a great personality. The best part is that he makes the material comprehensible. His exams are well organized and the class structure is great. Overall one of the best professors at Cal hands down.

analysis.name: Awwab Bukhari
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: BEST gsi I've had at cal! super helpful & funny! even if i came late he always stayed with me after his OH & helped me with my questions. really cool, and easy to talk to. just be honest with him and tell him if you're confused, and he'll make sure you'll do really well. Tells you what he wants for a perfect A. Highly recommend any course with him!

HE'S GREAT! I didn't get the subject at all, but he walked me through everything; really nice and understanding about personal issues. If you have a problem, LET HIM KNOW!! He's always helpful. I couldn't make his office hours, so he would always accommodate, either coming super late at night or on the weekends. Very clear, and nice when grading.

DON'T LET HIM BE YOUR GSI. Figure out WHO the GSI will be for the class before taking it!! This guy is a jerk. He doesn't care about the students and his grading is completely random. He barely gives ANYONE an A (I talked friends about their grade). AVOID AT ALL COSTS. He's also really anal about everything ie. he's picky about expectations.

He's a hardass. Doesn't really care about the student at all -- just wants you to stop bugging him. Kind of arbitrary grading: he just goes off of his gut feeling in giving you a grade which is not entirely fair. He's very clear in his expectations but I didn't really like him just because he doesn't care for the student much at all.
gregor's head gsi. go to his office hours. tells you what he wants for perfect A. scary to approach, but in emails he's cool

analysis.name: Denis Auroux
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I took this class thinking that the professor is good; however, after a few lectures into the class, I realised that the professor used to be good, but not anymore. His exams are unusually tough, but the grading is fair. No matter how you perform in the class, his curve will screw you over. In my case, 15% above the average score was only a B.

His lectures are incredible and very helpful. He is a delightful man who's got some great dad jokes. Take advantage of his office hours. While most professors can be intimidating or condescending, he is extremely kind and helpful.

Auroux is a very good professor for a wide range of students. He has enough challenging problems and references to applications of material and theory to keep students who want high level material interested but he's not pretentious and I think his lectures are accessible. Tests were generally well written. He is also willing to talk to students.

Denis Auroux is definitely one of the best professors that I have ever had. He explains every concept clearly and cares about students in Math 53. On the other hand, he gives lots of homework, and in the first class he says that the best way to master math is to practice more lol. Grading is rigorous but fair. Overall he is an amazing lecturer.

AMAZING PROFESSOR! Really cares about his students. His office hours are great, more students should go. Weekly homework is pretty extensive - do NOT wait until the last second to start. Tests in retrospect are very fair, really test your understanding of the material. As long as you do the homework and grasp the concepts, you will do well.

analysis.name: Avishay Tal
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He did a lecture on Godel's Incompleteness Theorems when I requested it and despite the extremely abstract material, makes it intuitive and very interesting to motivate everything we study. Incredible dude and one of my favorite professors (and most interesting classes) ever, even if the class was tough! He's also a nice guy, if shy. Talk to him!
Really good prof who knows his stuff! Really knowledgable and gives very good and clear lecture! 172 is a tough class though!

Professor Tal's lectures are great: he is awesome at building motivation and intuition, and exceedingly clear in navigating concepts. His policies are clear and fairly generous, the course is also ran well, and his homeworks tend to be pretty interesting. A pleasure to take his classes.
Great professor and nice courses. But he seems depressed when the students feel reluctant to interact with him. Cheer up!

analysis.name: Avideh Zakhor
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Many students were robbed of better grades when the average GPA of the class in fall 2021 was 2.779. They expected to be an average of 3.2 GPA like previous semesters. I wish the grading was more lenient because of the pandemic. The only memorable quote I remember: "It's unfortunate I love delta functions. Now we named the delta variant of COVID."

I was robbed of an A- since I did better on the final exam than on the midterm. I thought I would get that grade based on previous semester distributions. But in fall 2021, the distribution was harsher. She had no accomodations for extensions of homework and labs, even with the ongoing pandemic. Again, I was robbed of a better grade.

One of the worst professors at Berkeley with absolutely no respect for students. For example, the professor said being a student is the easiest your professional career will be along with other disrespectful statements. Midterm and final were harshly graded and there were absolutely no study resources provided to students.

This process has sloppy writing and I would rather that she uses an iPad rather than a laptop to write since she has so many problems with the laptop. She doesn't understand that we are in a pandemic and that students are adjusting with a return to in person classes. She didn't include a homework or lab drop. There is emphasis on tests.

Sloppy hand writing and fast paced lectures make attending lectures(lecture recordings) really inefficient; Grind discussion worksheets and Oppenheim textbook(problems with solution) if you want to learn efficiently. Tough grader. Tests are hard, and don't exam review help. Professor is fair does her job, but don't expect anything more.

analysis.name: Avy Valladares
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He is a terrible instructor. His lectures are neither clear nor helpful, you will end up learning nothing from him. He grades harshly but never tells you what his expectations are. Never go to his office hour because all he does is telling you how stupid your paper is and ask you to figure out yourself. I strongly suggest anyone to avoid his class.

Terrible teacher, not a bad person. Lectures are incredibly confusing and very disorganized. I don't think I learned a single useful thing from the class. You might do well in the class if your writing is not bad to begin with..I'm sure there're better R1A classes Berkeley can offer you. Avoid this one.

He has very high expectations for students, yet at the same time, doesn't tell us what his criteria is, which is unreasonable. Lectures are pretty disorganized and hard to follow. He's also arrogant and not very helpful and just tells you to go figure out things yourself even during office hours. Just don't take any class under him lol.

An eccentric yet brilliant man, so beware if these kinds of people aren't your type. Hard grader, but I truly felt my writing evolved in this class. At first writing a paper longer than 3 pages sounded excruciating, but as the class went on page minimums were less terrifying. My analytical skills are also much more nuanced now. Films are also fun
take attendance every class, the grading is lenient, funny and clear lecture, bearable readings also, but do go to class with the readings read.

analysis.name: Avril Angevine
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: showing up on the class everyday ,still get the participation grade On C?the most ridiculous teacher I ever see.

What a piece of work. English was my favorite subject until I took this class my freshman year. There is no negotiating around her opinions of what your literary interpretations are, and how essays should be structured.  She stifles creativity, yelled at us in French, and often dressed inappropriately (see-through tops) on the job. Unprofessional.

Hard teacher, but VERY helpful. My writing has improved more than I would have ever imagined. We write 4 essays and a final essay. There is a lot of reading, but the books are enjoyable. Go to Ms. A for office hours and she helps writing your essay so much! She is a very smart woman. OH and don't forget to raise your hand a lot in class.

Ms. A is a nice teacher. She's strict on essays meeting certain criteria and her temper swells when the class is silent to her questions, but she's alright. It's unfortunate that she can't take criticism for her teaching and grading style and often holds the fact that she grades papers over your critiques. Sad.

She is a harsh grader, but if you meet with her, she will help a lot, and get you a good grade. I think my writing improved a lot by taking her class. Also, make sure you come to class prepared. She will get mad if you don't have your book or if there is no/very little participation throughout the class. She is pretty particular but fair.

analysis.name: Avaren Ipsen
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Took this class last year.  Very sweet lady, really cares about her students.  During lecture, goes off on wild tangents and rarely makes it through her own outline.  Coursework is light, but reading is exceptionally dense.  Attendance is 1/3 of your grade.

Avaren is one of the most accessible teachers I've ever had.  She' completely available for questions, and even had everyone over to her house after the midterm.  The exams aren't easy but she's an understanding grader, and her lectures are clear with good examples.  She's also super nice and works really hard to make sure that everyone "gets it".

Nice person, but not a good teacher. Left wing radical feminist that only gives a biased and incoherent view of social theory. Lectures can be mildly interesting, but she is not at all interested in hearing differing viewpoints. As a liberation theologian, she is constantly trying to use her interpretation of the Bible to prove some point.

Avaren's an amazing teacher.  I've never had a professor so interested in my understanding of the subject.  She goes above and beyond the call of duty, and really, REALLY knows her social theory.  Almost too well, as she can bowl you over with a lot of info if you keep pressing her.  GREAT teacher.  Highly recommended!

I had to take this class for ISF & thought I hated philosophy, but Ipsen turned me around. She makes the subject interesting, engaging, applicable to modern life, and fun. Her lectures brighten my day (thought I'd never say that about ANYthing school-related, but she's that good). 1 midterm, 1 final = pretty easy =]

analysis.name: Aya De Leon
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
This is for AFRICAM 159!!
She takes attendance every class, but has not impacted my grade. Grades until the very last week of school, so kind of frustrating when the instructions of the assignments are vague. However, there were not that many assignments. Likes to talk about her experiences a lot, so it can be droning. No office hours.

It's a great class, but requires a lot of work for an AC class and is tailored to minorities. If you are a cis-white person, I would not recommend taking this class to fulfill the AC requirement because the assignments ask to write about a lot of personal stuff and oppression and you will struggle. Also does not hold office hours

Like others have said, Aya doesn't really do anything in the class, but from what I understand, she does decide how the class is run. As a warning, the class is a lot of work...way too much in my opinion. If you like poetry, though, it can be fun too.

Everyone involved with P4P acts like they're so out to fight oppression in all forms, but in reality it's filled with politics.  If you're good the other students try to knock you down on their way to the top in their quest to become famous writers. My STP was manipulative, others harass you to feel powerful.  Aya is fair weather like all the rest.

Aya will be on maternal leave for spring 2010, but this class will still run the same because it's mainly taught by STPs, student teach poets. Overall this class was alot of fun, but the lectures got repetitive and dull near the end. You will hear alot of "isms," but i recommend this class for those who have any interest in poetry.

analysis.name: Ozlem Ayduk
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Lectures very straight forward, though attendance is kind of necessary because she goes over a lot of research data that are later on in the midterms. No papers, and midterm grading scale is lenient. Overall, an interesting class with lots of memorization and common sense. Textbook reading wasn't really necessary,midterm based off of lectures.

She is a great professor. Funny, interesting, and very knowledgeable. The class became more interesting as the semester progressed, mainly because she was more animated during lectures. Definitely recommend this class with her. You will learn a lot about yourself and others.

this class is recorded, only required attendance in section. the review made on may 2025 is false. GSIs held outside review sessions & proctoring of exams. straightforward with exam content & practice questions scattered through lectures easy A+

no unprofessional comments made but students talked abt bombing her reviews in the class evaluations :/

Prof A is great! but often takes a step back and lets the GSI's run the class. I've never been in a class where it felt that instructors did not want students to succeed. The exams are more difficult then necessary, and unprofessional comments made before the exams make it more stressful. I'd only recommend this course if the structure improves.

She is great! She is very knowledgeable and seems very approachable. The tests are not hard if you read & attend lectures. I learned a lot in this. Not only about the subject but also about myself. Her research is interesting. She covers all theorists pretty well, shows she is a reasonable person. Some ppl only like to put their view out. Recommend

analysis.name: Ayelet Ben-Yishai
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She was really helpful in office hours-- go to them!! Her class really helped me learn how to write a thesis and essay. She grades on improvement so if you get A's from the start you're making it harder for youself.  the literature and theme she chose was so-so. I think she's in Israel but if she ever comes back, i recommend her class for R1A/B

I really enjoyed this class. 5 papers: 3 original, 2 revised. GO TO OFFICE HOURS. They were SO helpful - she is very receptive, encouraging, insightful. Come with ideas and she will give you so much direction. Grades fairly and on improvement. Work hard on your essays because improvement is key to getting an A.
I enjoy every lecture to the max with Dr. Ben-Yishai. She inspires and motivates all of her students in a creative manner.

analysis.name: Ayyana Chakravartula
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Chakravartula is the worst professor I have had at UC Berkeley. She made an extremely difficult class even worse. The lectures are a scramble to copy down a million formulas with no  logical derivation and attempt to apply them on an exam. The exams are a culmination of the most random and difficult material from the lectures.

She seems like a nice and caring professor, at first. She is a harsh grader, often taking off half-credit for minor mistakes. I got average on the first midterm, well above average on the second midterm and final, nearly perfect lab score, did all my homework, and ended with a B

At first glance, she seems to be a nice, caring professor. Wrong move, buddy. Although her lectures are clearly organized, she doesn't provide students with notes, and she structures the class so students have no feedback on their performance before exams. Also her tests are graded to give students half credit if they make calculator errors. AVOID

Just a lecturer at Cal. Ridiculously tough grader. Puts hella equations on the board and just expects us to memorize them all. Lets you bring a cheat sheet to tests BUT THERE ARE SO MANY EQUATIONS. I would say the best way to pass this class is to be Chakravartula herself, because no one knows what she's thinking or what is important.

This class was pretty interesting, and i feel like the topics are useful for industry. The tests in the class, however, are tough to prep for. It often comes down to how much you can fit on the cheat sheet. She sometimes puts up equations during class that she doesn't explain, but are on the exams. Individual lab reports can get very tedious.

analysis.name: Ayla Algar
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Ayla is an extremely caring and dedicated teacher. She knows the Turkish language, culture, and people very well, and is enthusiastic about giving her students a good understanding of it. She teaches a well-balanced class, she expends lots of effort, and is always available outside of class to help.
Ayla is a very caring person and is always willing to help outside of class.

analysis.name: Azin Seraj
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment:
Professor Seraj is incredible. I took her Beginning Video course (Art 012). Very engaging and hands on with the course content. Down to earth and has very inspiring lectures.
Easy grader and allows you to resubmit projects to get a higher grade than the one you got. 10/10 Professor, would take again!

Very interesting lectures, not much guidance but a lot of encouragement when it came to projects. She was not very strict on grading and very understanding when I had to miss a lot of classes due to illness and mental health issues.
Very helpful, funny, and genuine.

analysis.name: Babak Ayazifar
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 103 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: I believe it has something to do with the course structure a bit disorganised due to the recent reform, I have to admit it'd be impossible for me to follow along lectures let alone those “creative” exams without previous foundations in linear algebra. Very chill guy though; require more studying to really go down his trail of thought.

Prof Ayazifar's EE16A was challenging, and I didn't enjoy it much unlike other reviews. The long, late evening lectures made paying attention tricky and prohibited me from attending any clubs. Interacting in lectures felt intimidating, and reviewing material was tedious without a textbook and lecture notes being delayed to post to Ed.

Very interesting lectures that flowed well.  Exams are really hard either in time crunch or just difficulty of material but with clobber policy all hope is not lost.  Definitely would recommend 16a with him because we lays a great foundation for any higher level classes and their thinking.

I love Babak! He is a great teacher and one of the best! 16A class is difficult, which is too be expected, but he makes it interesting and engaging. His lectures are also pretty funny and I felt like he truly cared about his students. Would recommend.
I haven't even finished this course yet and I can tell this guy is a great professor. He genuinely cares for his students and wants them to succeed. I'd vote for Babak if he ran for president.

analysis.name: Milton Azevedo
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He has a tendency to go off on random tangents, but overall this course was very easy, as there was only a midterm, a final presentation, and a final paper.  He does have a wealth of knowledge on linguistics, so if this is a field that is of interest to you, take a class with Azevedo.  You'll get used to his Brazilian Spanish accent soon enough.

This professor avoids answering to questions clearly. Sometimes I feel as if he was mocking us. You have to read the book in order to learn the material. You have to teach yourself what is covered in class for the most part.

He stands alone!  He is one of the few professors who actually listens to his students and supports them.  He is very personable and charming.  You will learn more than just the standard fare in the course description.  His demeanor and humor make the drudgery of learning a pleasure.  He's an excellent professor!!!
Clear, articulate, smart with an infectious passion for linguistics. His classes were a pleasure.
A very encouraging and great professor. Gave a great insight to things I never thought before.

analysis.name: Daniel Barsky
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: His lectures are alright. The content is mostly verbal and his slides are not very helpful. The content covered in class does not feel thorough at all, but attendance is still mandatory... The best thing to do is self-study if you're already enrolled in his lecture. If not, don't take it.

This is for Physics 8B. An absolutely horrible professor. Lectures unorganized slides and he did no problems in class to help during exams. Practice problems would be "water is wet" and exam would be "calculate the quantum data from within the black hole from interstellar". Mandatory 4 hour discussions too. Avoid at all costs. Good person tho.

Ps this is for physics 8B, but I couldn't select that. He looks to get to know people and is super responsive and welcoming on ed discussion, but he just doesn't know how to make physics clear. Slides are disorganized and he goes too fast and way too technical. Averages on all tests were F's, but he has extra credit and is accommodating

Professor Barsky is one of the best professors I've had. He's what I hope scientists strive to be; curious about science and wants his students to learn. There are always less desirable things in certain classes, and 5BL and 5CL are no different (lots of work), but my experience was significantly better with him as a professor. Highly recommend.

This is meant for 8B, do not take him. The lectures are so disorganized, the practice midterms always have mistakes in them and the actual midterms too. He doesn't do examples during lecture. I love his passion for physics though.

analysis.name: Americ Azevedo
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 50 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This was a good class to take; I would recommend it. It's only one hour a week, and there are minimal writing assignments. It's a useful class if you need another unit, or if you want to learn about meditation.

Meditation was the class that saved me from breaking down completely during this semester. There's just something about having a safe, quiet, and peaceful place to sit and just do nothing that gives a sense of centeredness in your life. It was nice being away from the frazzled Berkeley study life for a while. Definitely going to take it again.

Extraordinary use of student power in dialogue--sat in a circle as opposed to facing the teacher, learned much more in this class than I have in many classes at Cal, was an amazing class--had the opportunity to plan and sketch out a "vision," start putting it into action, obtain peer review, read a few great books and discuss them

This is one of the most amazing professors I have had at Cal.  He is inspiring and thought provoking.  The class is taught exactly as a meditation class should be - relatively hands off with just the right amount of guidance, zero stress, and no extra work.  Take this class whether or not you have ever had any interest in meditation.

This is one of the most amazing professors I have had at Cal.  He is inspiring and thought provoking.  The class is taught exactly as a meditation class should be - relatively hands off with just the right amount of guidence, zero stress, and no extra work.  Take this class whether or not you have ever had any interest in meditation.

analysis.name: Balthazar Beckett
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
Dr B is the goat. Here are some reasons why:

A) He's down to earth and understanding. Super accommodating for extensions and stuff like that.

B) Gives you great feedback during office hours + for *mandatory* essay revisions (you're guaranteed to get a better grade if you follow his feedback).

C) Only caveat is you have to read A LOT.

Dr. B is truly one of the most amazing professors I've had here at Berkeley. I wouldn't say that I am the strongest writer, but his input and care made it so that I improved drastically in the time while in his class. His lectures were fascinating, and I enjoyed coming to class everyday. Participate participate participate!!!
Class discussions were genuinely interesting, genuinely one of the most caring professor I've taken. I looked forward to coming to class. A decent amount of work for an r1b but very manageable

Professor Beckett is very organized, and puts lots of thought and care into lectures and the syllabus. He lets you turn in a rough first draft and gives thorough feedback so you can revise your papers and get a better grade. Lectures have an interesting mix of media and topics, and are never boring. Very nice and accessible for help or feedback.

Grades essays harshly. You submit a rough draft first, he picks out a few things for you to fix, and he gives a new grade based on what you fixed. But in my experience, even when I fixed everything he pointed out, I still received a poor grade. 
He certainly does not set his expectations clearly enough. 
He gives TOO MUCH reading.
Quite political.

analysis.name: Diana Bautista
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: No real practice exams (can never know what to expect), exam info gets released super late, lack of transparency about course logistics, virtually unresponsive on Ed and email, stringent regrade policy, and hyper-specific rubrics so its impossible to get a 100%. GSIs also don't know what professors are expecting, so there's no one to ask for help.
This class was the hardest class ever. The exams were so difficult, zero curve, and felt absolutely hopeless.

Prof. Bautista is super nice and excited to teach - she gives good lectures (but not a lot of details are on her slides so be sure to actually attend them and take notes). Her midterm and final section were easy and straightforward and the material is interesting!

She was a pretty okay lecturer; taught by the slides. I got about 80% on the first test because I wasn't fastidious enough about taking notes (the slides were pretty much the guide to the course content), and because I wasn't specific enough about what was actually happening. I think the GSIs did most of the grading, though.

Bautista is one of the worst lecturers I've ever had. Her slides are almost entirely pictures and her descriptions of the images suggest she's just as lost as you are. The organization of lectures is also extremely jumbled and hard to follow. Although nice when talking one-on-one, the course seemed designed to make things as difficult as possible.

analysis.name: Hannes Bajohr
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: One of my favorite professors and classes at Berkeley by far! Definitely felt like I graduated having learned some of the most profound lessons in Bajohr's class. He's super approachable and office hours were amazing learning opportunities! Would definitely take more classes with him if I could!

Truly an awesome professor. Totally echo the person that said that this is the kind of professor/class that they came to Berkeley for, I felt the same way! There was a lot of difficult reading but Prof. Bajohr is very helpful and any expectations are made very clear.

The kind of class I came to Berkeley for. Best one I've taken, loved the material & readings, liked interdisciplinary aspect. Required reading responses (3/w) but not too much time, help engage with the material. Prof very knowledgeable, loved guest speakers he brought in! Projects/essays were really interesting, out of the box. Changed my life fr.
Evidently very knowledgeable and passionate about the subject material. Readings were interesting and well-curated. Cool guest speakers. Would recommend!

analysis.name: Geronimo Barrera de la Torre
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The class was easy, especially since I had pervious gis knowledge but I would say it would be easy to someone completely new at it too. The grading consisted of 5 reading reflections, 5 quizzes on gis activities, a final map, and a final essay. The lectures were not very helpful and often a bit boring, but the lab section more than makes up for it.

Amazing introductory class for QGIS. Took it with zero previous experience & it was very manageable & interesting. Awesome GSIs & the final project is just making your own map, but there's lots of support and time for completing it. Lectures were mostly whole class discussion of the readings. Attend lab so quizzes are easier!

Professor Barrera's lectures are more often than not based on the readings. There are lab assignments, 5 quizzes that are really easy if you attend lab, and a couple of voice recording assignments on the readings (which you don't really have to do if they aren't for an assignment although you will need to reference them in your final essay).
It says lecture is mandatory but it isn't really. The lectures and readings are interesting so I recommend you show up. He is a really nice professor.

analysis.name: Lee Bernstein
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Bernstein is an awesome lecture and really passionate about the material. However, the class has really a lot of material to cover, and he often doesnt have time to explain how to actually approach problems in class. Also, the class is crosslisted as a grad class, so dont feel discouraged if half the class seems to know the material way better.

Few are as passionate or capable as Prof. Bernstein. He pushes students to understand experimental design and the underlying, fundamental physics at work. I have taken a few different Reaction/Radiations Labs, but this was by far the most organized, high-level, and most put together course I have come across. An essential class for any NE major.

One of the most passionate and inspiring professors I've ever had the pleasure to be taught by. His enthusiasm for the course material is incredible, and his desire to help students is unending. His exams are quite difficult but are curved according to class performance

Lee is a great person, and you should probably take a lecture with him if you have the chance. Unfortunately, the lecture material and the course material often diverge and it isn't immediately clear as to what he asks of you to know for his assignments and lectures. The class doing well is honestly dependent on the GSI doing well in recitations.
Professor Bernstein gives amazing lectures, and is supportive of his students throughout the course of the semester.

analysis.name: Belinda Kremer
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Really tough grader and can't even explain why she gave the grade she gave. HORRIBLE at the feedback and has ridiculously high expectations from freshman just out of high school. Expects you to write like a scholar when you are there to learn. Very condescending and impatient. Go to OH and get disappointed. TAKE AT YOUR OWN RISK!
This professor, quite literally, will find any reason to critique and belittle your writing. Very condescending and passive aggressive with such high expectations. Save yourself the exhaustion.

I rated her before and don't know why everything has been taken down but for the sake of your mental health DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HER. Absolutely horrible teacher with nooooo compassion for her students, rude and TERRIBLE at explaining things. She expected us to know everything and then wouldn't help or answer questions. Save yourself!!

not the worst, she can be nitpicky but otherwise isn't an extremely hard grader. i do agree that her personality is a bit strong at times but as long as you stay on her good side/do what you're asked, you'll get through this class fine--class itself was meh content-wise, personally didn't have any issues with her, complaints are valid though

I am here to warn the public. This professor is the worst professor I've ever had. Literally have MINIMUM of 9 hours of work outside the class. She acts like this is the only class us students have, it's insane. Also not to mention if you miss class, its over for you. This class made my mental health worse. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! ITS NOT WORTH IT!

analysis.name: Jennifer Bergner
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 80 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Bergner goes over some hard content with confidence and detail. She taught the first two units which are fairly hard if you come in with only AP chemistry knowledge. However, it would be intuitive to grasp if you follow her lectures.
Bergner was an awesome professor to start your College of Chemistry journey! She conducts really fun experiments and lectures at the perfect pace and gives substantial practice for midterms.

Bergner is an incredibly fair lecturer and exam writer. Her lectures were always clear and easy to follow (though her soothing voice made it difficult to stay awake at times). Go through her chem quizzes to study for exams as her exam questions are around a similar level to them, and do all practice problems available to you!!!!

Professor Bergner is owesome! She presents the material in a clear and organized way, and her slides are super helpful, with questions that reinforce the content. The class is challenging, but she genuinely wants her students to succeed and is always ready to help during office hours. Highly recommend attending them if you need extra clarification!

The tests are on completely different levels of difficulty compared to past exams, assignments, her lectures, and practice problems. You don't even know what to study since they were all different. But the lectures are very engaging and interesting. If you don't care about the grades and want to really enjoy chemistry learning, this is the class.

analysis.name: Becky Hsu
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Becky was an amazing professor who really cared for her students. Becky would always give specific feedback on papers and would walk you through the process. Not too difficult as long as you show up to class since there are in class assignments and they are a big part of your grade, attendance is mandatory.

prof Becky is absolutely amazing! she is funny and truly cares for her students, such a sweet teacher. would bring snacks to class too. just make sure you go to lectures, read the materials, do homework on time and take her feedback into account. really enjoyed the course!
Not only a kind and excellent mentor, but also an amazing human being. Love her to bits. 100% recommend taking any courses she teaches— she's a ray of sunshine and a joy to be taught by.

Becky is a great professor who truly pushes you to step out of your comfort zone so you can actually grow. You're going to walk out a totally different person than when you first came into the class. The classroom felt more like a community.

Dr. Hsu was one of the best professor I have had here at Berkeley. She is the sweetest person and energetic. She is very open on helping her students one on one and never brings anyone down. Her class was always my favorite to go to.

analysis.name: Ben Porter
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Aforementioned comment is very accurate. However, I took the final it does require a great deal of memorization. For example, SAQout of 38 cities, only 8 cities are on the test. Alongside with fill in the blank and unfair, tricky MC questions. The photo IDs was okay, prof chooses 5 out of 20 pictures. Despite the exams, there are two projects&quiz.

The semester just started, but I'm already loving his class! Lectures are fun, homework is fair, and it's so clear that he cares about students. I'm excited for the rest of the semester and can't wait to take more of his classes in the future!

Professor Porter is an expert in his field and makes it easy for anyone of any major to understand. The course material has ups and downs of interesting and boring at times. His lectures are well put together yet can be boring at times (1.5 hrs). Class is extremely easy, midterm and final were take home with averages in the 90s, (class not curved).

Great prof, although sometimes lectures were a little boring with the amount of info thrown at you, but the content is interesting. attendance is key and mandatory (no recorded lectures). the GSIs are the chillest people and are an extremely valuable resource to succeed in this class. overall, great class, def take if you can

The class itself is interesting, but the lectures can be a bit boring. Attendance is mandatory. Professor Porter is super nice, and is clearly very educated and knows a lot about this topic. Easy A; reccomend taking.

analysis.name: Bharathy Rajulu
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Deeply kind professor who wants her students to do well. We took a field trip to Fremont where we visited a Tamil school and then got Dosa Hut afterwards. This was at 8 a.m. on a weekend, but most of the class went. Really tells you about how caring she is, fun her class is, and how she creates a community. Could not recommend more.
Great overall experience will go on to take Telugu 1B in coming semesters.

She is one of the best teachers I have had at Berkeley so far! Really enjoyed the low stress environment that she provided to be able to learn Tamil really well. Would highly recommend for a really awesome non-judgemental teacher :)

I took Tamil101A with Professor Bharathy my first semester at Berkeley, and it was the best decision I could have made! I went to Tamil school growing up, so I knew how to read and write, but this helped me get better. We had so many fun projects and assignments! Plus, she's the absolute best and wants nothing more than for us to learn and do well.

She's the best! I really did not understand much Tamil before, but after her class, I feel so much more confident in my speaking. She is really forgiving with academic stuff because she just wants you to succeed! I once failed a quiz so hard that I did not even receive a %. I went to office hours, she taught me the material, and let me retake! Best

analysis.name: Karenjot Bhangoo Randhawa
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I took this course pass/fail for my breadth requirement because I'm a math major. Lectures are not interesting. Most of class time is spent doing easy group projects. My biggest complaint is that the material on the exam was NEVER discussed in class. There were lots of readings that I never did and I wrote a lot of BS on the final and still passed!

Professor Randhawa's class was very focused and heavily relied on participation. She genuinely cares about her students, so be prepared to work on group projects, attend seminars, and more. Arriving late may result in being called out. Exams were pretty lengthy- all FRQ questions. Overall, great class- I personally found her funny and informative.

amazing prof with fascinating career history and massive passion for her job. will help you network and connect with people in anything you're interested in. clear grading standards. go to office hours.

Profesor Karen is amazing-- I learned so much in her class. I felt like all of the assignments were very practical, and she did her best to help us succeed. The midterm was definitely challenging, but as long as you really understand the readings, you'll be fine. Assignments included presentations, mock mediations, and papers.

Very nice professor but the lectures were very dry and very monotonous and so. much. reading. 1 group presentation, negotiations, papers, midterm, & final. This class called for a lot; if you're looking to take this course for the philosophy breadth requirement & don't have much interest in this subject, I'd consider taking a different class.

analysis.name: Rakesh Bhandari
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 57 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Easy grader--can get by without reading much. Makes time for students, holds review sessions, indicates what will be tested, and makes it as easy as possible to do well in the class. Still, his dedication to and understanding of his students is inspirational. He restored my faith in humanity even after the subject matter shook it. Thanks, B

Professor Rakesh is a fantastic guy. His lecture is very interesting and always caught students think deeply. Even though he will assign a lot of reading, the books are meaningful and sometimes change your attitude toward the world. I will definitely retake his class if I have the chance.

I very much enjoyed his class. He doesn't always give you the books as a file but you can easily find them online or just pay attention in lecture if you can. He really tries to have an engaging conversation about the book for that module. Honestly it's an really easy class and very fun if you pay attention. All exams are also open note too!

I think people who took ISF 100D spring 25 needs to learn how to be more respectful. Even if you did not enjoy the structure of the class, the topics themselves are very interesting and you are guaranteed to succeed in the class if you pay attention, show up and dont spend the class with your nose in your laptop. Have empathy and be kind, not rude.

no clear grading criteria, no feedback on midterms. hardly gives information about final essay or tests in general until pretty recently before, and then contradicts his online instructions with random things he says dropped in a 2-hour lecture that no one really pays attention to. Wish I could like this class more than the structure allowed me to!

analysis.name: Bharathwaj Muthuswamy
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Maybe it's because I took the class over the summer, but it seemed like he dumbed down the class until it was no longer useful. Getting 100% on the final wasn't even impressive. His lectures were tedious and unhelpful.

Had him for a comp sci class at TCNJ. He flew threw though a lot of the material during lectures and they weren't the clearest, but he is a very lenient grader and will not try to trick you on exams. Overall a good professor and would take the class again with him

Bart is the best teacher I've had at Berkeley and he's only a grad student!!!!  Lectures are clear and helpful although handwriting a little sloppy.  Tests have reasonable questions similar to homework.  Labs are super short and easy.  Grading scale is fixed so 90% is an A.  Overall, it was a pretty easy and enjoyable class

Ok teacher. The class itself sucks more than Jenna Jameson, but since its a requirement for BioE's, ME's, and Chem E's, there's not much choice. Back to Bart though, he's not bad. He makes it pretty clear what he expects of students, and puts reasonable problems on his tests.

analysis.name: Nayantara Bhatnagar
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Lectures are pointless. HW was only 20% of grade. She makes the final worth 70% of your grade if you do well, so that's a good chance for you to get a good grade in the class. I personally found the class very challenging as a business student and she was of little help. I would take another professor if I could.

WARNING! if you do want to learn something but not teaching yourself, avoid her! She does have knowledge, but she doesn't know how to teach. The mid-terms are different story than the homework or even from the bk. Moreover, her hand writings are kind of hard to read; also, she speaks soft.

Her lectures are pretty dull and hard to listen (she speaks softly).  Go to section, it's pretty useful, makes HW be 30% of grade.  Her test are not that hard, but her probability one was HARD, just read the book, and go to section and you'll be fine
She makes the materials more confusing. Avoid her!

Considering that Intro Statistics is a rather dry subject, the professor was fairly clear and interesting. She did speak in a soft voice, but she used a microphone. Homework was helpful in preparing us for the exams. Exams were fair. Overall, a good class and a very nice prof. I would recommend her!

analysis.name: Bharati Mukherjee
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I had this teacher years ago but I still tell stories about how bad the workshop experience was.  She let things get really negative.  Students were the ones who stepped in to say the class was being unduly harsh.  I also know people who stopped writing because of her.  I did learn things, but thought the class unnecessarily cruel.

Prof. Blaise (AKA Prof. Mukherjee) was a wonderful creative writing teacher.  She has a lot of experience to share, and she's really, really nice.  Her voice almost put me to sleep though - she's got this story-teller voice with a nice accent and it triggered a naptime response everything I heard it.  Great class.  Take it.

One of my favorite classes I've ever taken. Gives creative options to all papers, doesn't like finals so gives papers instead (awesome!), beautiful voice, great writer herself, and my absolute favorite book list of all time
She tended to lecture nearly the entire time, rather than encouraging class discussions.  However, she does offer a unique perspective (that of a writer) to the materials covered.
She is SO RUDE, especially when you stop by during office hours...doesn't seem interested in students...or teaching...so why is she there? to pay the mortgage I guess...

analysis.name: Leonard Bjeldanes
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This course was interesting, learning about drugs, diet, cancer, toxicology, chemicals, etc. There are 3 main professors, teaching 3 different modules. Each "quiz" for Midterms 1 and 2 and the final were 30-40 ?s. If you studied, looked over the notes, and the GSI's review and practice questions, then this class is easy. The final only had 40 ?s!!

Bjeldanes' lecturing was clear and some of the topics were truly interesting. His "quiz" was the hardest out of all the lecturers. The other lecturers were not as good (some of their powerpoints aren't that clear, so you should go to lecture), but the class as a whole was pretty easy. The final was only like 30 multiple choice questions.

Bjeldanes is dry, boring, and monotonous. He only teaches part of the course (the first and last few weeks), and his teaching style is basically reading off of a powerpoint (which often contained grammatical errors...). If you're taking this to fulfill the BS requirement, it's fine, you don't even need to show up to lecture to pass.

Clear, approachable, and very organized! I highly recommend his toxicology course. Only downside - notes were on powerpoint and had the usual pitfalls - LOTS of info, sometimes verging into boring and overwhelming

An interesting and funny lecturer, his slides are clear and easy to follow, the midterm is multiple choice, and pulled almost exactly out of his slides. The other NST11 professors are less so, so be careful.

analysis.name: Belen Bistue
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Bistue is an excellent and deeply caring professor who genuinely wants to see her students grow as writers. I would recommend her R1A class to anyone who truly wants to become a strong academic writer, but not to those looking for an easy A. She is a tough grader, but she consistently provides thoughtful and detailed feedback.

nice prof, kinda hard on grading so i recommend going to office hours. only 2 full essays, 1 being your final that you can rewrite. not too many assignments either, but she is a tough grader, overall she's caring and passionate and often gives extensions and extra credit, just participate and don't skip
Great prof, super caring and understanding. Reasonable grading, useful feedback. She is accessible and very willing to help you write and succeed in this class. She deserves a 5/5.

One of the best professors for R1B. The topic is interesting, readings for most classes but they are fairly short. She genuinely cares about students' ideas, and has great energy. Each class has a short assignment that you complete in groups. 2 essays that she allows revisions on + 1 presentation. Amazing professor and person. Take this class!

Awesome professor. Cares about students, super accommodating, and gives clear and concise feedback w/o grading harshly. Not an unreasonable amount of reading. If you participate in class you're pretty much guaranteed an A.

analysis.name: Robert Birgeneau
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Really nice guy, but really awful class. Almost impossible to hear, very messy handwriting. Test heavy grading and averages far under the other class. Homework is all calculation based, but tests are theory heavy and the formula sheet is basically useless. Very disorganized and almost zero support material. Labs are easy but not very helpful.

Don't take physics 7b with him, take it with any other prof that is offered. He is an incredibly slow lecturer and goes on confusing tangents and makes the midterms and exams so hard that the average is usually below 50%. Seems like a nice smart guy but just not a good teacher. Better off just reading textbook than going to class

This class made me have my first panic attack (for reference both of my parents passed in high school). So disorganized, no one knows what's going on including the GSIs. Textbook and a good GSI are yours best friend (loved Lia). Discussion problems help with the tests. Also no cheat sheet and the equation sheet gives you nothing.

The tests are unreasonably hard, very low averages with unhelpful cheat sheets. The prof is nice and obviously smart but unable to teach their knowledge in a way that helps students learn. I would highly recommend searching for another 7B professor. If you do take this class, the textbook will be your best friend.

Lectures were okay - always had to read the textbook to understand the material. He tells stories about famous friends during lecture which is pretty cool. Tests are very derivation based (which is good!). ALWAYS practice on his old tests before his exams, EXTREMELY helpful (since they are very similar). If you study & do your work, you will be ok!

analysis.name: Karl Van Bibber
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This is most likely the best class I'll every take within Berkeley. I took this course as a non-engi major but the lectures are so diverse and interesting. Basically no homework (1 discussion post per week), mid-term, and final. The mid-term and final were reasonable essay+proj. A class that you can actually enjoy learning without being stressed.

Prof is the goat. Class consisted of a guest lecturer discussing a topic every week and tying it back to ethics. The course itself is made up of attendance, discussion posts and a group project. Super fun class, take this!

Homework problems from the book were easy, but the problems he makes up were very conceptual and difficult, and accounted for the most points. He's enthusiastic (goes on physics tangents a lot) and will answer questions thoroughly. Concepts can be confusing since he skims the basics. Exams were very difficult (generous curve) so study the lectures.

A great teacher. His test always had one hard abstract problem that would throw a lot of people. He's very very enthusiastic about getting student involved and overall was a great teacher. His explanations were sometimes a little confusing but in the end he'll make sure you know the subject. Make sure you know "conflict of interest"
No HW, amazing guest lectures, no exams. Only a few supplementary assignments, and a final project. Highly recommend.

analysis.name: Terri Bimes
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Honors is a one of a kind experience and Professor Bimes is a cheerleader every step of the way, very approachable, and gives great feedback.

She is a very kind, approachable professor. She is very knowledgeable and passionate about what she teaches. Her slides are HORRIBLE, however. Her lecture structure, in turn, is disorganized and can be hard to follow, as others have mentioned. It is not a hard class, however. Readings are straightforward and exams are practical.
