I wrote my honors thesis in political science, of which Professor Bimes was an advisor. I've heard she's normally chill, but we had a few bumps in the road. I think it was due to a lot of variables not necessarily either of our fault. I'd be willing to take a class with her and see how she is in a classroom setting.

Professor Bimes is very knowledgeable on her subject. The class was enjoyable, with a heavy emphasis on group discussion. She grades fair. If you are interested in the subject you will be in good hands.

If you don't want to devote your LIFE to reading, dont take this class. Theres a 700 page reader, a 200 page book and then another book that you read half the articles out of. Bimes is very nice and helpful. Most of the class believed the grading was pretty harsh for exams. You learn quite a bit about the office though.

analysis.name: Thomas Biolsi
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof def cares about his course & shares a lot about his research. He is nice & gives great feedback in office hours. He also cares about timeliness—he's willing to give extensions per his syllabus but don't show up late for class or leave early. This class requires some light-moderate reading (for an upperdiv), all materials are on bCourses.

He is the best professor I've ever had in college! He cares deeply about his students and will devote time outside of class to meet with you and help you understand the material. His enthusiasm for Native American studies really shines through. Take his class! You won't regret it.

Thomas Biolsi is not the most engaging professor & tends to go off on tangents often; however, he is very knowledgeable and is very open to discussion in class. There are 5, 5-paged papers for this class and you are expected to incorporate lecture material & readings into the papers (maximum 6 readings per week). Grading is average.

Tom is kind, humble, and easy going professor-- he genuinely cares for his students. There is five essays and he is a bit of a tough grader. He is selective with the wording in essays. He gives us detailed feed back on how we can improve on each essay. There is a lot of books that need to be read. He has made me in a better writer I can say.

He goes off topic so much and has revised our syllabus 5 times to accommodate for how behind he gets. Lots of readings that are very dense. Lecture attendance isn't mandatory but is needed to connect readings for papers. 3 papers in total. Very picky about how he wants papers written so I suggest you run ideas by him in office hours.

analysis.name: Bill Fanning
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Bill teaches section & is considered an add-on prof, so he isn't the official lecturer FYI.  Would highly recommend avoiding his section. A bad teacher who values smooth-talkers over insight. In a class that should promote creativity and participation, he rudely shuts down your ideas/comments. Had my phone out ONE time and he lowered my grade...

Professor Fanning is definitely one of the best marketing professors here at Berkeley. I learned a lot of really core concepts and he did a great job at bringing in a lot of guest lectures! This class definitely thought me to think creatively. It wasn't as technical as I expected though so if you're looking for that, this isn't the class.

Professor Fanning is my favorite Haas marketing professor after having taken 3 of his classes. Very caring,  super straight forward with exceptions and assignments, has great projects with clear criteria, and fantastic guest speakers. Would highly recommend all of his classes!

I really don't understand the hate for this course. Consumer Insights was by far the best course I've taken in college! The professor is passionate and values perspectives of all backgrounds. The material is a really interesting mix of psychology and marketing. Great for anyone looking to go into consumer insights, UX research, market research, etc

So boring. This is not an engaging class like others said. Also, the grading in this class is ridiculous, the GSI will literally do anything to mark points off, and not give you a full score on anything. The lectures are mandatory, and pointless, though I will say the guest lectures in this class were very good, and helpful.

analysis.name: David Bilder
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I really enjoyed Bilder's cell biology portion. Not only is he a brilliant lecturer who knows how to describe cellular processes with the right words and analogs, but he simplifies the material well. His lectures are straightforward, but his exams require you to think outside the box and draw heavily upon the concepts. Overall, I recommend!

He is a great lecturer and makes the material even more interesting than it is. He only used slides and also showed some short clips to help our understanding. His exam was VERY long and much more complicated than I expected, the over all average was low. But a very interesting class and subject.
Uses chalk!  Teaches the material as a story, focusing on concepts and the way things were discovered as opposed to boring factoids.

analysis.name: Biwen Zhang
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Made this course a lot easier to understand and you can tell that she really cares about the future of her students. I would 100% take a class with her again. Would give her above a 5 if I could, extremely fair grader and you get cheat sheets on the exams. The grading is exam heavy but she does a great job preparing you for success.

Truly wonderful professor -- one of Haas' best. Dr. Zhang cares deeply for all students and rewards those who put in the effort. Her lectures are accessible and consistently engaging. Dr. Zhang's passion is clear in the personality she adds to every single lecture. Amazing experience and a must-take for anyone who wants some accounting experience.

Biwen was awesome! The tests were very easy, and you get a note sheet. On top of that, she curves the final heavily so even if you bomb it, you'll still get a decent grade. Only 4 hws the whole semester, and they were all quick and easy. Beware of cold calling in class though. Take her if you can.

She really tries her best to teach accounting in the simplest, easiest way possible at a (honestly, a little bit too) slow pace. She cold-calls but makes it fun somehow, and she brought in alumni accounting professionals 3-4 times during the semester. Gives out candy and even gift cards for Kahoot. She's also just a super amazing person all around.

Biwen is an excellent professor for those who are learning accounting for the first time, she really broke it down as much as she could during lectures. The course was very well run and I took away a lot from this class. 

The only thing I'd gently caution students is that 85% of your grade is determined by your performance in the midterm + final

analysis.name: Jim Bishop
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 37 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Absolutely one of the most horrible classes I've ever taken at Berkeley. I took this course as a breadth, which I expected to be interesting and easy. This professor made the materials so hard and so boring. I late changed this class to PNP, but honestly just don't take it.

I looked forward to going to Oceans every day. The material and lectures are interesting and enjoyable. I felt like this class taught me a lot. There are 6 assignments, 3 field trips/creative assignments, and 2 midterms. An average amount of effort will get you an A.

Prof. Bishop is a nice person and is very enthusiastic about the material, but listening to him can be really exhausting as he often loses his train of thought or doesn't complete sentences. Easy class, but lecture was a drag.

Prof Bishop's lectures do tend to feel monotonous at times, but he cares about his students, explained things well, and had many chances to boost grades, ex. having extra credit for attendance, and redoing questions on the exams. There were few homework assignments, and the GSI walked us through the steps to do them. Take chem before this class tho

The content of this class was not very difficult but every time Jim spoke in his monotone voice, it fell flat on many ears and caused a lot of students to just have to learn on their own. Especially true for the latter part of this class in which more difficult material was "taught" but it was just more and more confusing with little explanation.

analysis.name: Joshua Blumenstock
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Great and challenging class with thorough problem sets. Strong first principles learning (building key causal and ML algorithms from scratch without packages), followed by applying modern packages to novel datasets (usually policy as per his research/labs). I'm glad I struggled through it as I learned a ton
Hes one of the best profs at Cal. Evidently he really cares about his work and make sure students learn the materials in a more intuitive way than many math and cs profs.
I learned so much from the lectures and the problem sets! The TA's were also awesome, very helpul. The material can be mathy but he's one of the best profs at giving lectures I've seen at Cal!
One of the best classes I've ever taken. The way of teaching was great.
I had to work a lot on the side because I didn't know Python very good before, but it was worth the extra work, absolutely.

analysis.name: Dylan Bland
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Mr. Bland cares about his students and cares about doing education right. His EDSTEM class was not demanding at all, but participation was important in the two hours of class per week. I would take his class again. Always interactive, some activities more interesting than others. Great guy, easy to talk to.

Professor Bland is such a kind and caring instructor. He teaches at a local Berkeley high school and is a Berkeley CalTeach alum, which makes him perfect for teaching this intro CalTeach tutoring course. He was incredibly knowledgeable about the course. He was also understanding of the pandemic's effects on students and was lenient on grading.

analysis.name: Mark Blum
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: great professor if you truly wanna learn something about Buddhism! He's super kind and knowledgeable about Japan and buddhism and easy to talk with. A lot of readings and it will be worthy to do them, if you studied hard following the study guide he gave, you will be fineeeeee and A is not that hard!

Class was totally doable if you actually study. All in-class exams with lots of Japanese terms to memorize. It's a lot at first, but gets easier when you put in consistent effort. Professor is knowledgeable and explains things well. Grading is detailed and fair. Learned a lot and would recommend if you truly wanna know more about Japan

Honestly, this was the worst class I've ever taken. For the final, we had to know how to answer 100+ terms and 50+ essay questions. It would have been better if the grading wasn't so strict - I need to hit every mark to get a full score.
Never take this class unless you want to get a C, regardless of how hard you work.
Definitely a difficult class, but rewarding. Professor Blum's teaching style made it interesting and worth the effort. Grateful for the experience!

mandatory attendance and expensive printed pdfs, weird jokes about east asian culture unrelated to the contents and sounds condescending all the time, would kill an orphan to avoid taking this his class again.

analysis.name: Katie Blackford
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: One of the worst profs I've ever had, I know she's new so don't want to fault her too much but good god what a terrible class. Thank god my GSI was incredible which made up for it since lab was tons of fun. But the class was run so poorly, the lectures were mind-numbingly boring, and don't even get me started on the lab coordinator Ms. Briggs.

I enjoyed chem 3AL and 3BL with professor Blackford. I found her lectures to be pretty helpful for assignments and she also gives extra credit. Only really big downside is her finals are way harder than practice exams and we still had lab + a worksheet the same week as the lab final (for 3AL). Make sure you keep your grade up before the final fr

Blackford was great, extremely understanding. She would respond to emails immediately after them being sent and she was always super responsive on ed discussion. She also adjusts her bins at the end so if you're like 1-2 points away from the next letter grade, you can get that grade. Overall great professor and can't wait to take 3BL with her too!

One of the best professors I've had at this school. Teaches clearly and her lectures (+ slides) are so helpful. Really appreciate that she does annotated versions as well so you still get all the notes if you can't make it. Super easy to communicate with through email. Looking forward to taking 3BL with her as well!

Her lectures were always easy to follow. However, her grading on some of the data analysis worksheets were a bit harsh and it seemed as if the most of the GSI's didn't know what was going on either. Overall, not a bad prof, but not good either just ok. If you do the work you should be fine.

analysis.name: Isabelle Le Blanc
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Le Blanc was cheerful in lecture and office hours. She was also very funny with cool sound effects (Schloop!) that made learning fun! Super approachable outside of class and willing to explain things in detail. Exam was difficult and made you think and understand concepts.

Professor Le Blanc is one of the best professors I've had. To put it simple, she is straightforward so there will be no surprises on any exams or materials. She's passionate, Kind and she will never let you fall behind if you don't understand the material. It's a hard class but if you actually care to learn lab techniques and materials, she's got u

I love her but oh do I hate this class...more anxiety-inducing than it needs to be and while I get the philosophy behind her assignments I wish there were fewer of them. However, she's a great professor and was able to recognize there were issues with my lab partner without me ever needing to mention it.

Isabelle is an amazing professor who truly cares about her students. She is very honest and gives very direct feedback. She is not an easy A by any means but she will push you to develop your weaknesses. She makes herself available to students and goes out of her way to make sure you learn and grow, regardless of what your grade is.

One of the best professors I have had in my time at Cal. Genuinely cares for the students and is incredibly knowledgeable about what she does. Make sure to engage in the class and work with your peers. As well, ask the professor questions about the material. Many of the assignments are about independent reflection and clarification.

analysis.name: Benjamin Blonder
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: What everyone else said. He's really great. Good lecture pace, good amount of content, and he was the only prof to provide full practice tests -- he even gave a cumulative review lecture before the final. Office hours were VERY helpful (get ready to have him ask YOU to explain things you're confused about!) Just a really amazing teacher.

BEST professor out of the 3 for Bio 1B. Lectures were easy to follow and slides were extremely descriptive. Textbook optional. Gave clear information about what you can expect to see on the exams.  Only professor that gave us a practice midterm which was very useful. I wish he taught the whole course instead of splitting it up between 3 professors.

All I can say is -- Thank God for this professor. He is single-handedly keeping the entire Bio 1B department alive. He explains the content well, he provides a fair practice midterm, and asks questions that aren't insanely minute and abnormal (compared to the rest of the course). If you don't want your love for biology to shrivel, try to have him!

Very organized slides and handouts. Not the most interesting content though, felt very textbook surface level based. On the flip side, tests were easier. Only professor that provided a practice test which was extremely nice. However, this section had the hardest frqs (still easy, but required understanding the content well in other applications).

He was extremely clear on what is going to be on the test and prepares you well. My biggest recommendation is to make flashcards with every single term. If you memorize all of them, you are pretty much guaranteed a good grade on the midterm and final. I didn't even study for his section on the final and I scored a 95%.

analysis.name: Blake Johnson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: TAKE HIS CLASS! I took his online Hist 2A class online and this is my second time taking one of his classes. I just love how independent it is (great class for people that have to work). Easy assignments, no tests/ exams, EXTRA CREDIT! Responds fast. Overall, great teacher and class, 100% take his class. :)

No hard deadlines for anything, lots of extra credit opportunities. However, be aware that you'll have to do a LOT of reading and writing. I took him for History of California at Laney, and we had to write 12 essays in total for his midterm 2 + final. Interesting material, so the reading wasn't too bad. No late penalties, but don't slack off!

Took his class at Laney College, online. Amazing! 1 Discussion board w/ responses and 1 essay a week. Very easy. Slow grader. Extra credit! Clear instruction. Don't slack off or you will be behind! But a 10/10 professor and a 10/10 class!

The class had co-instructors and Blake was the much better one (the other, Alex, was very nervous and disorganized) who ended up doing most of the lectures. Blake's a good lecturer, cute too, and covered tons of stuff, but the highlight of the class were the discussions he ran at the end of every class which were much more interactive and lively.
I took Blakes history class at Laney College. Super awesome dude and very passionate about what he teaches.

analysis.name: Benjamin Blackman
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He doesn't deserve this low of a rating, IMO. His section is doable, and pedagogically sound, but it's very compact due to the contraints of the course in general. But it all makes sense and the exam questions aren't too heinous if you put in the time and effort to really know every bit of lecture material. His office hours are a godsend.

I recommend before every test rewatching every single lecture of his and writing notes on everything he says (emphasis on everything). On the ORGBIO midterm, I did not study that well, and scored a 45% when the class average was around 60%. Then, during dead week, I rewatched every single lecture and  when I retook the midterm, I scored a 93%.

He is kind and caring to students but rushes through the content WAY too fast.  Never went to lecture in person, and I had to keep rewinding the lecture recording to understand what he was talking about.  Would be a good professor if he slowed down and didn't cover as much material.  Exams were challenging due to the amount of things covered.

Good professor but way too much content. Take advantage of his org bio labs, since they were the most useful labs in the whole course; when you're not actively writing something on the handout, take notes at each station, ask the GSI questions, make sure you understand every step of the lifecycle and every part of the plant. DO HIS TOPIC HANDOUTS.

Organismal Biology is a tough section, but Blackman does a good job explaining everything. To be successful on his midterm and final, it is important to understand how every piece of information connects with each other, attend all the lectures, and go to office hours. I got a 95 on his midterm and a 90 on his section of the final by doing this.

analysis.name: Boroka Bo

review_highlights.comment: Prof Bo is AMAZING! Super approachable, clear, funny, caring, and would always ensure we actually learn in class, knowledge that is useful outside in the job market. She is a hard grader, but follows very clear criteria available to the class. As long as you can follow directions, you will rock both qual and quant methods. She wants us to succeed!

Boroka was my professor in a huge lecture course. Her sections made the programming we had to learn feel manageable, as she would always make sure that everyone understood the code and was able to function on their own before the tests. If not for our hands-on R sections with her, I would have for sure had to drop this class.

Prof. Bo is a huge asset to Berkeley's Sociology department! She is patient, explains concepts well, listens and encourages great conversations in the classroom. I tend to be more quiet, but in her class, I always feel like I will be heard and that my voice will be appreciated. She will not spoon-feed you with info, so you will have to work hard!

Best GSI I've ever had at Berkeley! Respects your time, super helpful, clear, caring and brilliant. Worked my a** off for her class, but totally worth it as she gave me a great recommendation for work. Owe her so much, highly recommend that you take anything she teaches (as long as you are into the subject of course).

She is a tough grader (this is an upper division course, so don't expect an easy A!), but you will definitely get great feedback! I am very glad I took the course, learned (and learning) a ton from Boroka. She is super easy to talk to, approachable, flexible when it comes to office hours, and insightful when it comes to the material. Best class!

This man is the worst profesor ever.

analysis.name: Irene Bloemraad
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: This is the worst class I've ever taken. Ridiculous amounts of assignments, projects, and readings (which are painfully dry & boring). The lectures are long and boring, over half the class stopped attending. The teacher is very clear but she has unreal expectations from students. Only take this class if it is absolutely necessary, otherwise AVOID!

By far the worst class I have taken here, not because of the course material but for the unrealistic expectations the GSI's as well as the teacher hold for the students. If you aren't working on the projects, sections assignments, or quizzes, you're working on the readings. 3 hours for the final, and over half the class did not finish. AVOID

Man, Soc 5 is the MOST boring class I've ever suffered though, though Bloemraad is pleasant and clear about her lectures. Seriously though, avoid this class unless you've got to take it. Medium use of the reader (share with a friend if you can). There are 5 assignments (easy enough) and a final..

It's a lot of work and tons of reading, but she is trying her best to get us to understand the readings and make them stick. there are a lot of quizzes and assignments, but it's not oh my god the most difficult thing in the world. She's a good teacher and tries to make such dense boring material interesting. I recommend you take her if anyone.

This is the most tedious class I've taken at Berkeley, but if you have to take it, for sure take it with Bloemraad. She speaks very well and is really into the material. She is very nice and understanding, though she makes the tests (especially the final) so incredibly long. At some point you just want to get up and bail.

analysis.name: Kristie Boering
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: I really enjoyed her lectures. They were engaging, and her demos were very cool! Her exams are very fair, and I think she does a great job at preparing her students for them. It is also very fun to go to her office hours; she is very eager to help with anything. She encourages curiosity, but is also very clear about what is actually tested!

Very bad professor, her lectures are impossible to understand due to random schizophrenic outbursts. Mind numbing and easy class though, again just be careful about labs. Don't attend if you already have strong fundamentals in chem, her lectures add almost nothing to the class, just use the textbook whenever you feel like you ned more.

Boering was absolutely wonderful to have for the second part of Chem 4A with her lectures making it clear how much she cares for the subject. Make sure to attend lecture for the fun demos and office hours for candy and thoughtful responses to any questions you have. Lectures can get a bit disorganized so best just to sit in and listen.

Very energetic professor and nice demos. It was clear that she cares about the subject! Always willing to talk outside of class. Super informative slides and she was always on top of correcting wrong things. Felt that she had fair exams although the portion of the units taught on the final was significantly harder than MT3.

Get ready for a lot of self-study. The lectures do not prepare you for the midterms or finals. She is the nicest person but when it comes to class, she honestly could have included more practice problems during lectures rather than demos.

analysis.name: Carl Boettiger

review_highlights.comment: He's a great person and really cares about students success and helps out as much as he can with code and troubleshooting but the class is run in such a weird way with beginners basically using AI for everything and the course content not really being new information for ESPM students. You will get an A if you just stick to what he writes.

The concept of this class is really amazing, however it really wasn't geared towards ESPM students, it catered more to the advanced coders. There is very little lecture time on learning Python with very advanced coding projects. You can use AI if you're a beginner, however subsequently I felt the grading was very harsh for beginner coders.
Very clear and accessible professor. His lecture format is very good for learning the subject because it emphasises the students working on the problems and him going around helping out when needed.

analysis.name: Catherine Bordel
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 74 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Reading only first 5 reviews FOOLED ME. As someone with 0 physics knowledge, this course was HELL. Examples in class? Understandable. Homework? Manageable. Exams? HORRIBLE. Yes, there is a HUGE curve but given the fact that the class average is a whopping 50% on a good day, if she didn't make the cutoff at 22%, probably 80% of the class would fail.

Prof Bordel is a subpar professor for multiple reasons. Her lectures are abysmal. She starts 5 minutes before Berkeley time, which leaves you scribbling furiously to catch up for the rest of lecture because she goes so fast. Her exams are extremely difficult but the curve is not at all generous. I used to be excited about physics, now I dread it.

prof bordel claims to care about students and genuinely seems like a nice person, yet her lectures are dry, exams have super low averages, and policies are unfair. 

All class material is low effort, and her teaching made me dread physics. The GSIs are super unaccommodating and refuse partial credit like it's coming from their own bank account.

If you are new to physics, this class is hard. Exams are harder than lectures and exam averages were in the F range (44-47%) which makes a really good curve but I don't really feel like I learned much. Try to stay within/ around average and you should be fine for some form of a B. It's hard but Bordel really cares and is very generous with grading!

She is a good lecturer but spends a lot of time on proofs and specific problems rather than general solving approaches. The exams are not too difficult but are not at all based off of the homework. Tutors for the class are unable to solve some of the homework problems and GSIs unhelpful. Attendance not mandatory but lectures not posted.

analysis.name: Jessica Boles
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: 105 and self-study of converters (or just reading a spec sheet) is much much more useful than this class. The lab TA was generally unhelpful and course staff never responded on Ed (IIRC this was policy, LOL...). Amazing professor. She is really helpful and caring about her students. The only thing is that the dates of quizes are weird. She cares a lot about the students and was always reachable by email. Lectures are very clear, HW prepared you for exams. Prof. Boles listened to student feedback throughout the semester and truly did the most to ensure everyone was able to learn. It is clear she really wants her students to succeed. Easily one of the best professors at Berkeley.

analysis.name: Maheemah Bokhoree

review_highlights.comment: Very passive aggressive, and the grading criteria for lab reports is VERY unclear. She always uses some type of confusing logic to say that the rubric is applied consistently across students, but we can't even see the rubric prior to answering questions.

Very nice professor, easily accessible and responds quickly to emails. CHEM 32 is P/NP, so very chill. A little bit new, but good lectures. Tbh I don't think I needed to take CHEM 32, because CHEM 1A was more intro than expected bc has review at beginning and the lecturer was really good, but CHEM 32 might be helpful if you want to ease into chem?

Biggest complaint would be rushing through lectures/asking questions to students on iclicker before even teaching concepts. Slides seemed somewhat disorganized. inexperienced lecturer, but she genuinely wants to help students learn. her slides are helpful. a good amount of tedious work. although its pass no pass she still gave a final, which i did not love. mandatory attendance and biweekly quizzes which were worth a good amount. if ur deciding between this and chem1a, don't waste your time, take chem1a.

She's a decent lecturer who genuinely cares about ensuring understanding. She can seem nervous at times but is clearly passionate about teaching and will happily answer any questions you might have. analysis.name: William Boos

Awesome professor!! Lectures are clear and engaging with lots of fun demonstrations. He gives ample guidance on HW/exams and he answers messages quickly. Class is crazy well organized and Prof Boos always has his student's learning and wellbeing in mind. Physical science and climate fundamentals in the context of interesting weather phenomenon.

Took this class pass/no pass, which I believe is the route to go if you're a non-science major and just taking this for the physical science breadth. 10/10 professor. Always went in depth into concepts, explained in terms anybody could understand, & made sure ppl understood before moving on. Goat professor and brilliant guy.

Professor Boos was great. He clearly cares about his students, and has a really kind grading policy. He dropped the 4 lowest homework scores, and curved the class at the end by a couple percent. he's smart but a horrible teacher. we all tanked the first test and then he blamed it on our incompetence not his inability to teach us the relevant material. he's eager to help but gets frustrated easily and doesn't communicate well. also told us on several occasions that a 50% isn't a fail by his standards then proceeded to fail people with 58%

Bruno is an inspirational professor. He is more than accommodating and goes out of his way to help students succeed during class. Make sure to do the review quizzes and to ask questions during class. Take another AC class.

analysis.name: Carmen Butcher

Asyn class. Only direct interaction with prof was through comments and one Zoom check-in session for the final speech, but she was extremely caring about my progress and really seemed to appreciate her students. I wish I took an in-person class with her.

This is honestly the worst professor I've had at Berkeley. She treats her students like kindergarteners and most of your time will be spent on busy work. Prof seems to care more about how much she cares than her actual students. This class made my writing worse. Insane attendance policies and will call you out if your camera is off  for a second

analysis.name: John Briginshaw

took him twice, failed both times. the exam material is nothing like the practice exams or homework and groups of people cheat which change the curve. he ghosted my emails and posted grades weeks late on calcentral. failed the most people at haas that i know of. taking kim was a breeze compared to briginshaw. take kim!!

Avoid this class at all costs. This professor just changes the syllabus based on his whims and fancies. Doesn't respond to student concerns. DO NOT take this class.

tests were too specific on topics not covered during lectures

analysis.name: Roland Burgmann

Roland is such a sweetheart who is so knowledgable about earthquakes. If you keep up with the class(easy assignments), it is an easy A and has very useful information on being prepared. It is kind of sad because people take this class for the GPA boost, but he is clearly so passionate about the material he teaches. Highly recommend!

I love professor Burgmann! Although sometimes I do struggle *just a bit!* with staying on track with the lecture because he talks a bit slow, EPS 116 with him was rather enjoyable. The grading bins are 95% or higher is an A, which is pretty insane. There are at least 2 quizzes per week, which, although are short, require a great deal of effort and lecture note taking.

Such an AMAZING professor. As long as you study the study guide you'll do fine for the exams. There are few readings and the lectures are straightfoward and chill

analysis.name: Terry Buehler

i went to maybe 6 classes the whole year, still did pretty well watching the lectures online. it's not very difficult as long as you take it seriously, but there's a lot of elementary level physics that make you want to just breeze past the course content if you already know some stuff. project 1 i got marked down for not enough physics

I took this class not knowing what to expect and I REALLY enjoyed this class! The lectures are super interesting and all of the concepts build on each other which helps with comprehension. Lots of fun demos in class. I attended almost every lecture (they are recorded too) and did well on the quizzes despite the quizzes being pretty hard

Terry was a great professor and the subject matter was fascinating! He was very accessible and fun to talk to during office hours. Textbook not helpful.

 French43A was fr my favorite class, maybe ever. Take it!

Will is incredibly understanding (especially when it comes to dsp) and a fantastic lecturer. The books are really interesting and always relevant to class. I Took her Political Science in fashion class and it was such an amazing course I loved attending it every week, and even though it was a 1 unit class it still opened up my eyes to the political side of the clothes we were in our everyday lives.

Worst professor i've had. Grading system is confusing and unnecessary. makes it super hard to get an A in the class. psychological torture

She is very knowledgeable and passionate about the subject she teaches, and answered all my questions happily. I finished this class with an A, and all of the material you are tested on can be found in her slides. Just study hard!

Prof Bunge is very knowledgeable, approachable, and sharp. The class had an experimental feel to it, because she was trying out new exams. That messed me up a little. She was very understanding though and allowed us many different opportunities to help us out.  I like her. She could be more organized, but the material was interesting.

Prof Bunge is obviously very knowledgable about neuroscience but that is her only strength as a professor. She is disorganized, glazes past important info, and makes students feel stupid for not having the same expertise she does when they ask questions (her tone is so rude). My GSI was the reason I learned anything. would not recommend.

As previous student mentioned, she seems to be all over the place. She doesn't elaborate in her lecture and basically reads off of the slides. Her study guide was just us writing bunch of random questions about the material. And whenever students ask question during lecture, she is often not sure how to answer them.

Professor Bunge obviously loves what she does, and it can be intimidating to attend her lectures because she just knows so much. I'm not a psychology major, and I just put an honest effort into the class, and she (plus the really kind GSIs) made me feel like that effort was worth it. Definitely read the textbook before lecture, though!

analysis.name: Roger Byrne
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I enjoyed Prehistoric agriculture. Byrne focuses on understanding patterns and the explanations for those trends rather than simply relating facts. This approach makes the course much more intellectually stimulating. For written exams, understand and elaborate on concepts using key examples. Know some archaeological sites and specific domesticates.

I fell asleep everyday in this class but got an A. So with studying you should pass no problem, but you will have to survive the boredom of 3 hrs of dry lecture a week (if you aren't interested in glaciers and clouds). Labs are easy & tests/quizzes aren't too hard either. The lectures also are a hard to follow... resulting in unpreventable sleep)

Byrne is a real gentleman. He really loves what he does, and he truly cares about his students. One of the rarest types of professors in a school driven only by people who want their name in a journal or win a prize. The school would be a better place with more Byrne's. His lectures were not the most clear, but just follow it really hard.

Decent teacher, likeable guy. Course was fairly interesting and useful. One annoying tendency: He likes to save main point & important info for very end of lecture, just as students are packing up to leave for next class, then dumps it on them all at once as everyone scrambles to get it down in their notebooks. Pace it, Dude. Pace it.

I really loved biogeography. I enjoyed all of Byrne's nuanced ideas about past climate and vegetation patterns. Make sure to come to class and pay attention during lectures. Focus  more on understanding the concepts than rote memorization...just know key examples for the exams. Roger Byrne is a great  teacher and a kind person.

analysis.name: Greg Castillo
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Expect a lecture going over different buildings in his PowerPoints. He is pretty monotone so its hard to stay awake if its an 8am class. I hated the pop quizzes on the readings because they were so early in class skimming the reading wasn't enough--and they were the only form of attendance. The final "museum exhibition" is time-consuming.

The class was at 8am T,Th. Attendance was not mandatory but there were weekly pop quizzes on the readings, so if you were not at class or showed up late, you would fail the quiz. The assignment for Greg's part of the class was fairly straightforward but the graders were vague sometimes on point deductioins

First lecture was boring (intro lesson), but everything after that has been super interesting; I'm learning lots in this course. Greg does speak a bit monotonously, but the way he lectures is very engaging and at times funny. His presentation of historical facts makes it seem like I'm listening to someone "spill tea", making me not fall asleep.
Prof. Castillo is a kind and brilliant lecturer. His lectures were extremely interesting and piqued my interest even during the 8 am class! I highly recommend attending his office hours.

Interesting intro class to architecture, urban planning, and environmental design in different places and times. A lot of lecturing from slides but minimal tests/quizzes and so the class time isn't stressful. Case studies are good for an intro lower div but also it's going for breadth rather than depth. Still neat and I found it fun and engaging.

analysis.name: Carla Hesse
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I adored professor Hesse. I don't know about the other classes that she teaches, but 166B was wild because she just knows literally everything. I had pages of notes every day. I'm not even really interested in more modern or political history but she got me completely hooked. Devastated I probably can't take another class with her. But difficult.

Professor Hesse is very knowledgeable and inspiring. Her lectures were in depth and my only complaint would be that it is hard to copy the notes down because she goes fast. There are 2 essays, a midterm, and my final was online. The midterm was very difficult from what I remember, but it was a formatting issue and not her fault! I loved this class!

Almost impossible to recover if you missed a day in class as nothing is recorded and the slides were vague. Readings are interesting but pile up very quickly (reading a book + other works in one week). Interesting course and essay questions but grading sometimes felt like a hit or a miss.

While the instructor seems kind and well-intentioned, I found little value in the lectures and discussion sections. Had attendance not been required, I likely would have chosen not to participate in either.

it is hard to catch what is being taught in the lecture
and the lectures are boring

analysis.name: Suncica Canic
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 48 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Canic's teaching style was unfortunately not for me, I really struggled to pay attention. Tests were worth 80% and the tons of homework (60-70 problems) were only worth 10% of our grade. The part that made this class unreasonably difficult was her insisting on NOT curving. In a pandemic. Borderline cruel in my opinion.

Toughest grader ever. Tests vary drastically in difficulty. Untruthful about the difficulty. Release trivial practice then an insane exam. Unclear rubrics. Graphing problems require computer level precision. Missing nonessential steps cost you 50% of a question, and yet A cutoff is absurdly high. and much more much worse (StopDueToWordLimit) AVOID!

Exams and quizzes were very similar to the textbook problems.  If you do the homework , the tests should be super easy.  Provided practice tests that were very similar to the actual tests. You can self teach the material by reading the textbook, watching videos online, or using her detailed lecture notes. Gave super easy 20% EC on midterm 2.

I never go back and leave reviews, but for this one I needed to. She assigned way too much homework, and her lectures were so disorganized. Her practice tests were nothing like the real deal, and her grading criteria was ruthless. I was a B+ calculus student before this, and this class has absolutely taken a toll on me. Save yourself and avoid.

Failed math 53 with Norman, took it with Prof Canic and I feel like i genuinely came to understand the most difficult topics like divergence/stokes/green because of how well she would simplify things and would have very clear notes on. Exams were very fair, practice exams were accurate. one of my favorite professors so far. very caring

analysis.name: Daniela Cammack
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This professor cares more about her own reputation than her students grasping "Modern Political Theory." Discrepancies between GSI's and prof. Grading changes throughout the semester. Casually rude and dismissive towards student complaints. This was neither informative on Theory nor what a Berkeley professor should be like. Don't attend lecture!

I did not learn anything in this class. Lectures were just about context of the readings which did not have anything to do with the papers. Also, what I disliked the most is the fact that the professor told students bad course evaluation ratings could cost her the teaching position and actually brought up her rate my professor ratings in an email.

She's very sweet and curved the class at least for my semester. However, the subject matter is confusing, there's a lot of reading, but she is helpful in OH. The GSI was very picky about the written assignments. Tough class honestly.

I have taken other theory classes and while they are reading heavy, they were organized and explained concepts clearly from each theorist. In this class, we would spend one day on difficult readings by Hegel or nietzsche. You dont have to write on all authors, but whats the point of taking a class that doesnt teach you the authors in the syllabus

While Professor Cammack was accessible and friendly towards your average liberal student, those who disagreed with her saw another side. From her condescending outbursts to her disparaging rants and feedback, Cammack had no room for dissenting opinion. Hypocritical is the best word to describe this professor that claims to respect her students.

analysis.name: Cecile Gaubert
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Average Econ class:super long exams (40 pages of pure computations), messy handwriting (hard to keep up with), and concepts that feel more complex than they need to be. Overall, though, not bad. There's a generous curve and pretty reasonable HW. GSI (Anson) was a crashout tho, and made it hard to ask questions (made you feel bad for not knowing).

Lectures were fine, just a bit dry; I wish she gave more interesting real-world examples and such. My section was very useful, but the textbook was not. The p-sets were pretty hard, but not too much work and fairly graded. Very generous exam curve because they're difficult and LONG - the final was something like 40 pages of computational problems.

Lectures were okay, but covered everything you needed to know; recorded. Psets are similar to exams and graded lightly. Exams are long and very computational. Brush up on Calc I. Curve/Bins are undisclosed but must be quite generous. Extra credit through polls, bonus for class participation. Gaubert has a lot of experience in the industry.

Definitely one of the better French econ teachers. Lecture and section are so important for her class. Her lectures can be a little all over the place, but section (go Anson!) really clears up the concepts. A lot of material for exam prep (exam averages around 50%) and curve is thick cuz some people forget its math intensive.

The professor and GSIs are nice and accessible outside of class (especially David). Most of the students who choose this class are really smart, so beware of that. However, the curve is pretty lenient, with a large percentage getting A's and B's. The problem sets are lengthy, the exams are hard. STUDY! Cramming does not work.

analysis.name: Celeste Kidd
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Not my typical style of preferred teaching but cant deny the easiness of the course. Things may likely change as she switched up her style recently. Class material was in person and only on paper. Exams were based on logical thinking on what we went over in lecture. Lectures tended to drag but overall professor was kind and caring

Grade really depended on you showing up and as long as you did that you'd basically know everything for the midterm. you'll also be super well prepared by the sandbox activities. lectures are fun and interesting! definitely one of the best professors at Cal!

Prof Kidd is the kindest professor! Her lectures are clear and engaging, and her work is inspirational. No HW, readings or finals. 3 exams. Pay attention in class and section and you will excel. She inspires her students to pursue research and helps students get information of future work in the field of psychology. I highly recommend this class!

prob the sweetest prof at ucb. she is very caring and preps students for gradschool stuff. however, sometimes it was difficult to understand some of her concepts. experimental confounds. look that up b4 u get into her class lol. otherwise, this class is so interesting, and there is no hw! only like a lecture question during lecture

I LOVE PROF KIDD !!! no homework, show up to class, take the midterms (took me avg 15-30 min easiest midterms i've ever taken and is based on the sandbox activities) if i could propose to a prof i would propose to her.

analysis.name: Celine Pallud
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Took ESPM 131. The lectures were filled with information that was not tested which I personally dislike. She's a nice professor I just didn't think the exams were very fair. Exams are also extremely long and are almost all paragraph responses required. Points are marked off for missing small details which would be fine if given more time.

pro pallud is great! clearly very passionate about soils and knows a lot about them. really encourages student qstns. spring '24 was behind in lectures for the entire sem but she cut some material out for the final, bless. heavy on the paying attn in class LMAO. tests are tricky and hmwk is a bit challenging (graded a bit harshly by TA).

Professor Pallud is extremely knowledgeable and I highly recommend this class for ESPM students as well as students looking for an elective outside their major. Homeworks are very doable but still are somewhat challenging and rewarding. Tests are based on lectures and readings. Expectations are clear and you will learn a lot about soils!

Professor Pallud knows a lot about soil and will give you a great introduction to the topic. The lectures are very text-heavy so make sure that you take notes, but if you have questions she always takes time to make sure students understand. GSI did most of the grading. Very understanding and knowledgeable.

analysis.name: Celeste Langan
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 54 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: My biggest gripe about this professor is that her lectures rarely featured close readings, just a lot generalities that were never convincingly anchored to the text(s). Caveat emptor.

Lectures were extremely confusing and abstract. Would rarely engage the students during lecture: instead, she literally read off of an essay she probably wrote the night before. Great ideas but presented poorly and hard to grasp. Never actually got around to the point of lecture until about the halfway mark, then would almost always run out of time

While I will admit that Prof. Langan is brilliant, however it's like she lectures out of a lit theory book written in a language only she understands. Works for some, not for me. Never got a response to the email I sent asking to set up a time outside of her office hours to talk about what I didn't get. She seemed really nice just not helpful.

She is brilliant, true, but entirely incomprehensible.  I felt like I needed a dictionary beside me through all of her lectures, in order to gloss every other word.  Rather boring, as well.  Probably better in upper div classes.

Very brilliant, VERY scattered. Never finished lectures on time & left me feeling like there was so much more she would never get to cover. Do the reading before class & come to every class or your grade will suffer. Lots of assessments--3 short papers, 1 long paper, final--but final + final paper pretty much determines grade. Not enough novels!

analysis.name: Celeste Saravia
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Despite other reviews, I enjoyed this class and Prof Saravia; she's a very kind and knowledgable professor.  Her lecture style may not be everyone's favorite but she gives a substantial amount of material/practice problems to review and records her lectures as well.  I did not find this course very hard whereas I thought other econ upper-divs were

This class was bad in so many ways. First of all, the professor was extremely confusing in her lectures and did not explain things well. Secondly, there is no curve, even though the average on the first midterm was a D. Thirdly, almost your entire grade is based on exams. I've never had a class where so much of my grade is based on exams. Beware.

It took almost two months for our first midterm to be graded and over a month for our second midterm to be graded. They released the grades one day after the final P/NP deadline. The grades are not inputted into bCourses (only on Gradescope) so you don't know your grade in the class. The professor is very confusing and unorganized. Don't take this.

I could tell Professor Saravia knew what she was talking about but I don't think she really knew how to teach efficiently. Her lectures were very hard to follow and she would lose her train of thought very often, which confused a lot of students. The class was almost based entirely on exams and there were no real assignments. Would not take again.

This class was extremely difficult and the grading policy was very confusing/strange. Over 80% of your grade is made up of exams. While we haven't taken the final yet, the midterms were extremely difficult and graded harshly. The professor did not explain clearly and the topics way were more confusing than they needed to be. It was unfair.

analysis.name: Cecilia Mo
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Lectures were interesting and introduced me to a few topics I had never heard of. Midterm was straightforward if you studied well and in advance for it because there is A LOT of content. I felt there could have been less coding assignments but it was still manageable and the GSI responded quickly. Takes time to learn everyone's names!!

Sure she's fine but as a professor? You're better off taking another course. GSI was also not good and lacked being a leader for the coding assignments. Cecilia gave boring lectures & hypothetical analytical questions to which she expected perfect responses. Overall, do not take this class. Midterm, Final, Coding, and group project? Ha, stay away.

Take literally any other Political Science course. The information presented throughout lectures is redundant, resulting in a halt in the consumption of any new knowledge since Week 5 of the course. There are 5 CODING assignments assigned throughout the semester ???, a midterm that left me questioning my sanity, a group project, and a final exam.

I would not recommend this course; very data-heavy for some reason and has unreasonable expectations for what students are capable of. Exams are in person with no notes allowed. Truly take any other political science course at Berkeley and save the stress.

Professor Mo is an OK instructor but the forced participation made this class a bit weird. Also, the class is WAY too hypothetical and unlikely to be applied in real life, so I felt like this class is quite useless. But as a general Ed class would suffice.

analysis.name: Cecil Giscombe
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Great guy to hang around with, lots of interesting anecdotes.  But when he's leading a workshop or reading your poetry, you'll find he has a definite aesthetic bias, which he'll try to thrust upon you.  After a while, it can get annoying.

While we cover a vast amount of writings within the seminar, Prof Giscombe is great at explaining topics and facilitating discussions that are relevant to what we've read. He's very easy to approach and clearly knows what he's talking about, while also being funny. Do the readings, ask questions, and you will do great!

His teaching has greatly improved my writing because he allowed me to think differently and helped expand my creative vision whenever we reviewed my work. His classes focus on discussion which allowed my work to be critiqued by many people rather than just one which I found helped avoid biases. He's immensely kind and accessible outside of class.

As a person, he is lovely. As a teacher, I found him interesting, but often biased and unclear about his expectations of our work. Work is reviewed workshop style, which isn't for the faint at heart. He randomly changes the syllabus and frequently doesn't let you know due dates/readings until the day before. Huge confusion on grading criteria.

Professor Giscombe was amazing at teaching me how to improve my writing without being bias. Creative writing is difficult to teach, yet he had a great teaching method by asking me questions about my incomplete works that inspired the writer in me rather than making his own suggestions that dull creativity.

analysis.name: Celia Rodriguez
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: IIf you want to take a class where you learn absolutely nothing and are just confused the whole time, then she is your best option. She is the worst professor I have taken in my entire educational career. Please, whatever you do, steer away from her. She is completely unprofessional and does not care about her students.

Celia is one of the best professor's I've ever had. She dedicates time to students on an individual level, and cares deeply for our spiritual, mental, and physical health. While some may be frustrated with her style, it is usually those that are used to a more rigid, hierarchical structure. She is all about communal learning. She changed my life.

Celia is an amazing professor. I learned so much from her and the class was taught very well. It is also very easy to communicate with her. On a personal side note, if you are interested in social justice, she is a great to her talk. She drops gems of knowledge every single class, to the point where you don't want to miss a class.

Class is pretty straightforward. She might come across as a "mess", but she actually just has a really open curriculum so the students create the class. Not meant for students who are assimilated in academia and expect everything to be given to them.

AVOID LIKE THE PLAGUE! Celia's teaching style is a mess. The woman was everywhere and yet we went no where in the class. The class meetings consisted of random tangents and ramblings that were hard to follow and irrelevant to the class materials. Readings were never discussed and assignments were never clear. The whole class was a headache. AYYYYYY

analysis.name: Chien-I Chiang
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 59 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Nice guy but exams are hard. Heavy on derivations that would be cool as HW problems but not so much in a timed environment. It's over for you if you don't perform well on the final worth over 40% of your grade. The practice exams he gave out were also a lot easier than the actual ones. HW is helpful and the late policy is chill. Just read griffiths

Not a bad professor, but I have some issues. He makes mistakes in derivations at times, lectures are poorly paced (often rushing the bulk of content in the last 5-10 minutes), and exams are notably harder than the practice ones he gives & sometimes include topics he specifically tells us not to worry about knowing (virtual images on the final...)

I've taken 3 classes with him at this point. He has a tendency to write exam that are incredibly confusing, either because the topic is very advanced/briefly covered, or because the question was worded poorly. Strangely, his exam questions pre-2024 were much more straightforward.

Great lecturer! Very easy to understand and clearly knows a lot about the material. Textbook does not follow the class to a tee but he gives you the sections he covers in class. Has a grace period of 4 days on homework and hw load is overall very reasonable. 1 midterm and final were hard but expected for the level of the class.

This professor lectures very well, and presents the concepts in a way that deliberately builds up intuition. He provides an abundance of external resources as well as posting recorded lectures. His homework sets are didactic and not time-consuming, and his exams are designed to tests your knowledge rather than your ability to calculate

analysis.name: Gregory Choy
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: INCREDIBLY chill professor who is obviously very knowledgeable about his work. His lectures do tend to be a bit monotonous and a bit directionless, but are still interesting most of the time. Class is heavily reading-based (though the readings are largely interesting), and the grade consists of three easy take-home exams and a group presentation.

Very nice professor, but his lectures can be pretty boring. 3 take-home exams which were super easy. I liked discussion section better than the lecture. This class was pretty introductory, but you learn a lot still. The final was a simple group presentation on a poem or a reading. take it for a chill class!

Lecture-style, and does not facilitate discussion. Lectures are not that compelling. When I asked a question, his response: "Why are you asking that question?" However, he is a very generous grader, and the readings themselves are generally very good. Short answer response exams and group project. Lectures are important for exams.

Accommodating, kind, approachable, and understanding. Our lectures were fairly long (3 hours!) but they never felt that way, and he did a great job of retaining the class' attention. The subject matter was very powerful and great to discuss. This professor is v active in the ES department and is clearly very qualified. He's worth taking!!
Folks here whining about Choy being boring, unfair, not nice, etc. Yeah, good luck finding an easier, more interesting and chill prof than Choy.

analysis.name: Jack Citrin
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 70 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Good: his lectures were pretty entertaining. Not: PS1 might be a different deal but PS164 was strangely difficult. The concepts weren't that hard, but the structure of assignments was really unclear. There was no rubric ahead of time. If you don't say certain "buzz words" on exams, you can get a zero on a question, even if the explanation is right.

One of the greats! Took both Poli Psych & Public Opinion with him.  Brands himself as the cranky Andy Rooney type in lecture, but he's really a sweet man and goes out of way to help you if you get to know him 1 on 1. Lectures are perfect balance of funny personal anecdotes & substantive material. Interesting research papers, grading can be tough.

Good class, but I felt he based a lot of his teaching on what Huntington thinks. GSI's all seemed great and worked hard for you. You might cry from laughter the first lecture. But through the semester I was only awake when he was telling interesting stories... his lessons were boring for the most part.  Also, all examples involved peanut butter.

Interesting class but I still recommend sitting in the front to catch everything he says. A little boring. A lot of students thought it was an in-depth AP Gov class. For those of us who didn't take AP Gov, you'll have to play a bit of catch up. 2 big papers. Exams (essay-style) based off readings (good!) AND lecture. Citrin posts slides online.

Professor Citrin is very intelligent with a sarcastic sense of humor that is very enjoyable. However, lecture is very dull and tedious. He often rambles on (his stories are interesting) with powerpoints he lets you see for about 5 seconds. No laptops so good luck getting everything down. Nice man though and really seems to care about his students.

analysis.name: Clayton Radke
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 37 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Absolute legend. Love this guy. Some students are scared of him, but if you just take the effort to go ask questions or engage more in the class past just going to lecture and doing homework, he's actually very approachable and clearly cares a lot about students. You can tell he genuinely loves teaching and chemical engineering.

You can tell by his age and demeanor that if he weren't passionate about the success of his students, he would be retired by now. The course is very difficult (B- average), but going to all lectures and discussions makes it do-able. Radke is respected and adored by many students for good reason.

Dr. Radke is witty, passionate about chemical engineering, and shows a great deal of care to his students. Lectures tend to stray off the material and Dr. Radke has a habit of going on tangents, but these are oftentimes attempts by him to integrate real-world, everyday engineering concepts into the lectures. Very well-liked by the class.
He is very passionate about the material; it's just a hard class with a pretty unforgiving curve.

Dr. Radke is a brilliant scientist and moreover possesses extraordinary pedagogical common sense. The logic of the material at hand is clearly and efficiently articulated and always accompanied by a wholesome, warm concern for his students' understanding and praxis of the material. Go to office hours always!

analysis.name: Clara Nicholls
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Clara is such a wonderful professor and person in general. She cares deeply about the subject and is a leading researcher in the field! She brought guest speakers who authored the class readings, which was neat. She's very approachable and is a great resource for anyone interested in food systems or ecology. I learned so much in this course. 100/10

Prof. Nicholls is an asset to students interested in environmental ecology. The class is mostly student led discussion, so be prepared to participate and have fun doing so! Her class enables students to develop their voice and their personal interest in aspects of rural development. Highly recommended class and straight forward grading & open OH.

Class is led seminar style, very biased left but I thought the readings were very interesting although sometimes a bit repetitive. She is really great in office hours and really cares about her students. I really learned a lot about the topic and found it really easy to get engaged. Definitely not a class for people who don't like speaking in class

Clara is a superb teacher and her class, sustainable rural development of latin america, is a really great class, though unfortunately overtly biased leftward.  It is taught seminar style and class format is a mixture of lecture and discussion led by Clara, students, and guest speakers.   Clara cares for her students and is a great contact too.
Came to RMP just to rate such an exceptional professor at Cal! Sophisticated lectures and meaningful student-led discussions...

analysis.name: Clelia Donovan
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Clélia is my favorite prof at Berkeley! She's really sweet, knowledgeable, and genuinely wants everyone to succeed and improve their Portuguese. We barely had any homework and I loved the class discussions, content, and how she organized the participation. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

Took Portuguese 103 with Clelia and it was so laid back, fun, and not too much work! Clelia gives a TON of feedback on your assignments and is so attentive. Clelia encourages you to speak Portuguese, even if you make mistakes it's okay! Overall I enjoyed this class and I loved having Clelia as my prof :)

Clélia is one of the best professors I have had while at Berkeley. Her manner of teaching is well paced and clear. If you do the work and come to class you will learn a lot and get a good grade. I am very excited for the possibility of having her again for Portuguese 103.
She is an amazing professor with so much knowledge She is also kind and accessible. WOLD DEFF RECCOMEND HER

Clelia cares most about using Portuguese well. She constantly encourages natural conversation throughout the class and takes every student where they are and helps them build their knowledge and fix mistakes over the semester. She tailors the lecture content based on the needs of the students & you can tell she's passionate and cares about students

analysis.name: Clare Talwalker
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 49 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Talwalker's class was an overall positive and highly developmental experience, I learned SO much across the semester. The assignments are straightforward and you are set up for success if willing to put in the effort for it. Course work can be a lot, but you do genuinely see a difference in knowledge as time progresses. Highly reccomend.

Talwalker is a nice and genuinely caring professor. Class is readings, which start long but by mid semester are like 10 pages, then write 1-2 paragraphs on the reading, for credit. then, lecture where we take the terms of the reading and create a deeper discussion. midterms/final have cheat sheet, relatively easy. recommend! lecture is slow but eh

This class is so boring. Don't need to do the readings at all u can lowkey just ChatGPT them and understand the main points. Do not need to pay attention in lecture at all but would participate in discussion. Really really boring class

Her boring lectures told you everything you needed to know about the readings so you don't have to do them, just remember her main points and regurgitate it on the tests. She claims she wants your ideas/interpretations, but really, you just have to reword her beliefs and you'll pass.  Stopped going to class because it wasn't thought provoking.

If you are not interested in understanding how the most influential thinkers over the centuries (Locke, Hegel, Marx, Polayani, Keynes etc) have shaped our recent political and economic systems then don't take this class. There is a mandatory attendance policy but I would have not attended class as much as I did without it. You get what you put in!

analysis.name: Clark Nguyen
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Clark's class on MEMS was a good technical overview of the subject. He taught it in a way such that an EE with little prior knowledge of mechanical engineering could follow along and succeed in the class. He does a good job teaching the basics. He can be a little hard to follow at times, but he has good lecture notes, albeit a little disorganized.

Clark is an amazing professor. He managed to completely redesign EECS16B into a great class. I really appreciate how he made himself very accessible outside of class and was genuinely receptive to feedback from the students. He listens to and cares for students and it shows in the quality of his teaching. He also shredded Metallica in class. Legend

Ppl usually don't come to lectures. I find it difficult to follow his teaching style. Notes are chaotic. Exams are easier compared to homework and lectures. The lab takes way too much time and the instructions are unclear. Make sure to study labs for exams. The class is on circuit design with no LA. PHYS 7B can be helpful before taking the class.
He has so much aura!! Best professor!!

Professor Nguyen is extremely knowledgeable in the MEMS area, which means he explains every concept very clearly, but sometimes the details can be overwhelming. He is very approachable and also very helpful during office hours. His homeworks are okay, but his tests are pretty difficult (but still fair). Definitely go to his lectures! Great prof!

analysis.name: Claire Tourmen
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I am in her French 1 class (I was only given the choice for selecting either French 2 or 3). She is unbelievably caring.

Really solid choice for a French teacher. Lectures are good- everyone attends ours for the most part, you'd definitely be fine if you skipped a few tho. Super nice with the grading and assignments- even though they're standard in the department she helps out with extensions etc. Textbook used 1-2 exercises per week,u prolly could get away w/out one

Professor Tourmen is a fantastic French teacher. I have taken class from her two semesters in a row and my French has improved immensely. She really cares about all of her students and truly wants us to learn the language. She is very accessible and always gives thorough feedback. Plus, she has the warmest demeanor that makes class a pleasure.

Claire is so personable and I love this lady. She is really understanding and funny and grades fairly easily. But attendance is really important because it affects your grade quite a bit if you miss enough.
Caring, knowledgeable professor. Really kind as a person. Encourages you when you make mistakes. Clear feedback for assignments. 100% recommend

analysis.name: Joseph  Coppola
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: THE GOAT!! I'm not even done with this class yet but I love it. Great lectures, entertaining, and Professor Coppola is super nice and really cares about students. He's easy to talk to, great at answering questions, super involved, super smart, and passionate. I would take this class a million more times. Couldn't recommend him enough. So fun!

I took Film 45, not Film R1B. I found the class very enjoyable, in large part due to Professor Coppola. He was always engaged with the class, would ask how we were as we walked in, and always tried to keep up with current shows and movies. He structured the course around readings, so be prepared to read a lot or you'll be lost. Very nice guy!

NOTE: I took film 45, not R1B
Coppola is a good teacher. He has an engaging way of speaking, I like how he bounces off student answers. I wish we watched more films in class as opposed to random TV Show episodes. I thought some of the content in the class was like too easy, like no duh, shallow analysis. But the hegemony lectures were good.

Friendly and encouraging. Interesting questions on tech. Cares about topics & students. Identity politics, but expected & fit well enough. Participation points, lenient grading, helpful. Casual writing class.
Discussion, not textbook: do the (small enough) readings+films, attend, put in effort to participate&discuss, & you won't need to worry much.
I took film 45. Legend. Amazing class discussions. Really well-spoken and engaging professor. Up to date with current events. Enjoyed that class thoroughly.

analysis.name: Sylvie Corteel
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data
