review_highlights.comment: Early review for people choosing classes for next sem. She always gives a full week from assigning a hw until it's due, usually 15-20 problems. Midterm 1 was straightforward and like the practice test. Average was an 80%. Her lectures are pretty clear and she'll try to answer any questions . Overall a reasonable professor and would recommend
Didn't feel like she wanted students to improve. Otherwise, the class seemed okay material-wise
Not a very understanding instructor at all. Almost mean when it comes to students understanding

I took Professor Corteel Fall 2023 for Math 55. Overall, I really enjoyed the content in Discrete and found that lectures were not very useful and lacked structure/consistency, but I was lucky I had an amazing GSI (Mitsuki).
Her exams are VERY similar to practice exams, which was nice because I didn't have to study much. Corteel is alsovery funny.

Professor Corteel is a good Professor, which means she's a fantastic Professor by Berkeley standards. Honestly this class was very fair (even if you are not a math major). Corteel loves induction so there is a little emphasis on that. Overall if you have the homework down, do the practice exams, and study for the quizzes, you'll do great.

analysis.name: Jason Corburn
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class tries to take the concept of social justice and ridiculously morph it into some sort of rigorous, systematic science, which is in line with how the Public Health department frankly takes themselves too seriously at times. Easy class to do well in, only due to Corburn's skills of pedagogy.

Coburn seemed to do as little of his job as possible. Not a single real lecture, just short, edited down recordings of previous semesters' lecture. If you like auto-graded multiple choice, that's literally all this class is -- hw, quizzes, everything. If you're like me and suck at MC, you're gonna feel cheated out of an easy A.

I did not think I would be really immersed into the material (PH major was a mistake for me) but Corburn's method of delivery makes you want to tune in. There's a lot of MC but they're very easy (perhaps too easy) to the point where a high-schooler could do them. I honestly might've preferred taking this class in-person and I love online now.

I didn't interact with Professor Corburn as everything was asynchronous and remote. He seems very knowledgeable and all assignments were relevant and interesting. Without the professor, the GSIs helped connect the class and the material. I wish I got to interact with the professor more. Grade is mostly from MC and wasn't too hard personally.

Corburn was a great professor and interesting lecturer. Make sure you go to class because he does use iclicker for attendance. The class depends on the quality of your GSI. Do not procrastinate on the homework assignments, and know the key concepts for the midterm.

analysis.name: John.D. Coates
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Amazing professor! I had him for c116 and he was the best. made class easy to understand, and was easy to come to for questions! I went to OH a lot and loved the GSI, she explained everything really well! He teaches really clearly and focuses on application and bigger picture messages! would take this class again

There are several issues with this class that I feel future students should be aware of before taking it. 1) ITS NOT CURVED: so everyone could get a C and the semester I took it 88% got a C or B-. 2) The GSI controls everything.He not only grades the hw and exams he also gets a lot of lecture time.If the GSI is a certain Cameron then please avoid

Easily the most interesting class I've taken. Prof Coates is a great lecturer and is very helpful at OH. He's an expert on what he's teaching and gives a great history of the field for the papers discussed. Tests are straight forward and questions come directly from what is emphasized during lecture (ie: if there's 10 slides on it, study it!)

analysis.name: Sharon Coleman
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Lectures consisted of her reading instructions for assignments (which was on bcourses) or for instance going over how to write a works cited. Lectures were monotonous and not always engaging. Consists of small group projects more or less every week. She is very caring and kind but does not teach you how to improve your writing skills whatsoever.

Attendance is mandatory. 70% of class time is group presentation. Sometimes no technology is allowed. Grading system is inconstant, during class when she went over my essay she said it was excellent and no changes needed to be made but she gave me a 64% for that essay with is confusing. And a lot of writing assignments in general outside of class.

Really sweet Professor. Definitely my favorite Professor this semester. 3 major essays with 1 final portfolio project. She allows for revisions on all essays which is very helpful. She cares about her students. However, make sure you go to class because if you miss more than 2 classes you have to take an in class final! 100% recommend Ms.Coleman

Ms. Coleman is very kind, but I feel she is not very engaging. the class time is spent either with her reading off of the board very slowly and monotonously OR by breaking us up into small groups and writing out answers to questions, then reading them to the class. Overall, I feel that I did not improve any skills taking this class.

A whole 1hour and 30 mins lecture was used to explain how to write an annotated bibliography which was completely unnecessary considering all the information was on b-courses and she was just reading off of the assignment instructions

analysis.name: Mark Csikszentmihalyi
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment:
Had him for Chinese 7A. Mark's a cutie. Lecture slides often have dense chunks of writing and he has a dense lecturing style which makes him a bit hard to follow. Readings were interesting, though lengthy.  
Ripe plums are falling/ Now there are only five/ May a fine lover come for me/ While there is still time

Favorite prof ever. Extremely knowledgeable and respectful. Cares a lot and is super friendly. Nerdy in the best way. 2 midterms, final, 2 papers graded by GSI who was also very knowledgable and friendly. Take good notes and tests will be fine (open note). An extreme amount of reading and I honestly didn't do most of it and did well so whatever

Mark is a lovely guy. He's funny, relatable, and fair. His lectures can drag a bit sometimes - he's an incredibly knowledgeable man, but a little awkward (in a good way!). You'll need to write several papers, but his grading is fair and feedback is plentiful. Office hours are easy to access, and he'll leave you loving both the sheep and the ritual.

Caring professor who really encourages students to come to office hours. Says "um" quite a bit but you can see he is quite passionate and knowledgeable about the subject. Be prepared to write quite a bit because you need to write 4 papers which isn't too bad though. Study guide for midterm and final preps you well. Midterm review lecture was fun!

As an EALC major student, mark is currently one of my favourite professors under our school department. He is caring, humorous(kinda cold jokes sometimes smh), and knowledgable. You can tell he is really passionate about his teaching and research and you will definitely learn a lot from him. He is a fair grader and his class is highly recommended.

analysis.name: Greig Crysler
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The lectures can be a little hard to sit through but they are actually interesting and the professor does actually care for the subject. He is very very approachable and knowledgeable. The class itself is pretty easy and fair.

If you are looking for an easy class and if you are not interested in working hard, you shouldn't even be in berkeley. He is a great professor for those who are keen and interested in learning, dull for those who could not be bothered.

Greig is a really great and caring lecturer. He doesn't take breaks which can make things feel like they drag on for a while, but overall the class was good. There were readings and reading responses every week but exams were open book. Had a pop quiz, was going to have more but he decided to change it to a time capsule project, which was nice.

Professor is very dull, and not very helpful. If you were interested in the topic before taking this class, your interest will disappear after taking this class. Besides professor doesn't care how many students attend the class, or whether students understand what is aspected of them. In all very bad experience.

Greig is a good prof, he sometimes rambles on a bit but he loves feedback and is happy to clear up anything you don?t understand. The content is useful and the sections and very stimulating. Easy midterm and final. Pop quizzes are too easy. The most work are the weekly reading responses.

analysis.name: Teri Crisp
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She's nice enough but literally did not grade ANYTHING until we got our final grades back. You will be swimming in homework during RRR week, and she doesn't really give adequate feedback. Throughout the course, it was extremely difficult to tell what was due, and when, and where, and what our grade would be. Take another R4B.

WAY TOO MUCH HOMEWORK. 3 essays due during finals week. (For some reason RMP won't let me say 1 of them was a 10-15 page r*search p*per.) I still do not have a single grade in that class (meaning I don't know what I got on any assignment nor do I know my final grade) and grades were due 4 days ago.
Made a person cry while giving feedback in front of everyone. Had to work throughout RRR week to start and finish the final essays that we hardly got any good feedback.

She gives amazing feedback, and everything is great, she is really nice and caring, you will definitely pass if you follow her rules. The only downside is that you would be doing 4 essays during dead week. Do the revision of the essay as fast as you can whenever you get the drafts feedback.

Teri Crisp is a caring professor that truly cares about her class more than anything else. She also gives great feedback on essays which helps you to become a more efficient writer. The only thing that was a downside was when she crammed 2 essays at the end of the class for the final portfolio.

analysis.name: Michael Cohen
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 85 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I'm an engineering major, so I'm not used to my grades being based mostly on opinions.  I can't believe a world class university really has professors that teach and grade with such outright political bias. He has a right to an opinion, but ruining my GPA because I disagree is just wrong.

The guy has charisma in the classroom, I will give him that.  But he's also arrogant, doesn't allow for dissent, and uses his authority and classroom as a bully pulpit for his political views.  I'd rather have a teacher than a preacher.  Lectures also seemed to lack any coherent organization.

AC27 was my favorite class I have taken at Berkeley, and I say this as a biochemistry major who initially only took this class to meet L&S requirements. Incredibly passionate/engaging and quite funny- if I have time in my schedule I would take another one of his classes just for the fun of it.

I don't pay thousands of dollars in tuition to hear this mislead fool spout his opinions in what should be a lecture.  The course is almost done, and I'm sure I wont get too high a grade because the last major paper I went against his garbage political propaganda. This college has a huge problem if they let this guy lecture.
One of my favorite professors of all time, I was always excited to go to his lectures and overall he was a really cool and genuine guy. Recommend 100%.

analysis.name: Crystal Chang
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 46 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I took professor Chang in the fall 2024 and spring 2025, and she has hands down been my favorite professor. She has helped me with my public speaking skills, before taking her class I was extremely shy, but after her classes my ability to speak in front of people has gotten better. She is also very understanding if you have an issue or a concern.

Had a fantastic experience in class with Dr. Chang. Super engaging lecturer that genuinely cares about students. Half the class was a history of Silicon Valley with the other half being a group research project on a startup of your choice. Groups were randomly assigned but don't think there were many issues.
Overall, could not recommend more.

Professor Chang is one of my favorite professors at Berkeley, and I loved this class with her! I would highly recommend her, she made the course extremely relevant to current day and related our theories to the news. Readings were not unreasonable and grading was fair. Participate and go to class because her lectures are always fantastic!!

Very enthusiastic and extremely knowledgeable. open minded and allows varied opinions to discuss points. She is opinionated but even in disagreement she makes sure everyone feels welcome to discuss. I chose cal because of professors like her. One issue is the essay promts are EXTREMELY vague which can hurt grade if not on the same page with the gsi

She's extremely biased. I don't think her course is either taught or managed poorly but after PE100 I expected so much more. I don't need to know what the professor's opinions are I just need to know what the arguments of the authors were and understand where they're coming from. However she would straw man those she disagreed with.

analysis.name: Alexander Craghead
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Very interesting class and passionate professor. Speaks quickly and doesn't share his slides so you need to pay attention but exams are open note. He prefers handwritten notes and staying off screens in class but allows printed notes for exams. Participate in the image analysis exercises in class: he's very encouraging towards all contributions.

Amazing class. Lectures always interesting and diverse topics. 3 big projects, midterm, final. Midterm and final both very open ended (in good way) and open book. Reading load not too heavy and you can cherry pick. Attendance not mandatory but you miss out on notes. He doesn't use text slides (just images). He's invested in teaching so talk to him!

Incredible lecturer. When he opened the class talking about railroads I was ready to be bored out of my mind, but it was way more interesting than lectures in topics I care about. 

If you don't care about humanities classes, I would not take Dr. Craghead's class. He is a lax grader for people who clearly care about the class, but not if you don't.

Really great + interesting class that provides a comprehensive overview of American landscapes and their component parts through cultural geography, architecture, and history. Reading heavy and grade comes down to midterm, final, and 3 papers/projects but instructions are clear. Prof knows his content really well and has a down to earth vibe.

"Making in America" has very interesting content from suburbia, to company towns, burning man, and American film. There is a ton of reading that makes up most of the midterm and final. Grading and expectations can be confusing. Wants you to engage with the material and challenge it, while simultaneously coming to the same conclusions he has.

analysis.name: Michael Crommie
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Very funny and engaging, though I personally found 137B to be pretty hard (partly my fault for slacking). Lectures helped build intuition but didn't always feel that useful. Tests were weird, I don't know if I like his style of giving a bunch of problems but letting you skip all the computation. Would take him again just for the personality tbh!
One of the best common sense explainers, he tries to make everything very intuitive despite the non intuitive nature of the subject. one of the best teachers ive had.

I signed up to this website just so I could rate this guy. He's totally amazing and FUNNY FUNNY FUNNY. Very entertaining lectures and clear explanations. Homework was pretty rigorous and midterm and final are fair. Generous curve. If you can take a class with him, I recommend it. I myself am looking forward to someday in the future have him again.

Hes legitimately the best Professor I have had at Cal, and Ive had experience with a lot of them in the physics department. Im the type of person that finds it difficult to pay attention during lecture and I learn from reading the book, but with Crommie, it was completely the oppositeI learned everything just watching him lecture. Caring guy 2.

I seriously cannot believe how great this guy is. Please, please, please take him! Youll be doing yourself a disservice by picking someone else. Go to every office hour! Youll learn more and seeing from Crommies lectures, repetition is key to learning physics. Hes not trying to trick you, hes there to help you learn. I was very afraid of

analysis.name: Cruz Carlos
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Incredibly kind and caring professor, wish he could teach every CivE class! Cruz only taught labs for CE60 this semester but I learned more from him than the lecturer. Very engaging and tends to build relationships with his classes over time.

Cruz is an amazing professor! He deeply cares about his students and makes you love the topic of the class, despite how boring it may initially seem. He focuses heavily on learning, so midterms are take home and unlimited attempts. Labs are super fun and worthwhile even though the lab reports can be a lot of work. I highly recommend!

Prof. Carlos is amazing! His lectures are extremely engaging, and helps you understand the material much more than the textbook (go to class!). The labs and accompanying lab reports can be long but aside from that, the class is reasonable. HW weekly, but it isn't too much. Carlos is very passionate about materials and makes the class very fun. :)

Professor Carlos has such a cheerful attitude and genuine passion for his area of study that you can't help but enjoy learning about seemingly, and deceivingly, mundane topics such as the type of rocks you use to make concrete. The workload was concise and to the point. I also never thought I'd be excited for concrete to dry just to crush it.

Best professor I've had at Berkeley so far! Professor Carlos is very accommodating + friendly. Tests are fair and short: all q's are taken from lecture content. Labs are hands-on + v interesting. Professors like Carlos at Berkeley are rare--he is both very knowledgeable on his subject and very good at explaining it. Would take again 100%

analysis.name: Cristina Farronato
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: A truly wonderful professor. Always smiling and exuding a warm vibe. Super clear and easy to follow instruction, highly accessible, and truly cares that her students do well. You wont regret taking her.

I could not recommend Cristina more! She is so caring and attentive as a professor, and consistently gives great feedback. 
She's a really kind grader, and will often give you points for effort if she can tell you understand
Professoressa Farronato is a really really nice person and an amazing instructor. Totally recommend her classes!

analysis.name: G Cristina Mora
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class sucked. I thought it would be such an interesting topic but her lectures were terrible. I came to every class and still got a D because who ever was my reader graded harshly. Readings were not talked about in lecture much but were heavy on exam. WORST prof at CAL i have had although she is nice, her class stinks.

Good researcher. Readings mostly from top journals such as AJS or ASR. Sound preparation for Socio major who wants to go to graduate school. (Ivester, for example, focuses on empirical side) However, hard for non-major who happens to be interested in culture or wants to fulfill Arts/Literature Breadth in terms of both content and grading.

Professor Mora will do more than teach you- she will inspire and really educate you. Even on uncomfortable topics, Professor Mora emphasizes the importance of education, plus she makes every lecture exciting and worth attending. Regularly reading-based in-class quizzes keep you on your toes, so attendance is mandatory.

Her class is hard to follow but not hard to get an A in, because she gives you all of the exam questions before each midterm which are 3- each 30% of your grade. If you get a good study group together its super easy to do well in the class with little effort. Super dry readings and horrible, bare slides but interesting material and a fairly easy A!

Professor Mora is the definition of a success story and always provides the class with material and motivation so we too can become one. She's so smart, funny, and a great resource. If you're looking for inspiration on being an absolute boss in Sociology- she's your girl to model after. Take her class!

analysis.name: Craig Miller
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Super fun and amazing!! I loved this course so much and I felt that it was really well structured and just overall super informative. Craig Miller is one of my favorite professors here at Cal and I highly recommend!! He helps with all questions and takes the time to help his students succeed. I feel that he genuinely cares for his students.

He is a very nice person and very much willing to help, but his part of class "genomics" was the hardest for me. He speaks too fast and if English is your second language, may God help you. I recorded his lectures and tried to listen to him at home to understand him. The average of the class was high for his exam, so maybe it's me and my English!

Professor Miller is the nicest professor I have ever had. He is adorable. Many people complain that he's monotonous during lecture, but he is extremely helpful during office hours. He will stay in office hours as long as there are questions and will often stay for HOURS. I love this man.

I thought I would hate this section but he actually did a pretty good job of making the subject interesting and easy to study. Recorded lectures, knew them backwards and forwards, and aced the exam. Pretty dry in lecture but I feel like I actually understand genomics!

A bit monotone but he makes the material he teaches actually interesting and applicable to medicine/bio. He always has a slide that lists all the key concepts from the lecture, and those are really pretty much all you need to know. His section isn't much memorization and is mostly conceptual, which I appreciated. Good professor all around

analysis.name: John Cutler
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Cutler was an exceptional individual who genuinely prioritized teaching. Throughout each lecture, his commitment to the subject matter was evident as he actively engaged with students, asking for their thoughts on the assigned readings. We had a few quizzes, collaborative efforts were allowed, and only two essays were required.

few discussions and quizzes, and there's only 2 essays to do. everything is based on the readings/what we learned in class. our grade depends on what we think we deserve which is amazing! he's hilarious and truly one of the best professors in the English department. take a class with him if you can!

[For ENG 37] Prof. Cutler is an amazing, caring professor who clearly cares about everything he has hand-picked to teach. He feels like a friend telling you about something cool he learned about in class, and his constant re-centering around historic and cultural relevance is on point. Occasional quizzes in class and attendance mandatory.

Really nice, interesting professor. Very kind and respectful. His grading is fair but my experience with his GSI was pretty bad. The GSI graded super harshly and had a bad attitude when the professor called them out on it after seeing their feedback on my paper. Cutler himself tho is wonderful. 4 papers + group project, manageable reading schedule

Professor Cutler is new to Berkeley, and he is kind and smart. He incorporates many things into grades (quizzes, a group project, papers, attendance). Your grade relies too much on the pretentious reader; I got an A- on the first paper and he said the paper is amazing but you still get an A- because no one is perfect and I'm nitpicky like that

analysis.name: Timothy Crockett
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 39 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He is really knowledgeable and his lectures do a great job breaking down the dense material from readings. Do the readings! At least skim them and get a general idea of what to expect. You don't have to fully understand the reading though because it can be difficult. There are three midterm essays and he gives out a study guide for the final!

One of the best philosopher professor I ever have! His lecture may seem hard to grasp at first (b/c of all the terms), but TAKE DOWN HIS LECTURE WORD FOR WORD. Then, his lectures become REALLY CLEAR. Much clearer than the reading itself! Readings are the original text translated; IMHO, a summary would have been better for this intro class

Took Professor Crockett with GSI Jenny this spring for Leibniz. The material is challenging but Jenny and Crockett are kind and super cool. The goal is for you to actually go out into the world and be able to speak on the material. Graded by 3 papers and 1 final. Definitely an upper division class to add if you actually want to "learn something"

3 papers and an in-class final centered around lectures. You can do the reading at home, but ideas presented by Prof, including  interpretations of certain passages, are essential knowledge for success on papers. So, lectures are mandatory in spirit. Extremely responsive to Q's and is sincerely invested in student understanding. Amazing Prof.

Very clear, calm and accessible professor. Philosophical concepts can be hard to grasp, but Tim breaks it down in a nice and thorough way. His lectures are so clear and to the point that even if you don't do the readings you'll probably find his lectures sufficient (it's a very reading-heavy course).

analysis.name: Lincoln Cushing
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Such a sweetheart. You can tell he is incredibly passionate about the things he teaches about. Class assignments are incredibly easy and straightforward. We even took a field trip to his house where he showcased his vintage poster collection and fed us bagels. I would 100% take again.
Such a sweet Professor, loved my summer Berkeley experience because of him!
He was honestly amazing one of the best classes I have taken. He truly cares for you and you will enjoy this class

analysis.name: Kurt Cuffey
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Cuffey is undoubtedly my favorite teacher, and his GEOG 140A course stands out as the most enjoyable class I've taken. His extensive knowledge, enthusiasm, and genuine care for students truly set him apart. While his jokes may not leave you in stitches, they certainly bring a smile to your face and brighten your day.

Cuffey is a great professor. very nice and engaging in lectures and definitely very knowledgeable. Make sure to prep for the tests but the exams do seem pretty fair though, mostly multiple-choice and all stuff he covered in lecture. Just take detailed notes and enjoy the ride! I highly recommend taking a class from Cuffey, 100% would take it again.

Prof Cuffey is a fun, knowledgable instructor. Works hard to ensure students understand  and uses humor to make class enjoyable. Okay with laptops and photos of diagrams for later review. Uses self-made handbook for note taking which is helpful and many photo slides to further concepts. Tests can be tough, so take good notes and you'll learn a lot!

I love physical geography and this is the best class I have taken since I transferred to UCB. Prof. Kurt is humorous. It helps me stay awake in class. I don't mean the class is boring but it is tough so it requires a lot of energy and focus during class. Sit in the front and take detail notes. Put a lot of markings on your map. Don't skip class!!!!

Cuffey is one of the best professors I had at Cal. He has an easygoing style of lecturing that is both enlightening and entertaining--he's really funny! You need to go to class otherwise its easy to get behind. And know specific exs of landforms he talks about on the US map the class requires for tests. Not an easy class but not hard if you study.

analysis.name: Tanja Cuk
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She's very inexperienced with teaching. Lecture materials are not as well organized and are from mostly places other than the course textbook. She only writes with chalk and the class is very fast-paced and hard to follow.

Her notes were beautiful and I really like her blazers. Tests were difficult, but fair. I wish she made her lectures more personal, but it was probably due to the dense nature of the material. I suggest reading the txtbook before the lecture. Labs and hw are a decent chunk of the grade so don't slack. Really enjoyed this class :)

Tanja gives extremely clear lectures, especially important since quantum chemistry your first semester can be really difficult. The problem sets were relevant, and both midterms in her half of the class were hard, but fair. Many people said her office hours were extremely helpful, but I personally didn't go to them.

Very engaging lectures. She covers tough stuff, but I always walked out feeling informed and curious to learn more.  Tests follow exactly what she covers in lecture, so the textbook is just a supplement. Labs and homework are all from the GSI team, but she does her personal part very well. Bonus: Cool demos.

At first many students including myself were caught off guard by the fast paced and dense lectures, but after the first few I really came to appreciate how well she knew her stuff and explained tough concepts. Assignments were really interesting  and challenging but helped me learn. Tests were fair.

analysis.name: David Culler
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Doesn't seem to care about teaching at the undergrad level. I had a doctor's appointment and missed the lecture before the midterm, so I missed directions to memorize the section number (five digit code) to write on the exam. I wrote the time and TA's name instead. He marked me down an entire letter grade on the exam despite my TA trying to help.

Culler is not a good lecturer or interesting speaker despite his high HKN ratings. Midterms 1/2 were pretty easy, but midterm 3 was very difficult. Lectures have no format/organization, avoid Culler and try to take CS150 with Katz if you can. Culler (or his staff) also has many problems with course logistics (for example, getting hw solutions out).

CS162 is one of the hardest cs classes but its my favorite by far because of Culler. No one goes to his office hours so I basically got private tutoring two days a week. He also often asked how I thought certain homeworks/projects/exams were and how they could be improved and seemed to take my feedback seriously. Overall a very caring guy :)
A reasonably good lecturer, but the labs were always more helpful.  I think he would've done better if he had more than, like, 12 lectures per semester.

Do not take the lab format of this class and do not take it from Culler.  Wait for Dan Garcia to teach it.  Culler only gave 10 lectures and wasn't clear at all.  The only students who did well watched Garcia's webcasts and skipped class, seriously!

analysis.name: Matt Culler
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: With surgical focus, he stared at me and said "I'm willing to reach out, get into your head"

You know, Matt was super nice for this class. He was always willing to help, and if you actually just TALK to him he's pretty chill. He's even nice about essays. Basically he's just a chill dude. Always willing to meet for office hours and talk about the material.

One of the worst GSI in the department. He has his favorite students and the students he likes to torment for no reason. Also he is absolutely no help in understanding the material - doesn't talk clearly and often told us different things from what was said in class.
Very helpful teacher and interesting lecturer.
doesn't know anything. he would look at his notes the entire lecture and made the material so so uninteresting and confusing. ugh and i love art history but this class was a DUD

analysis.name: Sean Curran
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Sean is the most caring prof I've had at Cal. He is very knowledgeable and passionate. He is straightforward with the class for when we need to step it up which is great because I want my teachers to push me to be better. He is great in OH, going above and beyond to help in any way. Lastly, he is funny and has a great singing voice. Thanks Sean!

Sean was probably one of the most articulate, entertaining, and intellectual GSI's I've had the pleasure of taking a class from. He occasionally strays from lecture topics, which are quite clear and interesting, to discuss personal topics and current events (which is a reason to not skip class). Take his class, you won't regret it!

You'll be lucky if you get him as your teacher..why you ask? because he is the best thing ever. he has a fabulous teaching style, sense of humor(we cried from laughter severl times), and he knows absolutely everything. seriously...he loves music, and teaching. You'll know everything about musicianship after...

Prior to taking the class, I honestly was not anticipating much and was hoping for the class to be a easy A. However, Sean really delivers the material in an interesting and engaging way. I definitely spent more effort in this class than I anticipated. However, I felt that I actually learned something in the end.

When rating Sean, thou shalt rate him 5, no more, no less. 5 shall be the rating thou shalt give, and the rating thou shalt give will be 5. Thou shalt not rate him 6, nor shall thou rate him 4, except that thou then proceed to 5. 7 is right out. Thanks for the great semester Sean!

analysis.name: Mary Cudahy
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Really great class. Inspired by teacher and material. Challenging, but interesting and engaging. Prof Cudahy was very accessible for help, and obviously wanted her students to thrive and grow in their writing/analysis abilities. One of the best Ive taken at Berkeley.
I absolutely loved this class. It's what inspired me to declare my major. With papers, you write once, get it back, revise it, and turn it in for the actual grade= very good.
You will write four 6-10 page papers. As long as you do the majority of the 25-50 pages of reading per class you will be peachy.Small class=good

Out of the music 20a teachers, daniel is by FAR the best, he is very funny and will help you individually alot if you need it

analysis.name: Cynthia Aban

review_highlights.comment: Loved taking class with Tita Chat! She made the material very easy to understand, and I feel like my Filipino definitely improved! It may be a bit tough for people who have never had any exposure to the language, but if you've heard a lot of Filipino growing up this class will be an easy A.

Tita Chat was a great professor. She deeply cares for her students and their success, and made herself easily available outside of class for outside help. The class itself requires a lot of verbal participation in order to better understand the material. 10/10, would recommend this class to anyone who wants to take a fun and relatively easy class.

She is a great professor who only wants the best for her students when it comes to learning Filipino. She's a bit difficult to get in touch with outside of class, but use her for help as much as you can because she is funny and informational. You do need to attend class because that is your grade and gives you answers to exams.

such a wonderful and caring professor! such a chill and entertaining class! even if you're not fluent in the language, you can easily pass the class with an A. one thing is that textbook is required 99% of the lectures and take advantage of her review sheets, they'll definitely help you out on the quizzes/midterm/final exam.

analysis.name: Cynthia Looy
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: 1/3 professors that taught BIO1B for Fall 2022 semester. She taught the plants/organismal biology section. Wasn't super respected by a lot of my peers for her odd teaching style and difficult exams. I thought she was fine. The average grade for the plants section midterm was low, and her test questions were oddly specific. Study well for her exams.

The lecture and slides lack coherence and organization. A systematic exploration of large-scale evolutionary trends is notably absent. As someone with a background in biology Olympiads, although I have no trouble understanding her lecture, I'm still disappointed by the overall quality of the lectures, which caused confusion in many of my classmates

I am sure she is a nice person but she just reads off the slides and it doesn't help that she is the one teaching the hardest unit of the class too. Many typos in her exams and some questions had to be redacted from hers. Her section of labs were the worst and her midterm averages were the lowest.

Looy's lectures are interesting, especially when she talks about her field of study (paleobotany). Be prepared to know lots of specifics for her exam. The exam itself had some questions we did not go over in the lecture at all and had to be re-graded for everyone several times. However, this was also due to other confounding factors this semester.

I loved Paleobotany. I learned a lot about the Earth's history through the lens of plant evolution. Lectures and powerpoints were clear, the textbook was accessible, and labs were sometimes difficult, but the GSI was there to guide. If you're into plant morphology and learning about ancient climates, you will enjoy.

analysis.name: Cybelle Fox
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The class itself is super interesting, but I personally don't like how she reads off her notes most of the time rather than lecturing off the top of her head, lectures get boring like that. But she is knowledgeable and encourages conversation in class. Super friendly and very approachable. 1 paper 1 final and 5 weekly reading responses.

Prof Fox is great at explaining concepts from readings. Gives a lot of examples (videos, graphs, images) and brings in things that are currently happening. A lot of key terms for midterm and final, but she gives them all in a study sheet. Also gives exact questions that will be on the final.

She is inspiring and interesting and so kind. Loved the class and learned a lot. Do the reading, and participate in your section. GSI was fair grader and interesting! Class discussions are interesting because the class has students from so many different backgrounds.

Prof. Fox is great in the sense that she is very knowledgable. However, I was only taking this class as breadth, not for interest or major requirement. That being said, I wouldn't pick this class if I had other options; there are easier breadth courses if you want an easy A. This class requires too much work and the material, to me, is SO boring.

Dr. Fox is fantastic. She only assigns relevant, illuminating readings; gives useful feedback & lecture material; & has dedicated her life to understanding the complexities of U.S. social welfare policies. She's brilliant; inspiring; accessible; down to earth; & an indispensable resource in every way - for both the U.S. as a whole & my own ed.!

analysis.name: Daniel Kasen
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dan is the best. So lovable and such a great teacher! I was actually sad when I had to miss one of his lectures. Definitely go to his office hours because he's really helpful and super fun to talk to about everything. His tests are fair and doing the homeworks thoroughly is useful. (Also read his comments on the homework because they're hilarious!)

He makes it easy to get up at 7:30am three days a week to learn about stat mech; need I say more? He writes his own lecture notes and problem sets, both of which involve all sorts of interesting questions & applications.

He is among the best, if not the best professor in the Physics department. If you have a chance to take a class with him, do it.

I took 161 with Professor Kasen and truly, one of the most amazing professors I have ever had. If I could rate him a 10/5, I would. If I could rate him a 100/5, I would. If I could somehow give him a Nobel Prize for being the best professor, I would. He really loves what he teaches and you can tell he genuinely wants everyone to succeed. Incredible

It's not even halfway through the semester, but I already know this is going to be the best class I have ever taken. He is AMAZING at writing homework that helps you learn as you do it, and his lectures make perfect sense. Asking a question? He answers it precisely and in a way that is super easy to understand. TAKE DAN KASEN WHENEVER POSSIBLE!

C161 isn't appearing on the courses he's taught so I'm reviewing that. Prof. Kasen is the best physics professor I've had at Cal. He really puts effort into helping you learn though lectures and homework assignments. Office hours are super helpful and conversations can go in all sorts of fun directions.

analysis.name: David Shuster
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: If you are looking for a nice Physical Science Breadth, like I was, do NOT take this class. Although the professor is accessible and kind, his lectures are just him babbling about random sh*t that has somewhat to do with what he is meaning to teach. The test will be on the readings and not on his lectures :/

One of those profs who likes to hear himself talk, is monotone and dry, and rarely finishes on time. Slides are good, but he did skip some he didn't know, then told us to review it for the exams. Exams asked us about obscure facts and values not overarching concepts.  Felt like waste of what this class could be with a better professor.

EPS 50 is a very dense, memorization-heavy intro to geology course with small margins for error, so if you want a fun or 'easy' physical science breadth, I would recommend looking elsewhere. For those who need it for their major, good luck!

That said, he presents the content well, so you should probably go to lecture if you take his class.

I loved Prof Shuster. Not only was EPS 124 super interesting, but he was always ready to help whenever I had questions. He made time for one on one office hours as well! Be sure to attend discussion section because he walks you through problem sets. FYI it was also my first upper division so I didn't know what to expect, but I am so glad I took it!

Disregard the previous comment, this student is clearly bitter and is providing misinformation. He does not babble, in fact his lectures are incredibly meaningful and relevant. Power points are very long, but all the information is there.  Test is comparable to reading and lecture. Lots of work in this class, especially labs. I have an 84% so far.

analysis.name: Demian Pouzo
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The worst professor ever. In the course, we covered 11 chapters, chapters 1-5 were on midterm 1. 6-10 on midterm 2, and chapter 11 was left for the final. We were told the final would be cumulative but we were tested entirely on chapter 11. Exams are very difficult and the grading structure is 90% exams (25%each midterm 40%final) and 10% homework.

I have never seen this. Professor respond to a single student question or even acknowledge anything on Ed despite the numerous attempt many students have made every single month about class policy/feedback!!! 90% exam weighted, no midterm drops or clobber or curve. Says final will be cumulative multiple times, then makes the final only on Unit 11..

Without a curve or clobber policy, your grade relies entirely on three high-stakes tests (25/25/40), and there is zero curve or policy to help your grade. Despite being told the final would be cumulative, it focused almost exclusively on the final handout. The professor is totally MIA on Ed Discussion. Extremely misleading and disorganized. 1/5.

The exam was explicitly said to be cumulative, and students wasted hours studying the concepts.
The final focused almost entirely on highly specific content from Handout 11. That is not what a cumulative exam implies, and it is misleading. 
The most deceitful class I've taken at Cal. Midterms were fine, but the state of the final is inexcusable.

Course design was a disaster. 90% of grade is 3 exams. Practice problems appeared word for word on exams, but practice problem answers were not released and were difficult to get out of GSI OH. Good luck if you have mandatory class during OH like me. Frequent grading errors (be ready to regrade request) and some questions answer keys were incorrect

analysis.name: Devin Leigh
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: One of my favorite professors I've had! He provided all necessary material information in an engaging and straightforward way. I always looked forward to lectures, every week was interesting. Your grade is based on weekly written assignments, 2 midterms, and a final so be sure to do your best. I recommend taking this class if you have the chance!

This class was my favorite class I took in FPF at Berkeley. Professor Leigh has a very engaging teaching style and the content of the course really changed my perspective on many things. His rubric and grading is clear---as long as you do the work the way he wants you will get an A! I recommend taking this class!

I loved this professor, no need to buy books he gives you all assigned reading. It is very clear how to succeed in this course. Conversations with him are amazing and I learned a lot in his class. Go to his office hours to get to know him if you can. He really cares about his students. I cannot recommend him enough.

He's one of the most amazing professors I've encountered here. You can tell he really cares about the success of his students. He provides great feedback and has the patience to discuss every student's questions and ideas, whether that's in class or in office hours. If you have the chance to take a class with him, I highly recommend it.

Absolutely amazing professor. His course content was really interesting and I feel that the workload he gave was extremely reasonable. We had to do one reading a week and one reflection a week. You should do your readings fully because that's what the reflections are testing. Apart from that, he's friendly, understanding and accommodating.

analysis.name: Brian Delay
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 71 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I LOVE Brian DeLay! Hands down BEST professor at this school. Hilarious, incredibly intelligent, and engaging. History 7A made me a history major and I recommend it to all of my friends. I plan to take as many of his classes as possible in my remaining time at Cal. Cannot recommend him highly enough. Take his class, you will love it!

Had his class back in Fall 2024, genuinely such an amazing professor. You could tell he was honestly interested in what he taught and made sure students could be interested too. Teaches amazingly and as long as you take notes and do the homework you'll probably get an A.

Professor DeLay was amazing! I took this class to fulfill a requirement and he made it super easy to follow along and feel like I was learning. Even online his lectures felt really engaging and it made the information really interesting. It was also super easy to access him if I needed help and he was super friendly so it wasn't scary to reach out.

Do yourself a favor and take a class with Professor DeLay. The class was lecture heavy but VERY engaging. You need to show up to lecture to do well. He imitated a Protestant preacher one class which was incredible. I'm not a history major but am so glad I took this class. He's the most passionate lecturer I've had at Cal and that's huge for me.

Watching lectures/attending is mandatory to pass. Readings not so much. DeLay makes history very language accessible, don't worry about not knowing these big a@@ words, he's very straight forward/adds his sense of humor/character into history. Super accessible teacher, he responds quick to email. Would take again! I loved his class.

analysis.name: Michael Deweese
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 62 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: His lectures are absolutely useless. He teaches you the bare minimum, yet his homework and tests expect that you have a complete understanding of each topic. Take this guy's class if you'd like to spend hours teaching yourself from the book.

It was so hard to get any feedback from this class. Even though they emphasized the importance of written homework at the beginning of semester and made it mandatory for us to work on them every week, they ended up not grading any of those. Tests were tough, but they were interesting and I liked them.

Lectures were interesting, but more of a complement to the reading. He went over theories and derivations often, which made the book material more clear. I went to lecture only about half of the time. Test questions were similar (sometimes identical!) to homework and practice problems.
DeWeese has amazing drawing skills, and is a fairly nice professor. Homework is the usual MasteringPhysics fare, and the exams were pretty tough too, with quite a few tricky questions in each exam.

Deweese was great for the online Physics 8A! He genuinely loves Physics and brings that passion into his lectures. I used to hate physics because I had a series of awful teachers, but Deweese explains the material in a digestible way + fun drawings. Hard class regardless, but great prof.

analysis.name: Matthew Denham
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: He's a great professor and super chill. He's very funny and won't judge you at all. He wants everyone to do their best. I would 100% recommend him to anyone who takes a phys ed class.
Amazing instructor, was nervous at first for taking a swim class but it really is an entry level class. Doesn't judge and is very encouraging and chill. 10/10 recommend.

Super down to earth and chill guy, wants his class to be fun. Wants to develop close relationships with all of his students, regardless of whether or not they are super skilled in the class. Has a lot of funky games as well to encourage bonding. Also very accommodating and doesn't make fun of people who are struggling

Matthew Denham is the best teacher I've ever had. His class is fun, and he always makes sure not to challenge people to the point where they don't want to try anymore. He's super helpful, and extremely understanding in all situations. Taking his class is a nice way to get through the week, and I would recommend that everyone should take his course.

If you need an outlet from school and a great way to meet new people and get some good exercise, take Mr. Denham's PE classes. He is the most enthusiastic and friendly teacher, and he creates a very positive environment for the students, so that it doesn't feel like a mandatory class and more like a fun activity outside of school. The BEST teacher!

audited in the course. amazing lecturer. after his lecture, I really want to transfer to aerospace engeering.

this isn't said lightly as a gender studies student.

It was her first time teaching when I took her class and it was fine. Definitely more relaxed personality than Dr.Head-Gordon. She herself took Chem 4A (and aced it) so she knows what she is talking about. Hopefully a teacher that will improve over time.
A very clear professor. She was funny and sincere about helping students and providing mentorship and guidance. i wish i could take more classes from her.
she is extremely nice and well educated and so helpful her test is easy, she is so smart and try to never  miss her because its can effect your grade

extremely BAD professor. French accent, can't explain the material well, and always makes mistakes during his prove (students have to correct him all the time). His grading system sucks! The textbook was not that bad, but he makes us memorizing EVERY theorem and proposition!!!

review_highlights.comment: The prof was really nice, but her class is unorganized. She cancelled 3 classes and had another 3 taught by librarians; it's like she didn't want to teach. There was no actual course content, it was lowkey just yapping. Easy A, but you don't learn and it's frustrating how unorganized and unclear the assignments are. Wtf is a conversational exam!

Took her for PS124W and it was her first semester teaching at Berkeley and it showed. She's really nice and caring, even changed grades/due dates to accommodate students, but this class was disorganized and confusing at times. The GSI and the professor were not 100% aligned on grading or even rubrics for projects worth 25%+ of the grade.

I don't get the animosity toward Dr. Wang. She's an awesome professor. She's super knowledgeable, approachable, and teaches some of the most engaging classes I've had at Cal. The material is interesting, relatable to everyday life, and I really liked the variety of class activities. I learned a lot in her class!!!

analysis.name: Alex Dimakis
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment:
Great lecturer. Bad curve (1-2 grade bins lower than prev years). Class content is straightforward. Very generous in extending DDLs. After MT1, the class went slow, and we didn't finish content

Homework, exams r not similar to lectures. EE120 is a smaller workload class. Too few TAs, thus nobody answers questions on Ed, upload lecture notes.

He just started at Berkeley this year, but I already love his class so much. I've heard in the past that signals and systems is a hard class, but he makes it not seem as bad as it probably is. With many clear in-lecture examples and a engaging teaching style, he has easily become one of if not my favorite professors in Berkeley.

Great Professor and made sure everyone understood what he was teaching. Hw was long, but I think this was always the case for the class, but grading for assignments were very nice. ***Grade bin was very off of previous semesters, only ~17% received an A or above compared to previous semesters 30+%.

analysis.name: Dipti Nayak
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Nayak was a great and passionate lecturer who broke down complex topics in a simple and eloquent manner. She also specified what reading was relevant on slides which enhanced studying. Exams were difficult but she also posted what topics are going to be covered. Cheat sheet allowed on exam.

Her lectures provided tons of examples and how to approach them, and she was a great lecturer, providing visual elements through the chalkboard and much more. She was approachable and kind. Her section had a fair exam, and I do feel her personal notes assisted in studying.
Very clear lectures with extra practice problems. She is very kind and has useful annotated slides ontop of the practice problems. Definitely one of my favorite professors from Cal.
Absolutely GOATED professor. I loved her, and highly recommend!!

analysis.name: Diana Negrin Da Silva
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Very chill professor who is clearly passionate about her work, and has interesting lectures. She assigns a lot of reading (you can skim them, but I found most to be engaging), and the grade consists of 3 papers and 4 reading responses. She does tend to go on tangents a lot and get off track when answering questions, but still engaging overall.

Professor Negrin is very passionate about her topic which creates an engaging lecture albeit long. Has extra credit opportunities but for minimal points. Only 3 graded written assignments and small discussion assignments. The final project is really interesting and you have freedom to choose your format. Grade booster class honestly, def recommend.

there were 3 straightforward papers and 4 reading responses. and if anything comes up, just talk to her about it. she's super chill and awesome. i loved everything we read and i found them to be foundational texts that I continued to reference in my classes I took later on

Super nice but is hand-wavy. Spends most of class discussing her research with a specific indigenous tribe in Mexico--everything comes back to that constantly. Heavy focus on "natural" systems--this is not a class that is a survey of political environmental movements. Not super organized. However, it's an easy class and has chill and fun lectures.
Negrin is a truly passionate and brilliant professor who cares deeply about her students. Could not recommend enough!

analysis.name: Diego Evans
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Overall, an exciting & intriguing class with lots of cool guest speakers, but co-taught & instructors often gave confusing &/or contradictory feedback, making it hard to iterate on group design assignments. It's evident that Digeo cares deeply for the class & students; however, despite corrective efforts, grading criteria were incredibly unclear

Instructor Diego cares for his students; he often checks for understanding and emails extra resources. Almost the entire course was based around one harshly-graded (but not difficult) group project, a slideshow presentation. We receive very positive feedback in class, but extremely low grades later on; assignment expectations were not very clear.

Diego is a great person and a super nice guy that cares about his students wellbeing. But, he is very confusing, this could have been due to a language barrier but seems like it is just difficult for him to articulate his thoughts. He gave conflicting instructions and unclear feedback to students. Very hard to understand objectives and assignments.

Had so many bad professors for SED leading up to Diego, where he was the professor that was dedicated, engaging, and grounded.
He structured the class around real-world work that made the capstone feel impactful. Though he brings so much to the table, it is important to be proactive in keeping him up to date on your work and team for a good grade.

Good project in theory, but difficult to execute. We were assigned a project in East Palo Alto (~2.5 hours away). Throughout the project, we were given positive feedback, so we assumed we needed minor improvement. However, once we submitted our final project, we were graded harshly. There was a lack of organization and communication.

analysis.name: Diane Dwyer
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I enjoyed this class and the professor. There are some amazing guest speakers from high up careers in marking and PR which is great. The only thing I did not like was how heavy the workload was on the group project. The requirements to me required a lot more than what a 2 unit class should require. But Diane is great and I learned a lot.

You do have to do some work, a lot of homework and a lot of group projects but the hw is pretty easy. Gives good feedback and wants to get to know her students she requires we all do ONE office hour appointment. I really like her though. Only had one exam (the final) and she told us what would be on it in her review session, she's nice.

it was o,, not great. It felt passive, at the end we had to take a big test but we didn't necessarily follow a curriculum so I was upset that the class was not  more organized so I can prepare for a test. We didn't follow a textbook or anything.  I can't say I learned anything. it felt superficial and not organized.
Fantastic teacher! Super relatable and kind, I highly reccomend her!!!!!!!
Great class! It was great working with real clients and presenting to the CEOs.

analysis.name: Dimitrios Konstantinidis
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Makes the final, which is worth about 40% of your overall grade, the hardest thing you have ever taken or done in the class. He will take the smallest topic or detail that is briefly mentioned and create an entire problem out of it that is worth 25% of the final. He needs to learn how to be fair to his students.

Clearly doesn't know how to make final exams that are feasible for students (especially with the final exam being worth 40%). It seems like he includes "interesting" topics that are rarely discussed in class out of pure amusement for himself.

Exams are difficult but not the worst, but the material on the final is the hardest and midterm 2 was also pretty hard. Exams were similar to practice exams. Some hw involved matlab so going to OH really helps to figure out what functions to use and how to debug your code. He will sit with you until you understand the material. Great professor!

analysis.name: Zhiyan Ding
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I took MATH 217 with him at Michigan and while his quizzes were harder than most sections, he dropped a significant amount of your lowest grades at the end of the semester so the grades were about the same as the other sections. He is very nice and is always smiling and laughing. Great professor and I definitely recommend taking 217 with him!

His Chinese accent is sometimes unclear during lecture. However, he makes up for it by providing quality typeset lecture notes that can basically replace the textbook (I studied out of just the notes). The only thing I did not enjoy about his class were the somewhat excessive difficulties of his exams, as compared to other professors this spring.

Prof Ding is hands down the best math prof I have taken a course with. His lectures are clear and easy to understand, and his notes are amazing (super organized + clear). I hardly had to use the textbook thanks to his notes. He is also very friendly and approachable in office hours. The course is hard simply due to the nature of the subject.

The best lectures I have had! The professor cared a lot about the student experience in class and put a lot of effort into class. In addition to the lectures and textbook (Ross), he provided his own notes as well. His lectures, notes, and the textbook all provided unique perspectives on the content. Highest of quality, highly suggest!

analysis.name: Peng Ding
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

review_highlights.comment: Peng seems awesome!  I think he'd be great in a grad level stats class. He is really nice and passionate. I feel like he's maybe not a match for data102 though because he tends to go a bit more into theory rather than stay on track with what's in scope. I feel like i miss a lot of what he lectures about due to the fact that I struggle with proofs.

Peng is a good professor if you ask him questions specifically about the topic, but the way he lectures requires lots of statistical maturity, and his lectures often go into complex proofs rather than explanations in comparison to Ramesh's easy to follow along slides. If there were slides for every lecture, the class would be easier to understand.

He's a really intelligent guy and clearly knowledgeable about causal inference, but hard to follow. I feel like his lectures require a level of mathematical maturity beyond the prereqs or scope of the class. I read the textbook and brush up on topics beforehand, but leave his lectures confused. I've heard that he's a nice guy in person.
This class was quite difficult, coming from STAT 135, and his lectures are hardly understandable. However, go to lab sections and stay on top of the textbook materia,l and you'll do fine
Absolute unit of a professor! He's smart, sharp, and you're in for a treat taking the class with him. My one concern is his naming convention. Variables names in his book are stacked!!

analysis.name: Djordje Popovic
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Amazing Prof. Very caring and interesting. One of my favorites at Berkeley!

NO.1 FAN OF POPOVIC! Feels like my intellectual level has been improved by 10 times after attending his class for one semester. Although it's a literature class, he would always bring in history and philosophy into the discussion. In terms of grading he's chill, but if you DO want to learn and participate in class you'd better do all the readings.

Took SLAVIC 39N - not sure why it isn't in the dropdown. The only assignments are weekly discussion boards & ex cred. No midterm or final. Even though the class meets once a week for 2 hours, Professor Popovic makes every meeting interesting! He is knowledgeable and enthusiastic about his subject. As long as you do the discussions, it's an easy A.

I literally made an account just to rate Djordje. HE IS THE BEST!!!!!!!! I've never had a more understanding or supportive teacher. He is charmingly long-winded and will work to make the class work for you. Though there is much reading to do, he gives incredible insight while allowing for your own interpretation. TAKE CLASS WITH HIM!

Easily one of the best professors in the department, if not the university. A classic educator, more emphasis placed on discussion, synthesis, analysis, and understanding than on points and grades. Definitely a must-take.

Ethan was such a great professor this semester. His lectures were incredibly clear and straightforward. However, the best part of his class was him entertaining us. His personality and looks are a 10/10. Most definitely recommend taking his class;)
One of the best. And we can't forget how cute he is.
Amazing instructor who tries to get us excited about the beauty of mathematics. Plus, super friggin hot - this man is a total specimen and I would do anything to be his forever.
Thanks to Ethan, I succeeded at getting a B-. In no-time, I will be pursuing a PhD in applied mathematics!

analysis.name: Dmitry Vaintrob

He lectured during RRR week (against university policy) because he "forgot RRR week existed."

He is a very nice professor and very understanding. I had him during the pandemic (when everything was online) and he was probably my only STEM professor that cared about the well being of his students. Although he does take awhile to grade, everything that is on his tests he has covered before. He doesnt try to throw hard balls or trick anyone.

A smart and nice professor. I received my first "not A" grade in math in his class at Berkeley, so this class is the hardest from my perspective. But his lectures are pretty interesting! The most interesting class I have ever had online. Would take again for p/np not for graded and simply enjoy his lectures :P
He seemed to care a lot more than most of my other professors, especially online. Sometimes he would grade assignments slowly, but he was always fair. He seems super smart
Hard professor but fair, genuine and legitimately cared about his students. Get ready to work.

analysis.name: Dmitry Taubinsky

review_highlights.comment: He always spend lots of time to present useless stuff. Problem set is not related to his lecture. Even his GSI did a better teach job than himself. DO NOT waste your precious time in CAL to take his class. totally USELESS .

Terrible. This class used to have an A- average, but I'm pretty sure he curved it to a B/B- for an upper division Econ class at Cal, which usually curves to a B+. His grading criteria was super confusing, and I felt really unprepared. Also, he didn't release final exam grades. No regrade requests. He obviously doesn't care about his students.

Lectures are filled with hundreds of half relevent behavioral experiments, psets are difficult because technical problems are never gone over in class. Got an A in 100A/100B/ Stats20 and yet my GPA was tanked by this class. Went into the final with a 94 and came out with a B, despite mastering every pset. Whole grading process is a black box.
Hes terrible, unclear, and unhelpful. His problem sets are even more useless than him. Take someone else unless you are interested in bringing down your GPA for fun.

analysis.name: Jennifer Doudna
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
Dear Dr. Doudna,

Your field needs to get to classification systems, founded on common principles, so science can develop over time. An example of this, is developing work from constant STEM principles for a strong solution or frame. Start with the most stable laws like physics (math), versus chemistry (fluctuate).

The class is not curved so good luck soldiers. Very difficult to fail this class but also very difficult to get an A. Doudna is not bad at teaching but it is clear she is only teaching because its required. Focuses more heavily on crispr and random genetic testing stuff in tests even though it was not covered.

I know that Doudna is an extremely well accomplished biochemist but with that being said she should NOT be teaching a general bio class. Her lectures were dense and seemed like she should have been talking to students who were WELL into their bio career already. Her teaching was just not for me. Get ready to sit there and be lost.

If you love bio, you'll love this class. Most lectures are interesting but occasionally go on a tangent. Really enjoyable, but keep going to lecture or you will fall behind quickly because there are 3 lectures a week. She encourages us to read from the textbook at night after lectures, I wish I did that...
the most boring class i've taken here at cal.  she has a really boring voice too.  MC tests.

analysis.name: Dmitry Livdan
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
