review_highlights.comment: Unless you want to learn a pile of theoretical crap then avoid Livdan. Hes a nice guy, but his lectures are mostly derivations, his exams are nothing like the homework, and the final topics are out of his MBA class material, not the text book. If you are an engineer or math major take with Livdan, otherwise avoid.

I agree with the rater below that Livdan DOES care about his students. If you approach him for help, he tries his best to be helpful and the graders seemed lenient. But the material was far too theoretical and difficult to grasp.. this class was truly frustrating. You put effort in and don't see results. Livdan is a nice, funny, sweet man though.

HARDEST CLASS OF ALL TIME. I have a 3.9 Haas GPA and I'm sitting here wondering if I'm going to fail the final today. Honestly, avoid this guy at all costs. The tests and practice material are ridiculously hard and like nothing in the book, final is going to be you looking at 500 formulas on your cheat sheet and praying something clicks.

This class was frustrating because I was really looking forward to learning finance. However, I ended up just learning everything from the book, which I could have done on my own. Even though he's very knowledgable, he just speeds through stuff as if we know the material like he does, and it just starts becoming a waste of time.

Hardest class I have ever taken at Berkeley. He is a nice man, but he cannot teach to save his life. He gives us material at the MBA level and his tests are 3 long questions which are far more difficult than anything done in class or for homework. Abort mission! Intro to Finance should not be this difficult.

analysis.name: Ross Doll
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Just a wonderful professor. Has an incredible breadth of knowledge about critical development around the world. In GPP 150, a discussion-based class, he's always willing to engage with students' ideas, often leading the class to valuable tangential concepts. Students always feel comfortable sharing questions & thoughts & how they're doing.

Professor Doll is a profoundly inspiring and compassionate lecturer whose course radiates humanity and hope. His approach to sensitive topics and his willingness to show his own humanness made the experience transformative. This class reshaped my perspective and should be a required course. I'm deeply grateful for his guidance and lasting impact.

I have never learned/cared about anything as much as I do GPP 115. Lectures are great.  The most important class anyone could take, it gives a lot of perspective. If you lack empathy/care for others, you won't enjoy, but you're prob shallow/boring and should get over yourself. I love this class and prof doll, and I'm sad it's over. 100% recommend

Prof. Doll is a very good lecturer and is clearly very knowledgeable on the topics covered in class. His lectures are interesting, and he explains things in a way that gives his opinion while still being able to let you develop your own. His slides don't contain much information, so attendance is important because 90% of the info comes from him.

Genuinely one of the most knowledgeable and caring profs I've had in some time. It is an accelerated course if you take it during the summer, so a lot of work is to be expected. Readings are interesting and complement the lecture well. This class is so good for your academic career, but also just to grow as a person. 11/10 would recommend!!!

analysis.name: Douglas Koshland
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: While I enjoyed the topics in his section, his lectures were difficult to follow given his teaching style. It felt like he was trying to converse with other experts rather than trying to teach undergrads. There was also a lot of assigned reading which while not required would help. His portion of the exam was also the most difficult.

His lectures did not seem to pertain to the material, but the problem sets were reliable. He gave a lot of background and not enough actual practice in his lectures; I would have preferred more examples. Definitely take Bio1A before this course. His section of the exams was probably the most difficult.

Prof. Koshland loves genetics and loves to teach! Although the course content was difficult conceptually, Prof. explained well and never hesitated to offer additional clarification during office hours. Free online textbook, practice tests, and doable group worksheet assignments were helpful. Exams really make you think, but graded on curve!

One of the best lecturers for MCB 140. The discussion sections are mandatory but personally they are very helpful. The exams are a bit unexpectedly hard but the curve is generous enough that 70% of the students are in the B and A range. (He also remembered everyone's names by the end of the second week.
Seemed to really enjoy teaching the class. Solid lecturer and accessible in office hours!

analysis.name: Donnett Flash
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 42 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Stop. Why are you even searching her up on here? Go to calcentral. Go to your schedule planner and change to a different professor please. I have just saved you some HUGE headaches. She is always yapping and blabbering about some random stuff that has nothing to do with your assigned essay. She isn't teaching English, she is teaching Yapanese.

Her expectations are all over the place and poorly clarifies feedback. She often doesn't fairly judge ideas that are contrary to her political beliefs and her lectures are lacking ins substance. Despite this being the first college English class for many, it is unnecessarily harsh and failed to meaningfully impact my writing.

Some material was interesting, but the course felt disorganized, and grading was very strict with unclear expectations. Feedback was discouraging and unconstructive, and I felt hopeless as my differing opinions were penalized even though she asked for them. This teaching style wasn't a good fit for my learning style and was frustrating.

This course raises serious concerns about evaluation standards and would benefit from departmental review. Severe disconnect between course delivery and departmental standards. Grading inconsistent/not clearly aligned with stated learning objectives. Requests for clarification often met with dismissiveness, discouraging student inquiry.

Lenient and supportive class. Four essays but your lowest gets dropped, and the last one is optional. Lots of detailed feedback and chances to heavily revise essays. Not heavy text analysis, more about reflection and building solid/supported arguments. Only one full book and a few chapters of another. Also participation is key.

analysis.name: William Drummond
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Drummond was a mixed bag when I took this class. I enjoyed his no-nonsense teaching style, and witty humor. However, class felt disorganized. Often, he would go on side tangents, and article feedback was limited to just occasional, brief critiques in lecture. Class sometimes ended super early. I felt like I learned more from the GSI, Emily.

Taking this graduate course and visiting San Quentin every Sunday was truly a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity—one that has reshaped my passions and career goals. Not only is Drummond an incredible advocate for criminal justice reform, but he is also an amazing mentor. If you get any opportunity to work with him, don't waste it. He has made history.

I took a seminar with Prof. Drummond about memes in the media studies department. I enjoyed his "hip" knowledge of pop culture and healthy skepticism of the media, despite being a journalist. I would take a proper class with him, given the chance. He is very invested in the bay area community, which is cool.

analysis.name: Andrew Bray
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Go back to stat 20 please. First half of the semester was great, grading fast, lectures were helpful, and then idk what happened but everything fell apart. Quizzes (50% of your grade) weren't graded till after the final, leaving you confused on where you stand in the class. Just not how an upper div programming class should have been run.

Bray is a great teacher and I loved his class, but the class assignments are structured to stress you out. Quizzes are 50% of your grade and are extremely hard. Plus, you have projects every other week, problem sets every week. You will suffer a lot but ps and projects are p/np so that's a plus. I can't keep up with class anymore after mid-term.

STAT133 used to be about projects and learning R. Prof. Bray offers a course all about looking nice, but filled with memorization. There are 7 "quizzes" worth 50% of your grade that are an hour long each. This is the worst path a prof can take to battle gen. AI. One look at other programming classes and the prof. would've made a better curriculum.

nice & chill guy but lowk class is a mess itself. quizzes are 50% of the grade and occur every two weeks, there's a group quiz and individual quiz and get averaged together for your official grade, meanwhile the final is 30% so beware of that. quizzes r pretty hard w/ the material given bcs it can be pretty different from hws.

Love him! His teaching style is organized and easy to follow/note down. The content isn't difficult and his class is interesting. It was easier spring of 25, lost the gsi and never had lab(we didn't code much). You do a semester long group project where you have full creativity. He's great to talk to and his exams are based on lecture (don't skip!)

analysis.name: Andrew Barshay
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Caring and extremely knowledgeable professor who is very passionate. The class is dense, as the prof. crams in a lot of info and themes about Japan both socially and structurally. Although lectures and readings were mostly dull, the class material was very interesting at times, and exams were very chill if you prepared. Learned a lot about Japan.

Professor Barshay is clearly very knowledgeable and passionate about Japanese history, but lectures often feel disorganized, tangential, and mentally draining. There are also lots of readings, most of which are quite dense. Grading largely depends on GSI, but for an intro class, it felt like there was an overbearing amount of information to learn.

Great professor. Super interesting lectures and is pretty funny. Engaging and is  good at making overarching connections. That being said, so much reading.  not sure if the grades are more contingent on him or the GSIs, but definitely not the easiest grading-- lots of papers that are harshly scored. Wish there were more chances to improve

super long lectures, always ran the clock even though he was out of things to say. so much reading and writing. hard rubrics, gsi grades incredibly harshly (not sure if its coordinated or not). exam prompts are given in advance but incredibly dense, honestly wish i p/np or dropped it, just not worth the time commitment.

He's clearly passionate about Japan, but I could never pay attention during lecture. Thankfully, he records all of them so they are available to view later. There's a lot of required readings, but I think doing half of them is more than enough to get an A. Overall, a pretty decent class!

analysis.name: Andrew Little

Posts lecture slides online with caveat "Use at your own risk." Very disorganized and seems confused about his own material. Practice midterm totally different from harder actual midterm. His lecture ability is nonexistent; he speaks far too quickly, slurs his words, and speeds through the complex material (like R, which was not taught in previous semesters of PS3). Class was an absolute disaster as mentioned by the other comment. Disorganized and lacked structure in the contents of the course. Little has little clue what he is trying to teach in any given lecture. What a waste of a semester.

This professor is by far the most challenging person that I have come across during my time at Berkeley. The problem sets and tests are not what ruin you, but rather his ability to speed through important concepts while dragging on explanations of useless ones . If he teaches PS3 again and you have to take it, PRAY for an amazing GSI.

analysis.name: Andrew Leong

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Leong is one of the most caring, thoughtful, and understanding professors I've ever had. Very encouraging, insightful, and skilled at overseeing and adding to student discussion without intervening. A self-graded class where you genuinely wanted to try and that I took a lot away from. Thank you Prof. Leong!

I loved taking Prof. Leong's class, as he had some exciting and insightful things to say about the readings. This class made me really love the short story form and refined my close reading skills. The class discussions were also really engaging and enjoyable, and his facilitation of it made it even more enjoyable.
Great lectures and really easy and accessible material! Definitely the coursework is manageable and intriguing. Definitely should take it.

He was so easy. Everyone either got A or A+. He spent a lot of time making a grade calculator for us to figure out our grade. Had so much buffer credit opportunities that you could literally ditch the final if you had enough points in the class. Didn't read a single book. I want him to teach more classes so I can collect those A's.

Demanding workload: no in class pop quizzes and no midterm. Final was in class, and definitely grueling. However, Professor Leong even made Robert Penn Warren enjoyable to read insert: applause. He layers his lectures with tons of info, and is super accessible if youre ever confused about material in class. A wonderful professor!

analysis.name: Andrew Garrett
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 37 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He teaches really well. He's probably one of the best lecturers in the Ling Dept! The homework he assigns are a bit tedious, but nevertheless it's doable. And I believe he was very generous when it comes to the grade cut-offs. He knows that the class is challenging. And did I mention he's so adorable. I want a mini-Garrett plush doll! :)

Most effective lecturer I've had yet at Berkeley. He's so funny, so topical - I'm someone who can often get bored or sleepy in lecture environments, but I was rapt every single day. He has so much love for Linguistics and for us and it really shines. He's got a dry sense of humor, so if you're down for it then you'll really find him a riot.

Great professor! I definitely recommend him! Lectures are very important, make sure to attend them all. Not an easy class, but if you work hard, you'll get a good grade. Homework assignments are difficult (get ready to spend 4-8 hours per homework; 1 homework per week), but they prepare you for midterms and a final.

I rarely went to lecture but as long as you understand the concepts you should be fine. He always gives opportunities to make up for missed grades and he's very understanding! As long as you're doing the homework, you should be fine and you might not even have to take the exam if you get full marks on the homework.

"Garrett the merciful" is how I would describe this professor. I have made so many mistakes and missed a lot of classes but Garrett was willing to work with me and give me more chances than I deserve. I think  this is an example how how a professor should be. Thank you Professor Garrett!

analysis.name: Andrew Kim
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He pushes students more than other professors—something that is annoying for the uninspired but terrific for the curious. There are weekly assignments and readings, and lectures are packed with interesting material. If you are interested in the topic, this is an amazing comprehensive overview presented and executed pretty well.

He's so interesting and kind, really engaging lectures and fascinating course material. I would sit in the front and ask questions, during and after lecture if you can, and take good notes. Write down everything he says and study them, with the charts, and read the textbook, then you'll be fine. Totally would take again.

weird dude. if you're not an anthro major, his lectures will be a bit of a snooze. midterm average was low but most people made it up by scoring better on the final. Questions were definitely nitpicky and the study guide he provides is kinda wack - better off ignoring it and creating your own. Amazing GSIs though!!!

Prof Kim is one of my fave Anthro Professors at Berkeley! Smart guy. Really funny/genuine instructor who wants the best for his students. Very accessible outside of lecture. I enjoyed seminar (~ 8 people, in-depth readings/discussions), but I will always rec his psychoneuroendocrinology (PNE) class. Accessible to STEM + non-STEM folk alike. 10/10.

Prof Kim was really cool! He explained things pretty clearly, and had some funny anecdotes to go along with his teaching. The exams are very fair, and a lot of your grade is just section attendance/completion points for homework. The GSIs are really helpful, and I learned a lot from them as well. Overall, a solid class :)

analysis.name: Courtney Dressing
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Amazing lecturer, did a great job at keeping students engaged and covering material, + examples explaining mathematical processes well. However, there was a disconnect between lectures and HW. HW rubrics were too rigid, points could be removed easily. May take a while to get a sense of the rubric before your scores get to where you want them to be.

Good professor, lectures were interesting and insightful. However, be prepared for very harsh grading on homework sets and difficult tests. Reading the textbook is technically optional, but is softly enforced by random hidden references to it in the homework sets. Overall I enjoyed the class, just be prepared to spend a lot of time on it.

Very kind and engaging professor; willing to answer many questions and super knowledgeable. The lectures were awesome but were often not sufficient preparation for the very difficult and harshly graded HW sets. Textbook readings were not mandatory, but I wish that I had read them since they often covered HW material not covered in lecture.

A very kind, caring professor. She clearly cares about her students and is always available for questions after lecture. She was there for all but two and the pace was reasonable. 

The textbook is essentially useless although some problems are from there. The only hiccup was a strangely long and difficult 2nd midterm, but at least she curved it.

Professor Dressing is a great lecturer, and the slides are posted beforehand for those that want to take notes on them. She had very fair homework and exam policies, and was very forgiving when one midterm was significantly longer than she had expected. Great class if you want to learn more about the universe and have some physics foundations.

analysis.name: Michelle Douskey
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 268 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Lectures weren't that good, the lab manual is all you really need to understand what's going to happen during lab. The lab reports were fine but there was no rubric which sucked, they're also just sometimes lengthy and time-consuming. The final exam was pretty much the same as the practice exams provided. Overall, not the hardest class just tedious

My favorite prof in the whole wide world. She might have cried at the Florence and the Machine concert, but I feel like crying after every lecture because they are so beautiful. Prof. Douskey, if you're reading this, pls be my best frand. WE LOVE YOU. 3 3 3 Enjoy your gourmet tea and dorm room moonshine.

The lectures are a waste of time, but the lab reports are graded pretty fairly and its a pretty easy A if you do the work and go to office hours. I have to say the GSI makes or breaks the class. My GSI was Josh Dillen and he was quite rude and condescending, but other GSIs were super nice (Keith was incredible)

Lectures were entertaining but did not help with lab reports. SO much work for a 2 unit class and questions were often vague + grading varied between GSIs. Go through the online lab before attending in person to make lab go smoothly.

lectures were such a drag and not very pertinent either to the lab, postlab report. final is a breeze if you do all the practice matierial because the content does not vary much between years. GSI makes or breaks this class, but most of the GSIs are great

analysis.name: Kamal Dulai
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Lecture is boring even though he tries to make jokes that comes off as insensitive to many students.Exams are cumulative so that makes it hard to know what to study for. Do not take everything he said literal. He said there was no questions on the stuff we didnt learn about but it was there on the final exam. But my GSI pulled thru.

Dr. Dulai is approachable and encourages questions, but is extremely unorganized. Exams were all cumulative with the final in particular being unfair.The material tested was content he said wouldn't be included.He crammed 130+ slides in the last lecture, made distasteful "jokes" and told students to use AI when asked a question. Wouldn't recommend.

analysis.name: Ian Duncan
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 44 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Duncan is incredibly knowledgeable about his subject matter, and fully willing to go above and beyond to assist students in their studies; whether related to his field or not. I am very proud of the essays I completed in his class, and felt that, though difficult, that I earned my grade in his class. He also has a fun, dry sense of humor.

He made 45B my favorite class this semester despite the fact that it was my least favorite literary time period. He made almost every reading interesting and really tied overall themes together well. He's totally funny and his accent is adorable. Lecture attendance is mandatory, participation is 25%, midterm and final are only worth 30% together.

I had the pleasure of taking Duncan twice: for my thesis course (Comedy) and for Scottish Literature. The man is brilliant but extremely humble. If you treat him with respect, and illustrate interest in his class, he will go out of his way to help you. I have graduated and he still helps me! I have a passion for Romantic Brit Lit thanks to him!

As described below, Duncan is still very accessible. He is very down to earth. He is one of the most acommodating Professors I have had. I got a B+, and I went to 5 of his office hours this semester. With a few more visits and great essay writing an A is possible, but not easy.

Duncan is the nicest teacher I have ever had at Cal, he is always willing to help and challenge you. He ordered everyone coffee and cookies at the final, too. He gives amazing historical and cultural context for everything and is a very fair grader, interested in seeing you improve and succeed. I loved this class, great coverage of the material!

analysis.name: Mi-Suk Kang Dufour
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I received better answers to my questions from GSIs. Sometimes she starts a thought a doesn't finish it bc there's sm material to go through. Exams are okay. Group work for the data skills project is incredibly annoying

Professor records all her lectures and pre-records them 75% of the time. It seems nice but she does not offer a lot of opportunity to reach her. So it feels like taking a YouTube course while you are paying thousands of dollars expecting an active lecturing and learning from a professor. If you want to learn, don't take  this class.

Dufour is clear and concise in lectures and her slides are clear and informative to the point that lecture attendance is not necessary for students with any slight inclination towards coding/statistics. While this class might feel different to mcb/pbhlth students due to its different content, it is graded fairly and the prof/GSIs are accessible.

Not a great professor. She pre-recorded all her lectures from years ago and basically posts the same material from 3-4 years ago. Not a good professor. She is not available to meet. The GSIs are also disorganized and always gave different answers on the data project. This is not a good course and waste of money...

The exams were incredibly long and unbearable. It's split into two parts, one timed and one take-home. The last exam was about 24 pages long. Even though you're given a whole day to do it, it was still frustrating to do. I wish the lectures showed more examples of what was on the exam.

analysis.name: Gaspard Duchene
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: very passionate. learned a lot!

Dr. Duchene is an amazing instructor! One of the best ones I've had at Berkeley. He's a really fair grader, even towards the lenient side (given that you do the work). Lectures are insanely clear. Super approachable and friendly. The class is definitely not an "easy A," but attending lectures and doing all of the required work is all that's needed.

Gaspard is a very friendly professor and his class was well-organized. He always encourages participation with open discussions and questions in class and really wants his students to succeed. He is extremely knowledgeable and enthusiastic about astronomy, and I really enjoyed learning so much in this course!

Incredible professor. Kind, extraordinarily approachable, and knows how to get the most out of you. Gets you to think about asking the right questions, not chasing the "right" answer. Could not ask for better.

analysis.name: Duncan Macrae
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Very knowledgeable, but lecture can be dull sometimes. He does bring in good multimedia throughout. Accessible during OH. HEAVY on memorization of a ton of Greek figures. The two main textbooks are a waste of money, but the section readings are absolutely mandatory and come up a lot on the two midterms/final. Final mythtelling project 35% of grade.

Professor Macrae is just a great professor and super kind and helpful. There are weekly quizzes instead of midterms and it is content heavy but just go to lectures and listen and take notes. Review your notes the night before the quiz and you'll get an easy A. This class was low effort for me and that's what I did. The most you will do is reading.

Macrae was a great professor. The course itself got a little boring at times but mostly an interesting class and easy to digest material. There's weekly quizzes in lecture but other than that, lecture isn't mandatory. Everything is basically graded by GSIs and you will have to read weekly texts which appear on quizzes. No midterm btw. Great class!

Professor MacRae was clearly very passionate about Ancient Roman studies and he's very caring and reasonable with his quizzes (and there's no midterm). Sections were just (pretty boring) reading  but GSIs go over them decently well and they were pretty thematic heavy. Lectures were broad but interesting, and there's an emphasis on themes.

Prof. MacRae is a great teacher; he explains concepts well in lecture & assigns interesting readings. He truly cares about his students & is passionate about the course material. The exams are based off of passages from readings & handouts, as well as handout keywords. The myth telling project is fun & straightforward as long as you think ahead.

analysis.name: John Dueber
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: 2 of the reviews are 1/5 because the professor gave everyone full points on a question from the midterm (my class). It's not curved so this only helps people. He's been very upbeat and caring in every class and has made an effort to learn everyone's names. I've honestly loved his lectures and homework is very light while still being very helpful.

Dr. Dueber does not deserve the disrespect he receives from his students - most being a result of clear misunderstandings. Many confuse his upfront manner with being "unprofessional," and it is easy to tell whose egos are threatened. I appreciate his drive to ensure that his students are learning and his great effort to connect with his students.

Pretty fair professor, very clear grade bins and questions are pretty fair on exams. Responsive on ed and very willing to answer questions in class! Only thing is that hw content for the bio portion of this class is a little diff than what's taught in class, but it's graded on completion anyways.

he's pretty nice! he is really active on edstem so you can always have your question answered outside of class, and it is probably one of the most helpful edstems ive ever been in. and the exams are quite fair so far.

I loved this class - set me up well for more advanced biochemistry courses and research. John is a caring professor who places real intention and effort to help us succeed. I highly recommend going to office hours and interacting on edstem. I missed a large portion of lectures due to family issues and was able to catch up thanks to their help.

analysis.name: Arianne Eason
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Probably the easiest class ever. Attending section was helpful to stay up to speed with the course. Weekly assignments were simple. A group project takes place but all was doable.

Ari is super passionate about what she teaches and has a ton of really cool research in dev psych and adult prejudice studies that her lab runs. Very easy class with not many assignments, but really enlightening lectures and opportunities to engage with peers and the material.
Pretty easy class + amazing lectures. No exams but weekly assignments/posts and one final group paper. Lectures were recorded and Dr. Eason is a really good teacher.

Many mistakes and ambiguous instructions in assignments, and she expects there to be one specific answer. Usually with strict grading, there will be straightforward answers and a clear criteria in which your response is graded. With this class, the free responses seem to disregard your own opinion and insight even though the prompt is unclear.

Lectures are great but excessive fillers words were distracting in my opinion. Young and passionate about the subject. Raises interesting questions and touches on engaging topics. Lecture attendance not mandatory- recorded. Pretty easy class (no midterms), weekly assignments and big final group project.
